title.zh: 悬疑小说怎么写：用线索账本检查公平揭示
title.en: How to Write a Fair-Play Mystery with a Clue Ledger

seo_title.zh: 悬疑小说怎么写：线索布置｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Plant Clues in a Mystery Novel | ZenStory

description.zh: 悬疑小说要让读者看见可推理的事实。用三方线索账本管理发现、解释和真相，附原创案件示例。
description.en: A mystery must show readers facts they can reason from. Use a three-part clue ledger for discovery, interpretation, and truth. Includes an original case.

answer.zh: 写悬疑小说，先列真相与作案条件，再为每条关键线索建立账本：读者何时看见，调查者怎样解释，真实含义何时改变。误导要建立在同一事实的合理误读上，揭底只收回前文出现过的证据。
answer.en: To write a mystery, define the truth and the conditions of the incident first. Then create a ledger for every crucial clue: when readers see it, how the investigator interprets it, and when its real meaning changes. Misdirection should arise from a reasonable misreading of the same fact. The solution should collect only evidence that appeared earlier.

heading.zh: 推理小说线索怎么布置？
heading.en: How Do You Plant Clues in a Mystery Novel?

body.zh:
给每条关键线索固定一个名字，避免正文里反复换说法。账本记录读者已见、调查者解释和真实含义。下面是“闭展后少了一幅画”的原创谜题：

| 线索 | 三方记录 |
|---|---|
| 两层箱签 | 读者：离场照片中，“借用画架”纸签翘起，露出下层“归还画作”字角。调查者：箱子以前装过画。真相：本次装画后，上面又贴错了画架签。 |
| 缺角衬纸 | 读者：画位边有三角形衬纸，箱盖缝的衬纸也缺角。调查者：只是同种材料。真相：两块断边可拼合，画曾按这只箱子的尺寸包装。 |
| 空画架仍在 | 读者：原定送走的唯一借用画架仍靠着工作间墙。调查者：搬运未完成。真相：离场箱子装的不是那副画架。 |

正文推进时更新“谁知道什么”。在让读者与侦探共同推理的故事里，关键揭示前应给出构成判断的事实；侦探可以更懂程序，但不要在摊牌时掏出从未出现的决定性证据。气氛细节不必全部是线索，账本主要管理承担解答的事实。
body.en:
Give each crucial clue a stable name. Record what readers see, the investigator’s interpretation, and the true meaning. This ledger belongs to the original puzzle “A Painting Missing After the Exhibition Closed”:

| Clue | Three readings |
|---|---|
| Layered label | Reader: an exit photo shows “Borrowed Easel” peeling up over the corner of “Return Painting.” Investigator: the crate previously carried a painting. Truth: the easel label was mistakenly added after this painting was packed. |
| Torn paper | Reader: a triangular piece lies by the empty display; paper visible through the crate lid also lacks a corner. Investigator: common material. Truth: the torn edges fit, connecting this painting’s wrapping to the crate. |
| Easel present | Reader: the only borrowed easel due to leave remains in the workshop. Investigator: the move is unfinished. Truth: the departed crate did not contain that easel. |

Update who knows what as events proceed. In a story inviting readers to solve with the detective, show the facts needed for the key inference before the reveal. The detective may know more procedure, but should not produce unseen decisive evidence at the confrontation. Atmospheric details need not all be clues; the ledger manages facts that carry the solution.

heading.zh: 误导怎样写才公平？
heading.en: How Can Misdirection Remain Fair?

body.zh:
误导来自**事实正确，解释暂时错误**。箱子确实贴着画架标签，调查者先按标签判断内容；某人确实撒谎，他隐瞒的是私事，未必与失物有关；时间记录确实有差异，原因可能在设备而非证词。

安排误导时写两条路径：它为什么支持当前假说，哪项已出现事实能在后面推翻假说。角色怀疑转移后，旧线索要获得新含义，读者会产生“原来早就看见了”的回溯感。

Oh Story 的误导方法还要求吸引注意力的支线有自身作用。比如某人确实藏着一张邀请函：调查者以为他想接近失画，后面查明他瞒的是未经确认的私人展览计划。邀请函若只让他“看起来可疑”，揭开后便无用；可以让这段隐瞒解释他为何错过交接，改变合作关系，或令调查者重新查实际离场路线。新增这种支线时，要同时补它的前置事实与查明过程，不能把它当成本例已经发生的事。

列两句：这条误导为什么合理；排除以后留下什么。如果只是拖走注意力，先考虑删掉，而不是再加更多可疑人物。
body.en:
Fair misdirection means **the fact is correct, but the current interpretation is wrong**. The crate really does carry an easel label, so the investigator initially trusts it. Someone really does lie, but the concealed private matter may have nothing to do with the missing object. A timestamp really does differ, but the cause may lie in the device rather than the testimony.

For each misdirection, write two paths: why the fact supports the present hypothesis, and which already introduced fact can later overturn that hypothesis. When suspicion shifts, old clues gain new meanings, giving readers the retrospective feeling that the answer was visible all along.

Oh Story also asks a distracting side thread to have a function of its own. Someone might genuinely hide an invitation. The investigator suspects access to the missing painting; later checks show an unconfirmed private exhibition plan instead. If the invitation only makes that person look suspicious, it becomes dead material after disclosure. The concealment could explain a missed handoff, change a working relationship, or redirect inquiry toward the actual exit route. Adding such a thread requires its own setup and verification; it has not occurred in the existing worked example.

Write two sentences: why this inference is reasonable, and what remains after it is excluded. If it merely diverts attention, consider cutting it before adding more suspicious people.

heading.zh: 原创范例：闭展后少了一幅画
heading.en: Original Example: A Painting Missing After the Exhibition Closed

body.zh:
画展结束，管理员朱闻发现一幅小画不见了。当天只有一只长箱被运走，按离场照片上的标签，里面应是借来的折叠画架。搬运单也写明目的地是楼下美术教室。她先怀疑来过展厅的收藏者私自拿画。

读者在开场就看见三件事：箱签有两层，翘起的上层下面露出“归还画作”字角；失画位置旁有一片三角形衬纸，离场照片里箱盖边的衬纸也缺一角；工作间还靠着唯一借用的画架。朱闻起初认为箱签是旧的、衬纸只是常用材料，画架则会在下一趟搬走。

她逐项检验解释：既然这趟任务是还画架，为何画架仍在，而箱子已经离场？她按搬运单去美术教室，在接收人面前找到未拆封的长箱；把留下的衬纸与箱盖露出的断边对照，两者吻合。打开箱子，失画就在里面，原定归还画作的下层标签也是这次新贴的。

画找回后，志愿者解释打包经过：志愿者把“借用画架”标签贴到了已装画的箱子上，又照着这张标签填写搬运单。物件没有凭空消失，离场路线早在照片与单据里出现；标签让调查者忽略了实际尚未搬走的画架。志愿者的解释说明失误如何发生，画的位置已由朱闻根据先前线索主动找到，揭底不依赖临时自白。

这是一则寻找去向的谜题，不把错贴标签直接升级为蓄意盗画。若要改写为犯罪故事，还需要提前建立动机、行为机会及能区分失误与故意的事实。

### 把查证过程写成正文：先找到画，再解释错签

沿用朱闻、两层箱签、缺角衬纸、仍在工作间的唯一画架和楼下美术教室。下面补成一段限知正文候选；接收人允许现场查看并拆箱，志愿者随后到场解释，是本例采用的交流落法。箱子的内容靠实际查看确认，错贴过程靠亲历者说明，不凭纸签外观断定何时贴上。

> 朱闻站在空出的画位旁，把那片三角衬纸拾起来。离场照片里的长箱贴着“借用画架”，纸签一角翘着，下面露出“归还画作”的字角。
>
> 她想起收藏者在这幅画前停过，手指移到照片边，却又走去工作间。唯一借来的画架还靠在墙上。
>
> 如果照片里运走的是它，这里不该还有同一副。她把照片放大，箱盖缝露出的衬纸正缺一角。那片留下的纸不证明谁偷画，至少值得跟箱子对一下。
>
> 搬运单写的是楼下美术教室。朱闻拿着单下楼，接收人指向墙边：“这只，还没拆。你看吧。”
>
> 她先把衬纸靠近箱盖露出的断边，边缘吻合。接收人拆开箱子，朱闻看见那幅小画，才松开一直攥着纸片的手。
>
> “画在这里。”她说。寻找去向的判断得到了验证，收藏者的停留并没有变成拿画的证据。
>
> 志愿者过来查看，指着上层标签：“这张是我贴的。画先装进去了，下面‘归还画作’是这次贴的，我又把画架签盖上去了。搬运单也照它写。”
>
> 朱闻看向工作间的方向：“所以画架还没走。先把这只箱子的内容登记正确。”
>
> 接收人把记录里的画架划去，改记画作。小画仍在打开的箱子里，折叠画架仍在楼上；它们不再靠一张错签共用同一项内容。

找回、听到失误说明与更正接收记录分别发生。更正记录是此候选补出的收束动作，不等于画架已经归还、画已经重新挂好或所有人都已原谅。正文没有新添决定性线索，主角也没有先靠志愿者自白才知道去哪里找。若你选择暂不写记录更正，可停在画被找到，但后续仍保留正确去向。
body.en:
After an exhibition closes, administrator Zhu Wen discovers that a small painting is missing. Only one long crate left that day. According to its label in the exit photo, it should contain a borrowed folding easel. The transport form also gives its destination as the art classroom downstairs. She first suspects that a collector who visited the gallery took the painting without permission.

Readers see three things at the opening. The crate has two labels: beneath the lifting upper layer, the corner of the words “Return Painting” is visible. A triangular piece of backing paper lies beside the missing painting’s place, and the backing visible at the edge of the crate lid in the exit photo also lacks a corner. The only borrowed easel still leans against the workshop wall. Zhu Wen initially assumes that the lower label is old, the backing paper is common packing material, and the easel will leave on the next trip.

She tests those explanations one by one. If this trip was returning the easel, why is the easel still present while the crate has already left? Following the transport form to the art classroom, she finds the unopened long crate with the recipient present. She compares the backing paper left behind with the torn edge visible beneath the lid; they match. The missing painting is inside, and the lower label for returning the painting was newly attached for this trip.

After the painting is recovered, a volunteer explains the packing sequence. The volunteer put the “Borrowed Easel” label on the crate that already held the painting, then copied that label onto the transport form. Nothing vanished into thin air. The exit route was already visible in the photo and paperwork; the label made the investigator ignore the easel that had not moved. The explanation shows how the error occurred, but Zhu Wen found the painting by following earlier clues. The solution pays off only evidence already introduced; it does not rely on a last-minute confession.

This is a puzzle about finding an object’s destination, not a mislabeled crate inflated into deliberate art theft. Turning it into a crime story would require earlier setup for motive, opportunity, and facts that distinguish error from intent.

### Dramatize verification: find the painting before explaining the label

Keep Zhu, the layered labels, torn backing, sole easel still upstairs and art classroom downstairs. This limited-viewpoint candidate chooses an exchange in which the recipient permits inspection and opens the crate, then the volunteer arrives to explain. Inspection confirms contents; a participant explains packing. Label appearance alone does not date its attachment.

> Zhu picked up the triangular backing beside the empty place. In the exit photo the long crate read “Borrowed Easel.” A lifting corner exposed part of “Return Painting” below.
>
> She remembered the collector stopping before the painting. Her finger moved toward the photo’s edge, but she went to the workshop instead. The only borrowed easel still leaned against the wall.
>
> If it had left in that crate, the same easel should not remain here. She enlarged the photo. The backing exposed beneath the lid lacked a corner. Her paper did not prove theft; it was at least worth comparing with the crate.
>
> The transport form named the downstairs art classroom. She took it there. The recipient pointed beside the wall. “That one. Not opened yet. Have a look.”
>
> She held the paper against the exposed torn edge. They matched. The recipient opened the crate. Only when Zhu saw the small painting did her grip on the paper loosen.
>
> “It’s here.” The destination hypothesis was verified. The collector’s earlier pause had not become evidence of taking it.
>
> The volunteer came to inspect and pointed at the upper label. “I put that on. The painting was already packed. The return-painting label was attached for this trip, then I covered it with the easel label. I copied that onto the transport form too.”
>
> Zhu glanced toward the upstairs workshop. “So the easel hasn’t left. Record this crate’s actual contents first.”
>
> The recipient crossed out easel and entered painting. The painting remained in the open crate; the folding easel remained upstairs. A wrong label no longer assigned both the same recorded contents.

Finding the painting, hearing the explanation and correcting the receipt are separate events. The record correction is this candidate’s additional ending, not proof of returned easel, rehung painting or universal forgiveness. No decisive clue appears late, and Zhu finds the destination before the confession. An author can end at recovery without the correction, while later writing must retain the true location.

heading.zh: 悬疑信息怎样分批揭示？
heading.en: How Should Mystery Information Be Released in Stages?

body.zh:
按本例的判断层次揭示：先发现标签与仍在场的画架矛盾，再查已经运走的箱子；断边吻合使方向更具体，打开箱子才验证画的去向。各条信息支持不同范围，不跳到“谁故意偷画”。

场景可在异常、查证、证词、旧线索改义与人物相处之间交替。长时间反复同一疑问而没有理解、行动或体验，容易停滞；一次等待、陪伴或讨论也可以有价值。按本书需要安排节奏，不给每章强加新证据。

一个问题解答后可以收束，也可以由已出现的新事实指向下一问题。章尾可留调查方向，也可落在找回画作的安心；不要求每次答案都变得更危险或牵出更亲近的人。复杂谜题仍须把已经承诺的关键查证完成。
body.en:
Reveal according to this example’s inference layers: the label conflicts with the easel still present; the transported crate needs checking; matching torn edges narrows the direction; opening verifies the painting’s destination. Each fact supports a different scope, without jumping to deliberate theft.

Scenes can alternate among anomalies, checking, testimony, reinterpretation, and company. Repeating one question for a long time without understanding, action, or experience can stall, but waiting, companionship, and discussion may also matter. Arrange the book’s rhythm without a new-evidence quota per chapter.

An answer can close its question or lead to another through facts already introduced. The chapter may end on the next inquiry or the relief of recovering the painting. Every answer needs no greater danger or implication of someone closer. A complex puzzle still must fulfill its promised decisive checks.

heading.zh: 悬疑小说常见不公平点
heading.en: Common Forms of Unfairness in Mystery Fiction

body.zh:
| 不公平点 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 凶手靠末尾新证据被抓 | 提前让关键事实进入场景 |
| 误导全靠角色说假话 | 用真实事实的多种解释制造岔路 |
| 线索名称反复变化 | 固定称呼，方便读者回看 |
| 侦探凭直觉跳到答案 | 写出验证步骤与被排除的解释 |
| 线索只负责神秘气氛 | 承担解答的关键线索要能支持判断；普通气氛细节可以保留 |
| 反转推翻全部前文规则 | 让新解释兼容旧事实 |
body.en:
| Unfair move | Fix |
|---|---|
| New evidence at the ending catches the culprit | Put the crucial fact into an earlier scene |
| Every misdirection depends on a character lying | Create branches through multiple readings of true facts |
| The same clue keeps changing names | Use one stable term so readers can look back |
| The detective leaps to the answer by instinct | Show the verification steps and the rejected explanations |
| Clues create only a mysterious mood | Make decisive clues support inference; ordinary atmospheric detail can remain |
| A twist overturns every earlier rule | Make the new explanation compatible with the old facts |

q.zh: 悬疑小说可以让叙述者隐瞒吗？
q.en: May a mystery narrator withhold information?

a.zh: 本文讨论读者能与调查者共同推理的写法：可以隐藏未被注意的意义，人物也可以撒谎，但要让读者有依据检验说法。不可靠叙述可以刻意歪曲，不过需要自己的视角设计与可回看的破绽；不能只在结尾宣布此前事实全是假来补漏洞。
a.en: This article concerns mysteries readers can solve alongside the investigator. Meaning can go unnoticed, and characters can lie, provided readers have grounds to test their claims. An unreliable narrator may deliberately distort events, but needs a designed viewpoint and revisitable cracks. Declaring all prior facts false at the ending does not repair a missing solution.

q.zh: 线索越多越烧脑吗？
q.en: Do more clues automatically make a mystery harder?

a.zh: 线索数量不会自动提高难度。少量线索拥有多层合理解释，并在不同阶段改义，通常比大量无关细节更便于公平推理。
a.en: No. A small set of clues with several reasonable interpretations, whose meanings change at different stages, usually supports fair reasoning better than a large amount of irrelevant detail.

text.zh: 用 $story-long-write 只设计或审阅悬疑细纲，附真相、叙述视角与现有事实。分开读者所见、调查者解释、真实含义和支持范围，检查查证与误导收回。保留原真相与作者文风，允许已解决问题收束，不给每章硬加线索、新秘密或危险，不续写正文。
text.en: Use $story-long-write only to design or review this mystery outline with truth, viewpoint, and existing facts. Separate reader observations, investigator interpretations, true meanings, and evidential scope; check verification and resolved misdirection. Preserve truth and voice, allow solved questions to close, and add no compulsory clues, secrets, or danger per chapter. Do not continue the prose.

作者文风与事实边界

title.zh: 网文流派有哪些：先看每种流派的核心循环
title.en: Web-Fiction Subgenres Explained Through Their Core Loops

seo_title.zh: 网文流派有哪些：核心循环一览｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Web-Fiction Subgenres and Core Loops | ZenStory

description.zh: 用核心循环理解凡人流、无限流、规则怪谈、都市高武、重生复仇等常见网文流派，并判断适合自己的写法。
description.en: Compare common web-fiction modes through core loops, from mortal-flow and infinite-flow to rules horror, urban martial arts, systems, and rebirth revenge.

answer.zh: 网文流派可以按反复提供的阅读体验来理解。凡人流循环利弊权衡与准备，无限流循环进入副本、解题与带回变化，规则怪谈循环观察、验证与付代价，都市高武循环训练、对抗与进入更高层地图。选流派时先看你愿意长期写哪种循环。
answer.en: Web-fiction subgenres can be understood through the reading experience they repeatedly deliver. Mortal-flow stories cycle through weighing risks, preparing, and making trade-offs. Infinite-flow stories cycle through entering scenarios, solving them, and carrying changes back. Rules horror cycles through observing, testing, and paying costs. Urban high-martial-arts stories cycle through training, confrontation, and entry into higher social and geographic tiers. Choose by asking which loop you want to write for the long term.

heading.zh: 常见网文流派与核心循环一览
heading.en: Common Web-Fiction Subgenres and Their Core Loops

body.zh:
下面是编辑依据 skill 归纳的常见写作方向，用于比较重复体验，不是平台官方分类或当前热度排名。“年代文”等题材标签与“系统流”等机制标签并不在同一层级，实际选型可交叉使用。

| 方向 | 循环与取舍 |
|---|---|
| 凡人流 | **核心循环：** 观察风险→准备→取舍→保住收益；**主要回报：** 谨慎与判断赢过强敌；**常见失效：** 嘴上谨慎，行动总靠冒险 |
| 无限流 | **核心循环：** 进入副本→摸规则→解题→带回变化；**主要回报：** 新世界、新难题与长期主线推进；**常见失效：** 副本互不影响，像短篇拼盘 |
| 规则怪谈 | **核心循环：** 观察→试探→记录→复用；**主要回报：** 限制被摸清，代价被躲过；**常见失效：** 规则临时改写 |
| 都市高武 | **核心循环：** 训练→对抗→获得资源→进入更高层地图；**主要回报：** 实力与社会位置同步上升；**常见失效：** 换地图后旧人物与目标清空 |
| 脑洞／系统文 | **核心循环：** 独特机制→制造问题→选择用法→承担代价；**主要回报：** 看同一机制玩出新组合；**常见失效：** 功能单一，重复同一种解法 |
| 重生复仇 | **核心循环：** 利用旧信息→改写选择→时间线偏离→重新博弈；**主要回报：** 命运被主动改写；**常见失效：** 主角全知，对手不学习 |
| 年代文 | **核心循环：** 现实缺口→经营资源与人情→获得生活改善；**主要回报：** 在限制中逐步改命；**常见失效：** 物件堆砌，现实账不动 |
| 追妻火葬场 | **核心循环：** 伤害→离场→追悔→证明与选择；**主要回报：** 关系权力翻转与迟到清算；**常见失效：** 只有虐和道歉，没有离场与证明 |

这张表按写作发动机归纳，实际作品可以组合流派。组合时确定一个主循环，其他元素负责提供场景、人物或变奏。
body.en:
This editorial comparison uses the skill’s methods to distinguish recurring reading experiences. It is not an official platform taxonomy or a current popularity ranking. Setting labels such as period fiction and mechanism labels such as system fiction describe different dimensions and can overlap.

| Type | Loop and tradeoffs |
|---|---|
| Cautious cultivation (凡人流) | **Core loop: ** Observe risks → prepare → make trade-offs → preserve gains; **Main reward: ** Caution and judgment defeat stronger enemies; **Common failure: ** The protagonist claims to be cautious but always acts through reckless gambles |
| Scenario-based survival (无限流) | **Core loop: ** Enter a scenario → discover its rules → solve it → bring back a change; **Main reward: ** New worlds, new problems, and progress in the long plot; **Common failure: ** Scenarios never affect one another and feel like an anthology |
| Rules horror | **Core loop: ** Observe → test → record → reuse; **Main reward: ** Restrictions become legible and costs can be avoided; **Common failure: ** Rules are rewritten whenever convenient |
| Urban high martial arts | **Core loop: ** Train → confront → obtain resources → enter a higher-tier map; **Main reward: ** Strength and social position rise together; **Common failure: ** A new map erases old characters and goals |
| High-concept or system fiction | **Core loop: ** Distinctive mechanism → problem → choice of use → cost; **Main reward: ** New combinations built from the same mechanism; **Common failure: ** One function leads to the same solution every time |
| Rebirth revenge | **Core loop: ** Use old information → rewrite a choice → diverge the timeline → compete anew; **Main reward: ** Fate is actively rewritten; **Common failure: ** The protagonist knows everything and opponents never learn |
| Period web fiction (年代文) | **Core loop: ** Practical shortage → manage resources and favors → improve daily life; **Main reward: ** Gradually change one’s fate within constraints; **Common failure: ** Objects accumulate while practical ledgers stand still |
| Groveling romance | **Core loop: ** Harm → departure → remorse → proof and choice; **Main reward: ** A reversal of relational power and a belated reckoning; **Common failure: ** Suffering and apology appear without departure or proof |

This table groups stories by their writing engines. A work may combine subgenres. Choose one primary loop; let other elements supply settings, characters, or variations.

heading.zh: 凡人流是什么？
heading.en: What Is Mortal-Flow Fiction?

body.zh:
凡人流通常让主角以普通或较弱的起点进入高风险世界，靠观察、准备、利弊权衡和及时退让生存。爽点来自判断与准备形成优势，实力成长服务生存选择。

写凡人流要让“谨慎”进入动作：提前准备退路，收益与风险一起计算，见到超出承受范围的敌人会撤退，配角也有自己的利益。主角每次全凭运气进入绝境，再靠隐藏底牌获胜，谨慎只剩标签。
body.en:
Cautious cultivation fiction (凡人流) usually gives the protagonist an ordinary or relatively weak starting point in a high-risk world. Survival depends on observation, preparation, weighing costs and benefits, and retreating in time. Satisfaction comes from judgment and preparation creating an advantage; growth in strength serves survival choices.

Caution must appear in action. The protagonist prepares an exit, calculates reward together with risk, retreats from an enemy beyond their capacity, and deals with supporting characters who have interests of their own. If every crisis begins through luck and ends through a hidden trump card, “cautious” is only a label.

heading.zh: 新手怎样选择适合自己的网文流派？
heading.en: How Can a New Writer Choose a Suitable Web-Fiction Subgenre?

body.zh:
先回答四个问题：

1. 你最想反复写的选择是什么：取舍、解谜、战斗、经营还是关系清算？
2. 你掌握的素材能否支撑多次变奏？
3. 主角每完成一次循环，会留下什么长期变化？
4. 读者下一次期待来自规模升级、规则变化、人物关系还是认知翻转？

能持续产生不同局面的循环更适合长篇。只喜欢一个开场设定，可以先写短篇验证，再决定怎样扩成长线。
body.en:
Answer four questions first:

1. Which choice do you most want to write repeatedly: trade-offs, puzzle solving, combat, management, or relational reckoning?
2. Can your material support many variations?
3. What lasting change remains after the protagonist completes each loop?
4. Does the next expectation come from greater scale, altered rules, changing relationships, or a reversal in understanding?

A loop that keeps producing different situations is better suited to a long novel. If you love only one opening premise, test it in a short story before deciding how to extend it into a long arc.

heading.zh: 同一个开头怎样写成不同流派？
heading.en: How Can One Opening Become Several Different Subgenres?

body.zh:
共同开头：药材仓学徒周岩发现一批货的标签与实物对不上。

- **凡人流**：他不急着举报，先确认谁能改账、货物流向和安全退路，用小批次试探对手反应。
- **规则怪谈**：仓库夜班守则要求标签错误的货必须原位封存，另一条却要求天亮前清空过期货，冲突迫使他验证规则。
- **脑洞系统文**：他能看见药材“下一次被使用的结果”，能力有次数与误判代价，选择把机会用在哪一箱成为核心。
- **年代文**：标签错误牵动采购指标、工位责任与熟人担保，他要在办事流程和人情账里自证。

故事表面仍是错货，读者持续等待的东西已经不同。流派由长期循环决定，场景装饰无法单独决定。
body.en:
Shared opening: Zhou Yan, an apprentice in a medicinal-herb warehouse, discovers that the labels on a shipment do not match the contents.

- **Cautious cultivation (凡人流)**: He does not report it immediately. First he learns who can alter the accounts, where the goods travel, and how he can leave safely, then tests the opponent’s response with a small batch.
- **Rules horror**: The night-shift rules require mislabeled goods to remain sealed in place, while another rule requires expired goods to be cleared before dawn. The contradiction forces him to test the rules.
- **High-concept system fiction**: He can see “the result of the next use” of each herb. The ability has limited uses and a cost for misreading, so choosing which crate deserves a use becomes central.
- **period web fiction**: The labeling error affects purchasing quotas, responsibility for workstations, and guarantees among acquaintances. He must prove himself through procedures and debts of favor.

The visible problem remains mislabeled goods, but what readers keep waiting for has changed. A subgenre is defined by its long-running loop; surface decoration cannot decide it alone.

heading.zh: 流派可以混搭吗？怎样避免主线散掉？
heading.en: Can Subgenres Be Combined Without Scattering the Main Plot?

body.zh:
可以混搭。先写一句主承诺，再标明每个元素的职责。例如“凡人流规则怪谈”可以让谨慎取舍做主循环，规则副本提供不断变化的风险；“年代重生文”让现实经营做主循环，前世信息只提供有限优势。

每个大段检查：主循环有没有推动，配角和资源是否从上一段继承，新元素有没有改变选择。若删掉某个标签后主线完全不受影响，这个标签只是宣传装饰；若多个循环争夺结算，读者会难以判断下一步期待。
body.en:
Yes. Write one primary promise, then state what each element contributes. A “cautious cultivation with rules horror” story may use cautious trade-offs as its primary loop while rule-bound scenarios supply changing risks. A rebirth story set in a period setting can make practical management its primary loop, while knowledge from a previous life offers only a limited advantage.

For each major section, check whether the primary loop advances, whether supporting characters and resources carry over, and whether the new element changes a choice. If removing a label leaves the main plot untouched, that label is promotional decoration. If several loops compete to provide the resolution, readers may not know what to anticipate next.

q.zh: 网文流派和题材有什么区别？
q.en: What is the difference between a web-fiction subgenre and subject matter?

a.zh: 题材说明故事世界与主要矛盾，如年代、宫斗、修仙；流派更强调反复运转的阅读机制，如凡人流、无限流、系统流。实际使用中两者经常组合。
a.en: A subject describes the story world and major conflict, such as a period setting, palace intrigue, or cultivation. A subgenre emphasizes a repeated reading mechanism, such as cautious cultivation (凡人流), scenario-based survival (无限流), or system fiction. Stories often combine the two.

q.zh: 一本书可以写几个流派？
q.en: How many subgenres can one novel use?

a.zh: 数量服从主线清晰度。确定一个主循环，其余流派元素只承担明确功能，并让上一阶段的人物、资源与后果继续存在。
a.en: The number should serve a clear main plot. Choose one primary loop, give every additional element a defined job, and carry forward the characters, resources, and consequences from earlier stages.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 比较我的点子适合凡人流、无限流、规则怪谈、系统流或重生文中的哪种核心循环，列出每轮选择、回报、长期变化和失效风险，不写完整正文”（Codex 里写作 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to compare whether my idea best fits the core loop of cautious cultivation (凡人流), scenario-based survival (无限流), rules horror, system fiction, or rebirth fiction. List the choice, reward, lasting change, and failure risk in each cycle. Do not write the full prose.” In Codex, write `$story-long-write`.

label.zh: 长篇题材目录
剧情循环设计

title.zh: AI视频动作崩坏怎么办：保住剧情信息，重写动作实现
title.en: When AI Video Actions Break: Preserve Story Facts, Rewrite the Action

seo_title.zh: AI视频动作崩坏怎么改｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Fix Broken AI Video Actions | ZenStory

description.zh: 动作反复出错时，先找出观众必须看懂的事实，再用替代动作、拆镜、停留或声音承担。附原创改写案例与不能省略关键过程的判断方法。
description.en: For failing actions, preserve the story fact; then substitute action, split the shot, hold a state, or use sound. Includes a rewrite and skip test.

answer.zh: 当准确写清动作仍难以得到可用结果，先别继续增加手指和位移细节。写下这一拍必须让观众知道的事实，再比较换动作、拆成前后镜头、保留结果状态或使用声音能否同样表达。改写后核对谁控制物品、谁知道信息、人物是否作出选择，不能为了画面顺畅把剧情改掉。
answer.en: When a precisely described action still fails to produce a usable result, stop adding finger and movement detail. Write down the fact viewers must learn from the beat, then compare whether a different action, before-and-after shots, a held result state, or sound can express the same fact. After rewriting, confirm who controls the object, who knows the information, and whether the character still makes the same choice. A smoother image must not change the story.

heading.zh: 先找出动作要求难在哪里
heading.en: First Identify What Makes the Action Difficult

body.zh:
Drama Skills 把下面几类写法作为生成项目中的重点检查对象。它们用于定位镜头要求，不等于某种模型能力的固定上限。

| 动作要求 | 方法与检查 |
|---|---|
| 两人同时争一件小物 | 提示词里容易含混的地方：接触位置、先后和最终归属必须同时成立 首先问什么：是否必须展示争夺过程，还是只需明确控制权？ |
| 多步双手配合 | 提示词里容易含混的地方：每一步都依赖前一步准确完成 首先问什么：哪一步承载剧情，其余能否拆开？ |
| “他终于明白了” | 提示词里容易含混的地方：只写内心结论，没有可见依据 首先问什么：观众通过哪项新行动知道他改变了判断？ |
| “没有接、没有按、没有看” | 提示词里容易含混的地方：没说人物此刻实际在做什么 首先问什么：哪个正在发生的动作能表达相同选择？ |

先查看真实输出，再标出具体问题：例如物品归属改变、动作跳过关键步骤或两人的手交叠不清。不要只记“效果不好”，也不要没有生成结果就声称某动作已经失败。
body.en:
Drama Skills treats the following patterns as priority checks in generative production. They help locate the demand a shot makes; they are not fixed limits of any model.

| Action requirement | Method and check |
|---|---|
| Two people contest one small object at once | What may be ambiguous in a prompt: Contact point, sequence, and final possession must all agree First question: Must viewers see the contest itself, or only understand who controls the object? |
| Several steps of two-handed coordination | What may be ambiguous in a prompt: Every step depends on the previous one being completed accurately First question: Which step carries the story, and can the rest be separated? |
| “He finally understands” | What may be ambiguous in a prompt: Only an internal conclusion is stated, with no visible basis First question: Which new action tells viewers that his judgment changed? |
| “She does not take it, press it, or look” | What may be ambiguous in a prompt: The prompt never says what the person is actually doing First question: Which action in progress can express the same choice? |

Inspect the real output first, then name the specific problem: possession changes, a crucial step is skipped, or two people’s hands overlap unclearly. Do not record only “the result is bad,” and do not claim an action failed without generated output.

heading.zh: 改动作前，先写一句不能改变的剧情事实
heading.en: Before Rewriting the Action, Fix One Story Fact That Cannot Change

body.zh:
用一句话固定这一拍的职责：

> 观众必须看懂：{谁}为了{目的}作出{选择}，使{物品归属／信息／关系／路线}变成{结果}。

例如：**许朔主动拒绝在调班申请上签字，申请仍留在他面前，对方知道这次请求没有被接受。**

在这个场景中，手指与笔尖的精确距离可以调整，主动拒绝和对方接收到拒绝必须保留。若改成“笔意外滚下桌”，画面虽然简单，却把拒绝改成事故。若改成申请突然消失，又丢掉了物品去向。这类改法不满足原来的戏。

先分清必要事实与可调整的实现，你才知道能省掉哪一步。
body.en:
State the beat’s job in one sentence:

> Viewers must understand: {who} makes {choice} for {purpose}, changing {object possession / information / relationship / route} into {result}.

For example: **Xu Shuo actively refuses to sign the shift-change request. The form remains in front of him, and the other person knows the request was denied.**

In this scene, the exact distance between fingertip and pen may change. His active refusal and the other person’s recognition of that refusal must remain. If the pen “accidentally rolls off the desk,” the image is simpler, but refusal has become an accident. If the form suddenly disappears, its destination is lost. Neither revision preserves the original scene.

Separate required facts from adjustable implementation before deciding which step can be removed.

heading.zh: 四种改写办法，逐个比较
heading.en: Compare Four Rewriting Methods One by One

body.zh:
| 方法 | 方法与检查 |
|---|---|
| 更换承担动作的对象 | 适用时机：物体或环境变化也能表达同一事实 检查边界：不能把人物主动选择变成偶然事故 |
| 拆成动作前与动作后 | 适用时机：过程本身不包含新选择，观众能理解连接 检查边界：偷换、作弊、关键手法等若依赖过程，就不能直接跳过 |
| 用停留或保持状态 | 适用时机：重要信息是坚持、拒绝、控制或等待 检查边界：先建立该状态如何出现，避免凭空改变持物 |
| 用声音配合反应 | 适用时机：声源已经明确，观众能把声音对应到事件 检查边界：声音不能代替必须看清的身份、字形或物品变化 |

按最小改动比较方案。某个方案改变剧情事实，就换下一个；都不成立时，保留关键动作，改用其他拍摄、动画或后期实现方式。需要改变故事结果时，先修改剧本与分镜，再写新提示词。
body.en:
| Method | Method and check |
|---|---|
| Change what carries the action | When it fits: An object or environmental change can express the same fact Boundary to check: Do not turn an active choice into an accident |
| Split into before and after | When it fits: The process contains no new choice and viewers can understand the connection Boundary to check: Do not skip a covert substitution, an act of cheating, or another crucial process when the process itself carries information |
| Use a hold or maintained state | When it fits: The important fact is persistence, refusal, control, or waiting Boundary to check: Establish how the state began so possession does not change from nowhere |
| Pair sound with a reaction | When it fits: The sound source is established and viewers can connect it to the event Boundary to check: Sound cannot replace an identity, written form, or object change that must be seen |

Compare options in order of smallest change. If one changes the story fact, try the next. If none works, keep the crucial action and use another filming, animation, or post-production method. If the story result must change, revise the script and storyboard before writing a new prompt.

heading.zh: 原创案例：拒绝签字，怎样避开精细手部编排？
heading.en: Original Rewrite: Refusing to Sign Without Fine Hand Choreography

body.zh:
**原设计**：许朔一边旋转笔帽，一边把申请滑到桌沿，在对方伸手接纸时用两根手指截住纸角，再反扣笔，靠一个细小摇头表示拒绝。假设输出反复出现纸笔混在一起、申请突然换手的问题，就值得重新安排实现。

这组动作包含很多操作，真正需要保留的是：**许朔选择不签，申请未交还，对方看懂拒绝。**

**改写方案**：

> 起点：许朔面前放着申请，右手握笔，对方坐在桌子另一侧。
>
> 许朔把笔横放到申请旁，手离开笔。他看向对方，说：“这次我不签。”随后双手收回身前，申请保持原位。
>
> 下一镜：对方看一眼无人拿起的笔，把准备继续解释的手放下。

这个版本给出可见动作与明确台词，保留人物的主动拒绝，也让接收者作出反应。它不再要求两个人在运动中的纸角上精确接触。

如果这一场原本要求无对白，可以在分镜层改为许朔将申请翻扣，再双手收回；此前需让观众看清这是一份等待签字的申请。翻扣表达拒绝是否足够清楚，要结合前后场面判断，不能只靠动作名称断言观众必然理解。
body.en:
**Original design**: Xu Shuo spins the pen cap while sliding the request toward the edge of the desk. As the other person reaches for the paper, he catches its corner with two fingers, flips the pen into a reverse grip, and signals refusal with a small shake of his head. Suppose repeated outputs merge paper and pen or make the request change hands. That is a reason to redesign the implementation.

The sequence contains many operations, but only three facts must remain: **Xu Shuo chooses not to sign, the request is not returned, and the other person understands the refusal.**

**Rewritten version**:

> Starting state: The request lies before Xu Shuo. He holds a pen in his right hand; the other person sits across the desk.
>
> Xu Shuo lays the pen horizontally beside the request and removes his hand from it. Looking at the other person, he says, “I’m not signing this one.” He then brings both hands back in front of himself. The request stays where it is.
>
> Next shot: The other person glances at the untouched pen and lowers the hand that was about to continue explaining.

This version uses a visible action and explicit line. It preserves an active refusal and gives the recipient a reaction without requiring two people to make precise contact with a moving paper corner.

If the scene must remain wordless, the storyboard can instead have Xu Shuo turn the request facedown and withdraw both hands. Earlier, viewers must have seen that this is a form awaiting signature. Whether turning it over communicates refusal clearly enough depends on the surrounding scenes; the action name alone cannot guarantee the audience’s interpretation.

heading.zh: 哪些过程不能为了省事直接跳过？
heading.en: Which Processes Cannot Be Skipped Merely for Convenience?

body.zh:
先问：观众是否需要通过这个过程判断人物做过什么。

- **关键偷换**：前一镜是原件、后一镜变成假件，若没人看到是谁换的，就可能改变悬疑的信息分配。
- **能力展示**：角色的专业本事正是本场回报，只展示“修好了”可能拿掉了观众想看的行动。
- **可争议的接触**：是否碰过某件物品决定后续指控，省掉接触过程会改变证据。
- **普通过渡**：从放下包到坐好，若中间没有新选择或信息，可以考虑更简洁的衔接。

不能省的动作可以重新拆镜、扩大关键物的可见范围，或选用能完成该过程的制作方式。减少动作难度服务于表达，不替代故事本身的要求。
body.en:
First ask whether viewers need the process to judge what a character did.

- **A crucial substitution**: If one shot shows the original and the next shows a fake, omitting who switched them may change how mystery information is distributed.
- **A display of skill**: If a character’s expertise is the scene’s payoff, showing only “it is fixed” may remove the action viewers came to see.
- **Disputed contact**: If touching an object determines a later accusation, skipping the contact changes the evidence.
- **An ordinary transition**: If nothing new is chosen or learned between putting down a bag and sitting, a simpler connection may work.

For an action that cannot be omitted, split the shot differently, make the crucial object more visible, or choose a production method that can carry the process. Reducing action difficulty serves communication; it does not replace the story’s requirements.

heading.zh: 改写后核对这几项
heading.en: Check These Points After the Rewrite

body.zh:
- 谁主动做出决定，是否仍与原剧本一致？
- 关键物品的归属、位置和数量是否解释得通？
- 观众与角色各自看到了什么，信息是否被提前或延后？
- 原来依赖过程的证据、能力或关系变化是否仍然成立？
- 拆出的镜头能否按同一持物与站位衔接？

如果动作方案不变，只是提示词缺少起点、接触对象或先后顺序，先参考[图生视频提示词](/drama-skills/image-to-video-prompts)把事实写清。本页处理的是另一层问题：写清后仍需要调整这一拍的动作实现，而非把所有镜头都简化成站立和说话。
body.en:
- Who actively decides, and is that still the person named by the script?
- Do the crucial object’s owner, location, and count make sense?
- What do viewers and characters each see, and has any information moved earlier or later?
- Does evidence, skill, or relationship change that depended on the process still work?
- Can the split shots connect with the same object possession and blocking?

If the action plan is sound and only the prompt lacks a starting state, contact object, or sequence, first use [image-to-video prompting](/drama-skills/image-to-video-prompts) to state the facts clearly. This page addresses a different layer: cases where a clearly written beat still needs a different implementation. It is not an instruction to simplify every shot into standing and talking.

q.zh: AI视频里不能写“没有按按钮”吗？
q.en: Can an AI-video prompt say that someone does not press a button?

a.zh: 可以把“不按”当作要表达的选择，但还需要明确可见状态，例如手停在按钮旁、随后收回，按钮保持未触发。写清人物实际做什么，比只留下否定结论更便于检查。
a.en: You may use “does not press” as the choice to convey. Also specify a visible state: the hand pauses beside the button and withdraws while the button remains inactive. Describing what the character actually does is easier to inspect than leaving only a negative conclusion.

q.zh: 拆镜是不是只要首尾两张图？
q.en: Does splitting a shot mean I need only the first and last image?

a.zh: 先判断中间过程是否承载关键选择或信息。只要过程重要，就需要安排观众能理解的动作覆盖；首尾状态相同，中间展示的证据与叙事信息仍可能不同。
a.en: First decide whether the middle process carries a crucial choice or piece of information. When it does, viewers need enough action to understand it. Identical start and end states can still contain different evidence and narrative information in between.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-video-prompts 根据这段镜头和我提供的实际失败观察，先列不能改变的剧情事实，再比较动作替换、拆镜、停留和声音方案；标明需要同步修改的分镜，不虚构生成结果。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-video-prompts`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-video-prompts` with this shot and the actual failure observations I provide. First list the story facts that cannot change, then compare action substitution, split shots, a held state, and sound. Mark any storyboard changes required, and do not invent generation results.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-video-prompts`.

title.zh: AI画面文字乱码怎么办：可读文字、空白区与后期字幕分开处理
title.en: Garbled AI Frame Text: Render, Reserve Space, or Add in Post

seo_title.zh: AI画面文字乱码怎么处理｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Handle Garbled Text in AI Frames | ZenStory

description.zh: 先判断文字是否承担剧情信息，再选择直接生成、图形表达、留白或后期添加。附提示词改写例子，以及参考图文字和视频字幕的排查顺序。
description.en: Classify text by story role, then generate it, render it as graphics, reserve blank space, or add it later. Includes prompt and reference/subtitle checks.

answer.zh: AI画面出现乱码时，先列出真正需要读清的字，区分剧情中的牌子、文件与画面外的字幕。重要文字可以明确写出准确内容并检查输出，或预留位置由后期添加；无关文字先从参考图和提示词里清理。不要一边要求读清店名，一边又全局禁止文字。
answer.en: When garbled text appears in an AI frame, first list the words that truly need to be readable and separate in-story signs and documents from subtitles outside the image. For important text, specify the exact wording and inspect the output, or reserve a place and add the text in post-production. Remove irrelevant text from references and prompts first. Do not ask for a readable shop name while also prohibiting all text globally.

heading.zh: 先确定这段文字负责什么
heading.en: First Decide What the Text Is Responsible For

body.zh:
| 文字的职责 | 方法与检查 |
|---|---|
| 店名、日期、消息等需要被读懂 | 可选处理：明确写出准确内容，或留给后期排字 要保住什么：文字内容、位置和剧情需要的读字时机 |
| 只需要表现有字的纸张或图案 | 可选处理：使用没有可辨字义的图形布局 要保住什么：纸张、版面与大致视觉密度 |
| 画面不需要任何字 | 可选处理：承载面留空，检查参考是否夹带文字 要保住什么：原有物体轮廓、材质和构图 |
| 内容还没定稿 | 可选处理：预留位置，待定稿后再添加 要保住什么：可供排字的干净表面与尺寸关系 |

把故事事实与制作方法分开写。例如剧情要求观众看到“周五闭店”，这条事实保持；本次图像可以选择留一块空白告示牌，后期再写入这四个字。空白只是制作中间态，最终镜头仍要让观众读到信息。
body.en:
| Function of the text | Method and check |
|---|---|
| A shop name, date, message, or other text viewers must understand | Possible treatment: State the exact text, or reserve it for post-production typography What must be preserved: Content, position, and the story moment when it must be readable |
| A page or pattern that only needs to look as though it contains writing | Possible treatment: Use a graphic layout with no legible semantic content What must be preserved: The paper, layout, and approximate visual density |
| A frame that needs no text | Possible treatment: Leave the supporting surface blank and inspect references for embedded text What must be preserved: The object’s existing silhouette, material, and composition |
| Content not yet finalized | Possible treatment: Reserve a place and add it after approval What must be preserved: A clean surface and suitable size relationship for typography |

Separate the story fact from the production method. If the story requires viewers to see “Closed Friday,” preserve that fact. This image pass may use a blank notice card and add the words later. Blankness is only an intermediate production state; the final shot must still communicate the information.

heading.zh: 一条有冲突的提示词，怎样改写？
heading.en: How Do You Rewrite a Prompt with Conflicting Text Requirements?

body.zh:
**原要求**：咖啡馆门口，门上清楚写着“周五闭店”，不要任何文字，不要字幕，高质量。

这里“必须读清告示”与“不要任何文字”互相冲突。可以按交付方法选择下面一版。

**方案一：本次直接尝试生成文字**

> 咖啡馆入口近景，玻璃门中部固定一张浅色长方形告示纸，纸上只写“周五闭店”。告示纸完整可见，镜头正对纸面，文字是本镜需要读清的信息。门框和把手位置保持，背景其他区域没有可辨招牌文字，画面外不添加字幕或标题。

**方案二：后期添加准确文字**

> 咖啡馆入口近景，玻璃门中部固定一张空白浅色长方形告示纸，纸面干净、完整可见，没有装饰覆盖或人物遮挡。保留门框、把手和玻璃反光，告示纸正面朝向镜头，供后期加入文字；图像中先不生成字形，画面外不添加字幕或标题。

方案二另记一行后期任务：**在告示纸上添加“周五闭店”，保持纸面透视，让角色看向告示时文字已经出现。** 不把这行后期任务混进生成画面时的“空白纸”要求里。

这两版是写法示例。方案一要核对实际输出是否逐字正确，方案二要核对最终合成是否真的补完文字；选了某条提示词就跳过检查，两条路径都会留下风险。
body.en:
**Original request**: At a café entrance, the door clearly says “Closed Friday.” No text of any kind, no subtitles, high quality.

“Viewers must read the notice” conflicts with “no text of any kind.” Choose one of the following versions according to the delivery method.

**Option 1: Try to generate the text in this pass**

> Close view of a café entrance. A pale rectangular notice is fixed at the center of the glass door. The notice contains only the words “Closed Friday.” The entire paper is visible, the camera faces it directly, and these words are the information that must be readable in this shot. Preserve the doorframe and handle positions. No other legible sign text appears in the background, and no subtitle or title is added outside the scene.

**Option 2: Add the exact text in post-production**

> Close view of a café entrance. A blank pale rectangular notice is fixed at the center of the glass door. Its clean surface is fully visible, with no decoration or person covering it. Preserve the doorframe, handle, and reflections in the glass. The notice faces the camera so text can be added in post-production. Do not generate letterforms in the image yet, and do not add subtitles or titles outside the scene.

Record a separate post-production task for option 2: **Add “Closed Friday” to the notice, match the paper’s perspective, and ensure the text is already present when the character looks at it.** Do not mix that post task into the request for blank paper during image generation.

These are writing examples. For option 1, inspect whether the actual output is correct word for word. For option 2, inspect whether the final composite truly adds the text. Choosing a prompt does not remove the need to check either path.

heading.zh: 姓名能读清，不等于签字已经可用
heading.en: A readable name is not an available signature

body.zh:
如果剧情要求识别某人的正式签字，先确认作者已提供哪种内容：只有签名归属、只有姓名文字，还是已有确认的签名字形。字体排出姓名，不能冒充尚未提供的正式手写字形。

例如，项目验收单需要在后续被人物认出签字，但作者只定了“由谁签”，没给字形。将这项记为待完成；若已有后期排字方案，保留签字区、透视与光照，待确认字形后合成。不要在空白区前安排人物已经辨认成功，也不让模型自行造笔画完成揭示。

本页的“准确生成”或“后期添加”都先依赖准确内容。后期任务写入清单是安排，只有最终镜头真的包含该字形且可读，才能完成这项观看职责。
body.en:
If the story requires recognition of a formal signature, distinguish attribution, a person’s written name, and an approved signature shape. Typing the name does not supply an unavailable handwritten signature.

Suppose a project acceptance sheet must later show a recognizable signature, but the author has specified only who signed. Mark the detail incomplete. With an agreed post-production plan, preserve the signing area, perspective, and light for the approved shape. Do not stage successful recognition of a blank area or let invented strokes fulfill the reveal.

Both direct generation and post-production need exact content first. Listing a compositing task is a plan; its viewing responsibility is delivered only when the final shot actually contains the required readable shape.

heading.zh: 为什么写了“不要文字”，参考图里的字还在？
heading.en: Why Does Text from a Reference Remain After the Prompt Says “No Text”?

body.zh:
提示词表达输出意图，输入参考却可能仍携带旧招牌、号码、界面或字幕。它们是画面里的可见内容，不能把一句否定词当成已完成的清理。

处理前先看参考图本身：

1. 找出可读字、近似字形、号码、标题条与屏幕界面。
2. 判断每处是否属于这次要保留的剧情内容。需要的文字核对版本；不需要的部分确定如何排除。
3. 对自己的或获准修改的素材，按位置选择裁切、局部清理、遮罩或换一张参考。
4. 检查处理是否伤到人物识别、道具结构或构图；有冲突就换素材或改后期安排。

例如，用一张咖啡馆旧图借鉴门框和灯光时，图里的旧营业时间不该自动进入新镜头。先处理旧告示，参考说明也限定为门框位置和灯光，不要求整图照搬。

只拿到图片文件名或别人的文字描述时，先索取可查看的素材，不能据此宣布画面已无文字。
body.en:
A prompt expresses the intended output, but a reference may still contain an old sign, number, interface, or subtitle. These are visible image content; a negative phrase does not count as completed cleanup.

Inspect the reference itself before production:

1. Locate readable words, letterlike shapes, numbers, title bars, and screen interfaces.
2. Decide whether each belongs to the story content being preserved. Verify the version of required text and choose how to exclude anything unnecessary.
3. For material you own or have permission to modify, choose cropping, local cleanup, masking, or a different reference according to position.
4. Check whether the treatment damages character identity, prop structure, or composition. If it does, change the material or the post-production plan.

If an old café image supplies the doorframe and lighting, its former business hours should not automatically enter the new shot. Clean the old notice first, and limit the reference instruction to doorframe position and lighting rather than copying the whole image.

If you have only a filename or someone else’s written description, request a viewable asset before claiming that the frame contains no text.

heading.zh: AI视频自动加字幕，先分清字在哪一层
heading.en: When AI Video Adds Subtitles, First Identify the Layer

body.zh:
“关字幕”可能指几种不同的东西，先看实际文件和制作步骤：

| 字在哪一层 | 方法与检查 |
|---|---|
| 剪辑工程的独立字幕或标题层 | 先检查：工程中是否有可单独选择的文字对象 对应处理：按交付需求关闭、删除或修改该层后重新导出 |
| 输入图片本身 | 先检查：首帧、角色板或场景参考是否已经带字 对应处理：处理参考，保留需要的身份和空间事实后再用于生成 |
| 生成视频画面内部 | 先检查：字是否已与像素融在一起 对应处理：评估局部修复、裁切或重新生成；裁切前确认不会丢掉人物与剧情信息 |
| 影片里的招牌、纸张或屏幕 | 先检查：是否是本镜必须读懂的剧情文字 对应处理：按准确生成或后期排字处理，不能当成多余字幕一概删除 |

独立字幕层与已经嵌进画面的字，需要不同操作。具体按钮取决于所用工具；先确定字的来源，再找对应编辑入口，避免为一层字幕重做整段人物表演。
body.en:
“Turn off subtitles” may refer to several different things. Inspect the actual file and production steps first:

| Where the text lives | Method and check |
|---|---|
| A separate subtitle or title layer in the editing project | First check: Whether the project contains a selectable text object Treatment: Disable, delete, or edit that layer according to delivery needs, then export again |
| The input image itself | First check: Whether the first frame, character board, or scene reference already includes text Treatment: Treat the reference while preserving required identity and spatial facts, then use it for generation |
| Inside the generated video pixels | First check: Whether the text is already fused into the image Treatment: Evaluate local repair, cropping, or regeneration; before cropping, make sure no character or story information is lost |
| A sign, paper, or screen inside the story | First check: Whether viewers must read it in this shot Treatment: Generate it accurately or add it in post; do not delete it indiscriminately as an unwanted subtitle |

A separate subtitle layer and words embedded in the image require different operations. Exact buttons depend on the tool. Identify the text’s source before finding the corresponding edit control so one subtitle layer does not force a complete redo of a character performance.

heading.zh: 文字交给后期，视频里还要检查什么？
heading.en: If Text Is Added in Post, What Still Needs Checking in the Video?

body.zh:
静态图上的字摆对了，进入视频后仍要跟着承载物走。后期检查围绕这段文字的职责展开：

- **位置**：字是否始终属于那张纸、那块牌或那个屏幕，物体移动时是否漂离表面。
- **可读性**：剧情要求读懂时，字有没有被手、人物、反光或过小画幅遮住。
- **先后**：角色因一句文字采取行动时，那句文字是否已经让观众看见。
- **版本**：同一告示前后内容一致；剧情要求换字时，变化发生在正确的镜头。

如果文本还没定稿，就把依赖它的镜头记为待完成。不要在空白告示前写“人物看懂闭店消息”，却把排字任务留空。
body.en:
Text placed correctly on a still image must continue to follow its supporting object in video. Check according to the text’s story function:

- **Position**: Does it remain attached to the paper, sign, or screen, or drift away when the object moves?
- **Readability**: When the story requires comprehension, is it blocked by a hand, character, reflection, or frame that is too small?
- **Order**: If a character acts because of a line of text, has the audience already seen that line?
- **Version**: Does the notice remain consistent across shots, and if the story changes the wording, does the change occur in the correct shot?

If the text is not final, mark every shot that depends on it as incomplete. Do not write “the character understands the closing notice” in front of a blank sign while leaving the typography task empty.

heading.zh: 交付前的文字检查清单
heading.en: Text Checklist Before Delivery

body.zh:
- 每一处必须读清的文字都有准确版本和承载位置。
- 直接生成与后期添加已选定，不同时要求清晰文字和全局无字。
- 输入参考中的旧字、号码和字幕已经核对。
- 后期任务完成后重新检查最终画面，而非只检查提示词。
- 无关文字没有挤占需要读懂的剧情信息。

如果问题已经定位到生成画面的一小块，先保留其他正确部分；[图生视频提示词](/drama-skills/image-to-video-prompts)继续负责镜头中的动作与变化，文字处理不应顺手改掉角色身份或剧情结果。
body.en:
- Every required readable text element has an accurate version and a supporting location.
- The team has chosen direct generation or post-production addition rather than requesting legible text and no text at the same time.
- Old text, numbers, and subtitles in input references have been reviewed.
- The final image is inspected again after post-production work, not merely the prompt.
- Irrelevant text does not compete with story information that must be read.

If the issue is confined to a small area of a generated frame, preserve the other correct parts first. [Image-to-video prompting](/drama-skills/image-to-video-prompts) remains responsible for action and change in the shot. Text treatment should not casually alter character identity or the story result.

q.zh: 所有文字都交给后期更好吗？
q.en: Is it always better to add all text in post-production?

a.zh: 看准确度要求、画面运动和后期成本。剧情关键字适合明确控制内容；背景无需读懂的纹理则不用逐字排版。先按职责分类，再决定制作路径。
a.en: It depends on accuracy requirements, image movement, and post-production cost. Story-critical wording benefits from explicit control; background texture that need not be read does not require letter-by-letter typography. Classify each element by function before choosing a production path.

q.zh: 只加“不要字幕”能解决所有乱码吗？
q.en: Can adding only “no subtitles” solve every garbled-text problem?

a.zh: 不能把它当作完整处理。先查输入是否带字、提示词是否要求文字、工程是否添加了字幕层，以及实际输出中问题出现在哪里，再选择对应修正。
a.en: No. Check whether the input contains text, whether the prompt requests it, whether the editing project adds a subtitle layer, and where the problem appears in the actual output. Then apply the correction for that source.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-image-prompts 检查这些画面的文字要求，区分必须读清、只要图形、留白和后期添加，写清准确内容与位置，找出参考图和负面要求的冲突。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-image-prompts`。提供可查看的参考，才能核对图中已有文字。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-image-prompts` to inspect the text requirements in these images. Separate text that must be readable, graphic-only writing, blank reserved space, and text to add in post. State exact content and position, and find conflicts between reference images and negative requirements.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-image-prompts`. Provide viewable references so existing text can be inspected.

准确文字、呈现方法与输入参考检查

title.zh: 漫剧画风怎么选：动态漫、二次元、水墨与Q版的制作取舍
title.en: Choose Motion-Comic Styles: Limited Animation, Anime, Ink Wash & Chibi

seo_title.zh: 漫剧画风怎么选｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Choose a Motion-Comic Art Style | ZenStory

description.zh: 从认人方式、动作安排、线条色块和关键信息出发选择漫剧视觉方向。附同一场景的四种表达方案与可执行画风词表。
description.en: Choose a motion-comic style by character, action, line/color, and key information. Compare limited animation, anime, ink wash, and chibi in one scene.

answer.zh: 选漫剧画风，先看故事靠什么让观众理解：人物表情、清楚的动作、关系距离，还是流程与符号。再比较角色怎样被认出、什么需要持续运动、哪些细节必须读清。用同一个场景试写几种视觉方案，保持剧情不变，比较各方案是否保住这些信息。
answer.en: Choose a motion-comic style by asking what lets viewers understand the story: facial expression, clear action, relational distance, or process and symbols. Then compare how characters remain recognizable, what must keep moving, and which details must stay legible. Write several visual treatments for the same scene, keep the story facts unchanged, and compare whether each treatment preserves that information.

heading.zh: 四种常见方向，先比较制作重点
heading.en: Compare the Production Priorities of Four Common Directions

body.zh:
下面按 Drama Skills 的制作形态卡整理。这些名称可以有交集：动态漫强调怎样动，二次元和水墨更多描述怎样画；比较时看具体实现，不把它们当作互斥的分类。

| 方向 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 二维限动／动态漫 | 先决定什么: 哪些画面保持，哪些局部活动; 重点保住什么: 轮廓、固定色块、正在行动的主体; 常见代价或风险: 全员与背景一起飘动，注意中心消失 |
| 精细二次元表达 | 先决定什么: 角色之间的结构差异与情绪表现; 重点保住什么: 脸型、发型、识别色在不同光色下仍可区分; 常见代价或风险: 只堆“精致唯美”，同剧人物越画越像 |
| 水墨笔触 | 先决定什么: 哪些边缘可散，哪些必须清楚; 重点保住什么: 关键轮廓、手中物、必要空间关系; 常见代价或风险: 留白或洇化把证据与动作对象一起抹掉 |
| Q版表达 | 先决定什么: 比例体系、主色块、需要放大的识别记号; 重点保住什么: 同一角色跨镜比例与物品相对大小; 常见代价或风险: 持续弹跳、满屏符号让因果难以读清 |

“选水墨”不能替代“这一镜需要看清谁把什么交给谁”。遇到精确文字、机械结构或必要动作细节，先安排清楚的承载镜头，再决定周围哪些地方可以概括。
body.en:
The following summary draws on Drama Skills production-format cards. These names can overlap: motion comics emphasize how images move, while anime and ink wash more often describe how they are drawn. Compare the actual implementation rather than treating them as mutually exclusive categories.

| Option | Record |
|---|---|
| 2D limited animation / motion comic | Decide first: Which images hold and which parts move; Preserve above all: Silhouettes, stable color blocks, and the active subject; Common cost or risk: Everyone and the background drift together, erasing the center of attention |
| Detailed anime treatment | Decide first: Structural differences and emotional expression among characters; Preserve above all: Distinct face shapes, hairstyles, and identifying colors under different lighting; Common cost or risk: “Delicate and beautiful” accumulates while characters in the same story look increasingly alike |
| Ink-wash brushwork | Decide first: Which edges may dissolve and which must remain clear; Preserve above all: Crucial silhouettes, held objects, and required spatial relationships; Common cost or risk: Blank space or ink bleed erases evidence and the target of an action |
| Chibi treatment | Decide first: Proportion system, main color blocks, and identifying marks to exaggerate; Preserve above all: A character’s proportions across shots and the relative size of objects; Common cost or risk: Constant bouncing and screen-filling symbols obscure cause and effect |

“Choose ink wash” cannot replace “this shot must show who gives what to whom.” For precise text, mechanical structure, or necessary action detail, plan a clear carrier shot first, then decide which surrounding areas may be simplified.

heading.zh: 用同一个场景比较，避免只挑漂亮图
heading.en: Compare Styles with the Same Scene Instead of Picking Only Pretty Images

body.zh:
原创比较场景：一名短卷发、穿橙色外套的成年人，把脱线的布偶递给修补师。修补师暂停桌上的缝补，先把手中工具放回桌面，再用双手接稳布偶。对方松手后，他把布偶放在桌上的空位，用空出的手把原布片移到桌边，示意对方坐下等。关键事实是**布偶交接完成，对方愿意处理这个请求**。

| 方向 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 二维限动 | 视觉与动作方案: 清楚线稿与平整色块；交接这一段让手和布偶动，背景工具架保持，工具先落桌；接稳并把布偶放到空位后，再移开原布片; 比较时看什么: 橙色袖口、布偶和修补师手部是否分得开，交接是否有结果 |
| 精细二次元 | 视觉与动作方案: 保留同一人物体态与发型，用面部近景表现等待；交接用能看见双方手部的镜头，随后给修补师抬眼回应; 比较时看什么: 表情是否补充关系信息，光色是否遮掉角色识别特征 |
| 水墨 | 视觉与动作方案: 人物衣形与布偶轮廓保留清楚边缘，工具架淡化，桌旁留白表现等待距离；交接结束后再让局部墨色缓慢展开; 比较时看什么: 留白有没有吞掉布偶，观众能否看清请求被接受 |
| Q版 | 视觉与动作方案: 先确认此版本的夸张比例与主色块，交接过程只突出布偶和接收动作；接稳后再加简短回应符号; 比较时看什么: 符号是否只是强调已经发生的接纳，而非替代实际交接 |

前三项可以沿用既有体态设计来比较表达；Q版若改变身体比例，应先确认改造后的角色设计，再检查前后镜头一致。画风试验不能悄悄替换已接受的人物。

这张表是创作方案，不是生成效果排名。实际比较时用同一段信息要求检查样片，避免一版只给表情、一版承担复杂动作，最后误把任务难度差异当成画风优劣。

四种方案都保留上述接收顺序与桌面落点。表情、墨迹或符号可以强调接纳，不能让已在两手中的布偶和原工具同时占据同一只手。这里是作者比较卡，不是原生制作形态文件，也没有展示实际生成结果。
body.en:
Original comparison scene: An adult with short curly hair and an orange coat hands a stuffed toy with a loose seam to a repairer. The repairer pauses the sewing on the table, sets the hand tool down, then receives the toy securely with both hands. After the visitor releases it, the repairer sets the toy in a clear space on the table, moves the previous fabric aside with a free hand, and motions for the visitor to sit and wait. The crucial facts are **the handoff is complete, and the repairer agrees to handle the request**.

| Option | Record |
|---|---|
| 2D limited animation | Visual and action plan: Clear line art and flat color blocks; move the hands and toy during the handoff while the background tool rack holds; set the tool down first; after receiving and placing the toy in the clear space, move the previous fabric aside; What to compare: Whether the orange cuff, toy, and repairer’s hands remain distinct, and whether the handoff reaches a result |
| Detailed anime | Visual and action plan: Preserve the same body type and hairstyle, use a facial close-up to show waiting; frame both pairs of hands during the handoff, then show the repairer looking up in response; What to compare: Whether expression adds relational information and whether lighting obscures identifying features |
| Ink wash | Visual and action plan: Keep clear edges on clothing shapes and the toy, fade the tool rack, and use blank space beside the table for waiting distance; let local ink spread slowly only after the handoff ends; What to compare: Whether blank space swallows the toy and whether viewers can see that the request was accepted |
| Chibi | Visual and action plan: Confirm the version’s exaggerated proportions and main color blocks first; emphasize only the toy and receiving action during the handoff, then add one brief response symbol after the grip is secure; What to compare: Whether the symbol merely emphasizes an acceptance that already occurred rather than replacing the handoff |

The first three directions can use the established body design while comparing visual treatments. If chibi changes bodily proportions, confirm the redesigned character first and then check consistency across shots. A style test must not quietly replace an accepted character.

This table is a set of creative plans, not a ranking of generated results. Compare samples against the same information requirement. Do not give one version only a facial expression and another a complex action, then mistake task difficulty for style quality.

All four plans preserve that reception order and tabletop destination. Expression, ink, or symbols may emphasize acceptance without putting the toy and previous tool in the same occupied hand. This is an author’s comparison card, not the native production-form file or a set of generated results.

heading.zh: 漫剧画风关键词，怎样写得可执行？
heading.en: How Do You Turn Motion-Comic Style Labels into Executable Terms?

body.zh:
| 方向 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 动漫感 | 补成可观察的选择: 清楚外轮廓、平整主色块、少量硬边阴影; 检查对象: 描边和阴影体系能否跨镜保持 |
| 厚涂感 | 补成可观察的选择: 可见笔触，以明暗塑造体积，材质边缘有软硬变化; 检查对象: 体积与材质是否仍有区分 |
| 国风感 | 补成可观察的选择: 墨线粗细变化、分层设色、留白分配前后距离; 检查对象: 线条和留白是否保护了必要地理 |
| 水墨意境 | 补成可观察的选择: 人物轮廓浓，背景淡；布偶外缘保持清楚，桌后局部允许洇化; 检查对象: 指定物是否仍然可见 |
| 可爱Q版 | 补成可观察的选择: 已确认的比例、大色块、简化材质，表情与手中物可读; 检查对象: 比例和物品尺度是否漂移 |

每个词都回答一个画面问题。没有特效遮挡就不必加一长串特效排除词；没有重要手势的近景也无需机械声明“所有手完整入画”。

先写主体、位置和当前状态，再补视觉表达。不要用一段风格词盖住尚未决定的剧情事实。
body.en:
| Option | Record |
|---|---|
| Anime look | Observable choices: Clear outer contours, flat main color blocks, and a small amount of hard-edged shading; What to inspect: Whether outlining and shading remain consistent across shots |
| Painterly look | Observable choices: Visible brushwork, light and shadow shaping volume, and hard-soft variation at material edges; What to inspect: Whether volumes and materials remain distinct |
| Chinese-inspired look | Observable choices: Varied ink-line weight, layered color application, and blank space that separates foreground from background; What to inspect: Whether line and blank space protect necessary spatial information |
| Ink-wash atmosphere | Observable choices: Dark character silhouettes and a pale background; keep the toy’s edge clear while allowing local bleed behind the table; What to inspect: Whether the specified object remains visible |
| Cute chibi | Observable choices: Confirmed proportions, large color blocks, simplified materials, and readable expressions and held objects; What to inspect: Whether proportions and object scale drift |

Each term should answer a visual question. If no effect blocks the frame, there is no need for a long list excluding effects. If a close-up contains no crucial gesture, there is no need to mechanically declare that “all hands are fully visible.”

State the subject, position, and current condition first, then add the visual treatment. Do not let a paragraph of style words conceal undecided story facts.

heading.zh: 画风定了以后，哪些地方保持，哪些可以变？
heading.en: After Choosing a Style, What Stays Fixed and What May Change?

body.zh:
把已经确定的视觉方向拆成两份：

- **跨镜保持**：认人的结构与色块、线条和上色方式、角色比例、服装结构，以及项目已经选定的材质处理。
- **按镜头调整**：关注谁、哪一层活动、局部光色、是否需要特写，以及当下有叙事作用的效果。

例如同一二维漫剧可以有对白定帧和动作段，变化的是行动与注意，不必顺手从平涂换成照片式皮肤。夜景可以降低整体亮度，但应保留足以区分角色的特征；情绪特效也要给关键物品留下位置。

把角色暂时看成纯黑轮廓，是检查剪影区分的一种办法。它特别适合依赖发型、衣形认人的设计；若项目主要靠面部结构区分角色，还需要正面与侧面等对应检查，不能让一个剪影测试替代全部识别。
body.en:
Split the chosen visual direction into two lists:

- **Keep across shots**: structures and color blocks used for recognition, line and coloring method, character proportions, clothing construction, and the selected material treatment.
- **Adjust per shot**: who receives attention, which layer moves, local lighting and color, whether a close-up is needed, and effects that serve the present story beat.

The same 2D motion comic can include held dialogue frames and action passages. What changes is action and attention; it need not switch casually from flat color to photographic skin. A night scene may lower overall brightness while preserving enough features to distinguish characters. Emotional effects must also leave space for a crucial object.

Viewing a character temporarily as a solid black silhouette is one way to test differentiation. It works especially well when recognition depends on hairstyle and clothing shape. If a project distinguishes characters mainly through facial structure, corresponding front and side checks are also needed; one silhouette test cannot replace every recognition check.

heading.zh: 不知道选哪种，按这三个问题缩小范围
heading.en: If You Cannot Choose, Narrow the Options with Three Questions

body.zh:
1. **哪种信息最不能丢？** 对话关系、具体操作、身份辨认、文字证据分别列出；先淘汰没有办法清楚承载这些信息的方案。
2. **哪些镜头值得投入连续动作？** 把选择、交接、转折等关键时刻列出来，其余考虑保持姿势、局部活动或剪辑衔接。这里是项目取舍，没有统一限动比例。
3. **你能稳定复用什么？** 比较角色结构、背景、服装与效果的维护方式，别只看第一张图是否惊艳。

选定后记录一段简短视觉说明：采用什么线条、色块和比例，哪些识别点保持，动作与效果怎样分工。接下来用[角色一致性方法](/drama-skills/character-consistency)把这些决定带进后续镜头。
body.en:
1. **Which information can least afford to disappear?** List dialogue relationships, specific operations, identity recognition, and written evidence separately. Eliminate any option that cannot carry them clearly.
2. **Which shots deserve continuous action?** List crucial moments such as choices, handoffs, and reversals. For the rest, consider held poses, local motion, or editorial transitions. This is a project trade-off; there is no universal ratio for limited animation.
3. **What can you reuse consistently?** Compare how character structure, backgrounds, clothing, and effects will be maintained instead of judging only whether the first image is impressive.

After choosing, record a short visual note: the line, color-block, and proportion system; the identifying features that remain; and how action and effects divide their jobs. Then use [character-consistency methods](/drama-skills/character-consistency) to carry those decisions into later shots.

q.zh: 水墨漫剧只能做古装吗？
q.en: Can an ink-wash motion comic work only for historical costume stories?

a.zh: 题材和画法可以分别选择。重点是水墨的浓淡、留白和边缘处理能否清楚表达这部故事需要的信息；现代场景也应先保住人物、物件和必要空间关系。
a.en: Subject and rendering style can be chosen separately. The question is whether ink density, blank space, and edge treatment can clearly express the information this story needs. A modern setting must still preserve characters, objects, and necessary spatial relationships.

q.zh: 动态漫就是让整张图轻微动起来吗？
q.en: Does a motion comic simply make the whole image move slightly?

a.zh: 先确定观众该注意哪项变化，再选择局部动作、姿势切换、背景视差或效果承接。整张图同时漂移容易掩盖真正发生的事情，运动应有明确职责。
a.en: First decide which change deserves the audience’s attention, then choose local action, pose changes, background parallax, or a connecting effect. Moving the entire image at once can conceal what actually happens. Motion needs a defined job.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama 比较这部故事的制作形态，保持同一场景事实，给出线条色块、角色识别、动作分配与关键信息风险，再记录选定视觉方向。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama` to compare production formats for this story while preserving the same scene facts. Describe line and color treatment, character recognition, allocation of motion, and risks to crucial information, then record the selected visual direction.” In Codex, use `$short-drama`.

title.zh: 竖屏短剧分镜怎么设计：多人站位、景别与字幕避让
title.en: Vertical Short-Drama Storyboarding: Blocking, Shot Size, and Overlays

seo_title.zh: 竖屏短剧分镜怎么设计｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Vertical Short-Drama Storyboarding | ZenStory

description.zh: 竖屏分镜先保住人物关系、关键动作和证据可读性，再选景别。用三人场景示例说明纵深站位、反应镜，以及按实际播放界面检查遮挡。
description.en: Keep relationships, key actions, and evidence readable before choosing shot size. A three-person example covers depth, reactions, and actual UI occlusion.

answer.zh: 竖屏分镜先确定这一镜必须看懂的人、动作或物件，再安排纵深与景别。多人可以分布在门口、桌边和后方，但关键反应不能被无意遮住。字幕和播放控件的避让范围取自本次实际交付方案；不要套一个未经确认的通用安全框。
answer.en: For a vertical storyboard, first decide which person, action, or object the audience must understand in the shot, then choose depth and shot size. Several characters can occupy the doorway, counter, and background, but an important reaction must not be hidden by accident. Derive clearance for subtitles and player controls from the actual delivery layout; do not impose an unconfirmed universal safe frame.

heading.zh: 画竖屏分镜前，先填这张小表
heading.en: Complete This Small Table Before Drawing Vertical Storyboards

body.zh:
| 项目 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 本镜重点 | 问自己: 观众看完多知道什么？; 记录什么: 一项主要事实或人物决定 |
| 行动空间 | 问自己: 谁能靠近物件，谁挡住谁？; 记录什么: 门、桌、走道与人的相对位置 |
| 同时反应 | 问自己: 哪两件事必须一起看见？; 记录什么: 行动者与接收者的可见位置 |
| 景别 | 问自己: 人脸、手或整体关系哪个最重要？; 记录什么: 能读清这项信息的取景范围 |
| 播放遮挡 | 问自己: 本次字幕、角标或控件挡哪里？; 记录什么: 实际截图或模板中的占用区 |

先处理画面中的任务，再谈“电影感”。竖屏宽度有限，把所有人物并排塞满画幅，会让脸、手和关键物件同时缩小。改用前后距离时，也要检查前景人物是否正好挡住本镜要看的证据。

这是按读者问题缩小后的编辑表，不是完整原生分镜格式。重点也可以是情绪、等待或关系距离，不要求每镜都得到新证据；需要多少镜由这场戏决定。
body.en:
| Item | Record |
|---|---|
| Shot priority | Ask yourself: What should the audience know after this shot?; Record: One main fact or character decision |
| Action space | Ask yourself: Who can reach the object, and who blocks whom?; Record: Relative positions of the door, counter, aisle, and people |
| Simultaneous reactions | Ask yourself: Which two things must remain visible together?; Record: Visible positions of the actor and recipient |
| Shot size | Ask yourself: Is the face, hand, or overall relationship most important?; Record: A frame wide enough to read that information |
| Playback obstruction | Ask yourself: Where will this delivery’s subtitles, badges, or controls appear?; Record: Occupied areas from the actual screenshot or template |

Solve the shot’s storytelling task before pursuing a “cinematic” look. A vertical frame has limited width. Packing every character side by side shrinks faces, hands, and key objects at once. Depth blocking creates room, but a foreground figure can still cover the very evidence the shot needs to reveal.

This is an editorial worksheet narrowed to the reader’s question, not the complete native storyboard format. A shot may center on emotion, waiting, or relational distance; it need not uncover new evidence. The scene determines the coverage.

heading.zh: 竖屏用什么景别？从需要交代的信息选
heading.en: Choose Shot Size by Information, Not by Habit

body.zh:
| 项目 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 全景 | 适合先交代什么: 出入口、三人位置、谁阻挡谁; 要注意丢掉的信息: 细小表情和纸面文字难以承担重点 |
| 中景 | 适合先交代什么: 手部动作、人物互动、物品交接; 要注意丢掉的信息: 仍要确认重要物件在画幅内 |
| 中近景 | 适合先交代什么: 说话与反应，保留必要的手势; 要注意丢掉的信息: 背后人物或出口容易离开视野 |
| 近景／特写 | 适合先交代什么: 决定、关键细节、某人的反应; 要注意丢掉的信息: 空间参照减少，需让观众知道它属于哪里 |

先找一档能持续看清本场互动的工作景别，再在注意对象改变时调整。例如双方一直围绕桌上的钥匙谈判，中景可同时保留手和钥匙；只有出现需要看清的刻痕时，才插入细节镜头。

每句台词都切一张头像，会丢掉人物靠近、退让和阻挡的过程。反过来，一直保持全景也可能让决定性的小动作读不清。
body.en:
| Item | Record |
|---|---|
| Wide shot | Best for establishing: Entrances, three-person positions, and who blocks whom; Information at risk: Small expressions and text on paper cannot carry the main point |
| Medium shot | Best for establishing: Hand actions, interaction, and object handoffs; Information at risk: Confirm that the important object remains inside the frame |
| Medium close-up | Best for establishing: Speech and reaction with necessary gestures; Information at risk: A background character or exit can easily leave the frame |
| Close-up/detail | Best for establishing: A decision, decisive feature, or individual reaction; Information at risk: Spatial reference decreases, so viewers need to know where it belongs |

Find a working shot size that keeps the scene’s continuing interaction readable, then change it when attention shifts. If two people negotiate over a key on the counter, a medium shot can retain both hands and the key. Insert a detail only when an engraving or other small feature must be read.

Cutting to a talking head for every line loses the process of approaching, yielding, and blocking. Holding one wide shot throughout can make a decisive small action unreadable.

heading.zh: 原创三人场景：刻字前，谁看见了错字？
heading.en: Original Three-Person Scene: Who Spots the Typo Before Engraving?

body.zh:
**剧情**：陶艺店柜台前，客户闻悦来取定制杯。店主乔雯把刻字样稿递给她确认，学徒已经拿起空白杯准备进后方工作间。闻悦指出样稿将“江舟”写成“江周”，乔雯立即叫住学徒，先改样稿。

**先定空间**：闻悦站在柜台外，乔雯在柜台内，学徒在后方工作间门边。纸样在乔雯手里，杯子在学徒手里，尚未刻字。关键是客户发现错误、店主传达停止、学徒听见后停下，三人的信息接收顺序都要可读。

| 项目 | 记录 |
|---|---|
| 建立互动 | 构图安排: 竖屏中景沿柜台斜向后方取景，闻悦靠近镜头的一侧，乔雯在另一侧稍远处，门边学徒可见；闻悦肩部不遮住店主递出的纸样; 本镜完成什么: 交代纸样与空白杯分别由谁控制，学徒即将离开 |
| 发现错误 | 构图安排: 纸样细节中让“江周”清楚可读，闻悦手指停在“周”字旁，说“应当是舟船的舟”；纸样保持由乔雯拿着; 本镜完成什么: 观众知道错在哪里，这个错误足以要求暂停刻字 |
| 传达并接收 | 构图安排: 回到能看见柜台与工作间门的角度，乔雯叫住学徒；学徒停在门前并回头，杯子仍在他手里; 本镜完成什么: 停止要求确实被听见，避免只拍发令者却遗漏接收结果 |

后续再拍修改后的样稿与客户确认。这里的三个镜头只示范如何让注意从纸面转向门边，不规定每场都用三镜。

若关键文字落在本次字幕覆盖区，先调整细节镜头的取景，让纸面信息可读；若柜台近景把学徒完全切掉，就在停止要求之后给他一个可见回应。不能为避让把杯子改放到客户手里，也不能让后镜无缘无故出现已经刻好字的杯子。

本例样稿中的“江周”和应改成的“江舟”已由剧情逐字给出，文字政策要求读清，分镜只安排载体、角度与阅读时间，不在这一环节另造姓名。文字提示和细节规格还需在实际成片中核对；未生成时不称已经可读。
body.en:
**Story:** At a pottery-shop counter, customer Wen Yue arrives to collect a personalized mug. Owner Qiao Wen offers the inscription proof for her to inspect, keeping hold of the sheet, while an apprentice picks up the blank mug and prepares to enter the rear workroom. Wen Yue sees that the requested name “江舟” has been written as “江周.” Both final characters are pronounced Zhou, but 舟 means boat; the written character is the evidence here. Qiao Wen immediately stops the apprentice so the proof can be corrected first.

**Establish the space:** Wen Yue stands on the customer side of the counter. Qiao Wen stands behind it. The apprentice waits by the rear-workroom door. Qiao Wen holds the proof; the apprentice holds the blank mug, which has not been engraved. The audience must read the order in which the customer notices the error, the owner gives the stop instruction, and the apprentice receives it.

| Item | Record |
|---|---|
| Establish the interaction | Composition: A vertical medium shot looks diagonally from the counter toward the rear. Wen Yue occupies the nearer side, Qiao Wen stands slightly deeper on the other side, and the apprentice remains visible by the door. Wen Yue’s shoulder does not cover the proof Qiao Wen extends.; What it accomplishes: Establishes who controls the proof and blank mug and that the apprentice is about to leave |
| Reveal the error | Composition: In a readable detail of the proof, show “江周.” Wen Yue’s finger stops beside 周: “The last character should be 舟, meaning boat, rather than 周.” Qiao Wen continues holding the sheet.; What it accomplishes: Makes the label error legible and gives a sufficient reason to pause engraving |
| Send and receive the instruction | Composition: Return to an angle containing the counter and workroom door. Qiao Wen calls to the apprentice. He stops before the doorway and turns back, still holding the mug.; What it accomplishes: Shows that the stop instruction was heard instead of filming only the person who gave it |

A later shot can show the corrected proof and the customer’s approval. These three shots demonstrate a shift of attention from paper to doorway; they do not prescribe three shots for every scene.

If the key lettering falls beneath the subtitles used in this delivery, adjust the detail framing until the proof remains readable. If a counter close-up removes the apprentice entirely, give him a visible response after the stop instruction. Do not avoid an overlay by moving the mug into the customer’s hand, and do not let a later shot suddenly contain a mug that has already been engraved.

The story supplies both “江周” and the intended “江舟” verbatim, and the text policy requires legibility. The storyboard places the surface, angle, and reading window rather than inventing another name. The text instruction and detail specification still need checking in the actual output; before generation, legibility remains a requirement.

heading.zh: 竖屏构图安全区：先确认遮挡，再避让
heading.en: Vertical Safe Areas: Confirm the Obstruction Before Reframing

body.zh:
“安全区”要对应这次播放时实际叠加的内容。向交付负责人拿到页面示意、模板或截图，确认三件事：占用哪一带，是否一直显示，哪类内容会覆盖在上面。

如果本次方案在底部放字幕，就重点查看落在底部的纸张文字、交接动作或坐姿变化。如果侧边存在互动控件，检查关键手势是否只发生在那一条区域。没有明确方案时，先按画面本身的可读性设计，并把遮挡范围留待确认，不自行编出统一百分比。

| 遮挡到什么 | 优先考虑的改法 |
|---|---|
| 必须读清的纸面文字 | 调整机位与取景，或给能读清的细节镜头 |
| 决定性的手部动作 | 在保持真实空间关系下改变观察角度，让动作离开覆盖区 |
| 人物的关键反应 | 换合适的景别或构图，保留反应而非一味缩小主体 |
| 无关紧要的背景 | 保留构图，不必为了每处遮挡重排整场戏 |

把播放界面的占用区叠在分镜草图或关键帧上检查。换了交付页面或字幕样式，就重新核对相应镜头；旧版避让结论不能直接沿用。
body.en:
A “safe area” must correspond to what will actually overlay this delivery. Ask the delivery owner for a page mockup, template, or screenshot, then confirm which bands are occupied, whether they remain onscreen, and what type of content covers them.

If subtitles sit at the bottom, inspect any paper text, handoff, or seated movement occurring there. If interaction controls occupy one side, check whether an essential gesture happens only beneath that strip. Without a confirmed layout, design for the image’s own readability and flag the overlay area for confirmation rather than inventing a universal percentage.

| What is obstructed | Preferred revision |
|---|---|
| Text on paper that must be read | Change the camera angle and framing, or add a readable detail shot |
| A decisive hand action | Preserve the real spatial relationship while changing the viewing angle so the action leaves the covered area |
| A character’s crucial reaction | Choose a better shot size or composition; retain the reaction instead of merely shrinking the subject |
| Unimportant background | Keep the composition; not every obstruction requires restaging the scene |

Overlay the player’s occupied areas on the storyboard sketch or keyframe. If the delivery page or subtitle style changes, recheck the relevant shots. Clearance decisions from an older layout do not carry over automatically.

heading.zh: 多人切镜时，怎样避免左右跳和人物消失？
heading.en: How to Avoid Screen-Direction Jumps and Vanishing Characters

body.zh:
- 先记清人物之间的连线，以及摄影机主要从哪一侧观察。
- 分开写“画面左侧”和“角色的左手”，避免两个“左”混成一件事。
- 对切时让视线能互相对应；改变观察侧或人物穿越位置时，用可见移动或重新建立空间帮助理解。
- 第三人仍在场时，决定观众此刻需要看见他的什么反应。可以留在同框、给独立反应，或有意暂时保留；不要因为切了两个近景就把他从剧情里忘掉。
- 物品交接只发生一次。后续细节镜头展示新状态，不要再把同一个让位或递物动作重新演一遍。

竖屏构图可以采用遮挡，但遮挡应服务叙事：藏住尚未揭示的人物，和不小心挡住已经需要看清的手，是两种不同选择。
body.en:
- Record the line between the characters and the side from which the camera primarily observes it.
- Write “left side of frame” separately from “the character’s left hand” so two meanings of left do not collapse into one.
- In shot/reverse shot, match eyelines. If the camera crosses to the other side or a character changes position, use visible movement or a new establishing view to restore orientation.
- When a third person remains present, decide which reaction viewers need now. Keep that person in the shared frame, give them a separate reaction, or withhold them deliberately; do not forget them merely because the edit has moved into two close-ups.
- An object handoff occurs once. Later detail shots show the new state rather than replaying the same yield or transfer.

Vertical composition can use occlusion, but it should serve the story. Concealing a character who has not yet been revealed is different from accidentally covering a hand viewers already need to see.

q.zh: 竖屏短剧一定要大量特写吗？
q.en: Does vertical short drama require lots of close-ups?

a.zh: 按当前镜头需要读清的事实选择。特写突出反应和细节，也会暂时失去空间关系。多人互动、让路或阻挡需要整体可见时，应保留合适的中景或全景。
a.en: Choose according to the fact the current shot must make readable. A close-up emphasizes reactions and details but temporarily removes spatial relationships. When a multi-person interaction, yielding, or blocking must remain visible, retain an appropriate medium or wide shot.

q.zh: 横屏直接裁成竖屏可以吗？
q.en: Can I simply crop a horizontal video into a vertical frame?

a.zh: 先检查裁切后是否仍能看懂人物关系、关键动作和证据。如果动作两端分布在横向两侧，简单裁切会删掉其中一端，需要重新取景、补镜或调整版式。
a.en: First check whether the crop preserves character relationships, essential actions, and evidence. If the two ends of an action sit on opposite horizontal edges, a simple crop removes one end. You will need to reframe, add coverage, or change the layout.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-storyboard 为这场戏设计竖屏分镜，先写清人物与物件位置，再按每镜需要读懂的信息选择景别；依据我提供的播放界面标出遮挡风险，保持动作与视线连续。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-storyboard`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-storyboard` to design a vertical storyboard for this scene. Establish every character and object position first, then choose each shot size according to the information viewers must read. Mark obstruction risks using the player layout I provide, and preserve continuity of action and eyelines.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-storyboard`.
