title.zh: AI视频一镜到底怎么写：让连续动作有完整落点
title.en: How to Plan a One-Take AI Video Scene

seo_title.zh: AI视频一镜到底怎么写：让连续动作有完整落点
seo_title.en: How to Plan a One-Take AI Video Scene

description.zh: 从连续等待、表演与空间关系判断是否需要一镜到底。附合租房告别案例、完整提示词、拆镜取舍与时长检查，不把一次生成等同于不切镜。
description.en: Plan a continuous scene with clear space, actions, sound, and an ending. Includes an original farewell, prompt, timing checks, and when to split.

answer.zh: 一镜到底是画面连续、不切镜，不是只提交一次生成任务。先确认这场戏为何需要持续观看，再排清人物路线、持物、声音和最后状态；在当前景别下让必要动作都能读到。若关键细节、完整对白或连续性无法容纳，重新安排镜长、调度或切镜，不用“一镜到底”四个字替代设计。
answer.en: A one-take scene remains visually continuous without cuts; it is not defined by submitting one generation job. Identify why uninterrupted watching matters, then map routes, props, sound, and the ending. Necessary actions must be readable at the chosen framing. If detail, full speech, or continuity will not fit, revise duration, staging, or cuts rather than treat “one take” as a complete design.

heading.zh: 什么时候一镜到底有价值
heading.en: When an uninterrupted take matters

body.zh:
连续等待让观众与人物一起承受时间；同框的两人让回应无法被剪掉；一次穿过空间的行动，可以让距离和阻碍真实可见。先选这些观看效果之一，再决定长短。

| 需要保住的效果 | 设计取舍 |
|---|---|
| 连续等待或沉默 | 明确等待什么、谁仍在场；不为画面忙碌加无关手势。 |
| 完整表演 | 让触发、接收与回应在同一时间里成立；不让人物提前知道后面的台词。 |
| 连续空间 | 路线与遮挡可解释；相机只能看到当前机位能看到的区域。 |
| 精确证据或不同表演选择 | 可改调度或分镜；需要特写时，不硬把所有信息塞进宽镜。 |

多镜头容器可以在一次生成任务中切几次，它仍是多镜头。一镜到底可以最终只使用一段截取，但采用范围里要保持连续。
body.en:
Continuous waiting makes viewers share time with a character. Two people in one frame retain a response that cutting might remove. Moving through space can make distances and obstacles visible. Choose the viewing effect before choosing length.

| Effect | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| Waiting or silence | Define what is awaited and who remains present; avoid unrelated gestures. |
| Complete performance | Preserve trigger, reception, and response in one timeline without premature knowledge. |
| Continuous space | Explain routes and occlusions; the camera sees only what its position permits. |
| Exact evidence or different performances | Reblock or split when needed; do not force close detail into a wide frame. |

A multi-shot container can cut several times in one generation job. It still contains several shots. A long take may be excerpted in editing, provided the selected passage remains continuous.

heading.zh: 先排路线、持物与注意
heading.en: Map routes, props, and attention

body.zh:
画一张很简单的平面关系：入口、出口、固定物件、人物起点和可通行路线。再逐拍写动作条件与结果：放下后才松手，空出手后才提另一物；对方听见后才回应。

相机也有自己的路线。固定镜头可以让人走出画面，跟拍可以保住移动者；两者都可用，但同一区间不能既全程固定又全程跟随。若中途转为运动，写出从何时开始、跟谁、停在哪。

动作之间自然共享时间，例如说话时看向对方；互为前提的步骤不能用“同时”压缩。小眼神承担唯一转折而远景看不到时，改成能读到的选择或调整景别，不只是加更多情绪词。
body.en:
Sketch entrances, exits, fixed objects, starting positions, and a passable route. For each action, name prerequisites and results: set an object down before releasing it; free a hand before lifting another; hear a line before responding.

The camera has its own route. A fixed frame may let someone leave it; following can retain a moving person. Both are valid, but cannot govern the same interval simultaneously. A transition to movement needs a trigger, subject, and stopping point.

Naturally parallel channels can share time, such as looking while speaking. Dependent steps cannot be compressed with “simultaneously.” If a tiny glance carries the only turn but a wide frame cannot show it, revise the action or framing rather than add emotion words.

heading.zh: 原创案例：离开合租房
heading.en: Original example: leaving a shared apartment

body.zh:
芮蓉已经搬走其他物品，回来归还钥匙；宋夏知道她今天搬离，仍愿意送她到门口。剧本只要求归还、告别和离开，不在本镜解决两人全部关系。芮蓉站在钥匙托盘旁，右手握钥匙，自己的小行李包在脚边；宋夏站在门边，门尚未打开。桌旁到门口是两步可通行路线。

这场选择固定中远景，让托盘、两人、包和门同时可见。关键变化是芮蓉真正松开钥匙、宋夏打开门、她带自己的包离开；无需特写读钥匙刻字，也不让脸部微表情承担唯一信息。

| 阶段 | 连续行动与状态 |
|---|---|
| 归还 | 芮蓉把钥匙放入空托盘，松开右手；钥匙留在托盘，没有交到宋夏手里。 |
| 告别 | 她转向宋夏，短暂停住。宋夏看见钥匙已经放下，打开门，说“路上慢点”。 |
| 离开 | 芮蓉听完后提起脚边自己的包，沿空出的路线跨过门口离画；宋夏留在门边，钥匙仍在托盘。 |

一镜不断的作用是把松手后的停顿、回应与离开连起来，不用切镜帮两人迅速化解尴尬。钥匙放下支持归还，不能直接证明房租、押金或关系争执已经结清。
body.en:
Rui Rong has moved her other belongings and returns the key. Song Xia knows she is moving out today and is willing to see her to the door. The script requires return, farewell, and departure, without resolving their entire relationship. Rui stands beside an empty key tray, key in her right hand and her small travel bag at her feet. Song stands by the closed door. A clear two-step route connects table and doorway.

A fixed medium-wide frame includes the tray, people, bag, and door. The key’s release, the door opening, and Rui leaving with her bag carry the change. No engraved detail needs a close-up; subtle facial movement is not the sole information channel.

| Stage | Continuous action and state |
|---|---|
| Return | Rui places the key in the empty tray and releases it. It remains there rather than transferring to Song’s hand. |
| Farewell | She turns to Song and pauses. Song sees the key set down, opens the door, and says, “Take care on the way.” |
| Departure | After hearing the line, Rui lifts her own bag and crosses the clear doorway out of frame. Song stays by the door; the key remains in the tray. |

The uninterrupted take joins the pause after release, the response, and departure without editing away discomfort. Returning the key does not establish settled rent, a deposit, or every relationship dispute.

heading.zh: 可复制的连续镜头提示词
heading.en: A continuous-shot prompt

body.zh:
以下是上述原创场景的自然语言示例，不是已生成视频。若提供真实起始帧，先核对它符合起点；没有图片输入时，保留完整静态说明。

> 合租房门厅，固定中远景，钥匙桌在画面左侧，门口在右侧，两者之间通道空着。芮蓉在桌旁，右手握一把钥匙，小行李包放在她脚边；宋夏站在尚未打开的门旁。全段保持同一连续镜头。芮蓉把钥匙放入桌上空托盘，松手，转向宋夏停住。宋夏看见钥匙落下后打开门，说：“路上慢点。”芮蓉听完，右手提起自己的包，沿通道走过门口离开画面。结尾保留宋夏站在门边、托盘中一把钥匙的状态。相机固定，不跟到走廊。保留放钥匙、开门、提包的同期声与房间底声；无旁白，不在本镜新增配乐或标题。

持续身份、服装与布局接项目已有参考；不把“钥匙已经在托盘”的尾帧冒充起点。若下一镜要拍走廊，从芮蓉已出门、仍右手持包的状态接，不让她第二次放钥匙。
body.en:
This natural-language example describes the original scene rather than a generated result. With an actual starting image, verify its state; without image input, retain the static description.

> Shared-apartment entrance, fixed medium-wide view: key table on the left, door on the right, a clear path between. Rui stands by the table with one key in her right hand and her travel bag at her feet. Song stands beside the closed door. Keep one continuous shot. Rui puts the key in the empty tray, releases it, turns toward Song, and pauses. After seeing the return, Song opens the door and says, “Take care on the way.” Rui hears the line, lifts her bag with her right hand, and walks through the doorway out of frame. End with Song by the door and one key in the tray. The camera stays fixed rather than following into the corridor. Retain key, door, and bag sounds with room ambience. No voiceover; add no score or title within this shot.

Use the project’s established identity, clothing, and layout references. An ending image with the key already returned cannot stand in for the start. A corridor shot continues after Rui exits with the bag still in her right hand, without returning the key again.

heading.zh: 先演一遍，再判断时长
heading.en: Rehearse before trusting duration

body.zh:
先按实际路线、完整台词和停顿排一条时间线。能自然并行的看人与说话共享时间，放钥匙、松手、提包与出门按前提顺序排。给结束状态留下可读时间，不把“最后走出去”当作动作已完成。

本例没有计时演练或声音文件，因此不声称精确需要几秒。选择项目允许的镜长后，用走位或同句同表演录音检验，再回看实际生成；不能只因为提示词写了“十秒内完成”就当作可行。

一处失败可以只剪下合格部分，但若缺掉归还或告别就不再覆盖原场职责。补拍是否替代完整镜头、哪些内容仍由原片承担，要写清；为了缩短而删台词、跳到门外或变成画外音，应先修分镜与剧本。
body.en:
Build a timeline from the actual route, full line, and pauses. Looking and speaking may naturally overlap; placement, release, bag pickup, and exit follow their prerequisites. Leave time to read the end state instead of merely declaring departure complete.

This example has no timed rehearsal or recording and therefore claims no exact duration. Choose a duration allowed by the project, check blocking or a same-line, same-performance recording, then review the actual generation. “Finish within ten seconds” does not establish feasibility.

A failed take may contain usable excerpts, but removing the return or farewell loses a story responsibility. Explain whether pickups replace the whole shot and what the original still covers. Shortening speech, jumping outside, or converting dialogue to voiceover requires a storyboard or script revision first.

heading.zh: 什么时候切开更好
heading.en: When splitting serves the scene

body.zh:
- 必须看清的证据太小：给它独立可读画面，或先重排距离。
- 表演与行走互相挤占：减少无关动作，仍放不下再延长或拆镜。
- 一段生成反复在同一位置失败：定位实际失败，比较修改起点、路径、时长或制作方式，不把重抽次数当原因证明。
- 切开后道具换手：逐项接住持物、位置、视线与门的状态。
- 为“高级”强保长镜：回到观看效果；连续性有价值就保留，反应与节奏需要不同选择就切。

拆镜增加跨镜一致性工作，一镜到底增加局部失败的替换成本。以这场戏的体验和真实输出取舍，没有所有项目通用的最优方案。
body.en:
- Essential evidence is too small: give it readable coverage or adjust distance.
- Acting and movement compete: remove irrelevant activity, then extend or split if necessary.
- Generation repeatedly fails at one point: locate the observed defect and compare starting state, route, timing, or production method; retry count does not prove cause.
- Props switch hands after splitting: match holdings, positions, gaze, and door state.
- A long take survives only for prestige: return to the viewing effect; retain useful continuity or cut for response and rhythm.

Splitting adds cross-shot continuity work; an uninterrupted generation can cost more to replace after a local failure. Choose using the scene’s experience and actual output rather than one universal optimum.

q.zh: 一镜到底一定要摄影机移动吗？
q.en: Must a one-take scene move the camera?

a.zh: 不用。固定机位也可保留完整表演和沉默；是否运动取决于需要持续看见谁、哪项信息和空间关系。
a.en: No. A fixed view can retain complete performance and silence. Movement depends on who, which information, and what spatial relation must remain visible.

text.zh: 用 $short-drama-storyboard 只设计这场一镜到底方案：说明连续观看的理由、人物路线、持物、声音、开始与结束状态，保留原剧本选择与台词。与切开方案比较；未测时长注明估计，不生成视频。
text.en: Use $short-drama-storyboard only to plan an uninterrupted scene: explain its viewing purpose, routes, props, sound, start and end. Preserve script choices and exact lines. Compare a cut version, mark unmeasured timing as estimated, and do not generate video.

动作、表演与声音预算

title.zh: AI视频空镜提示词怎么写：场景、声音与叙事作用
title.en: How to Write AI Video Prompts for Empty Shots

seo_title.zh: AI视频空镜提示词怎么写：场景、声音与叙事作用
seo_title.en: How to Write AI Video Prompts for Empty Shots

description.zh: 先判断空镜要建立地点、承载等待还是保留余味。区分空场参考图与动态镜头，附放映厅案例、完整提示词和画外声音边界。
description.en: Give empty shots a purpose in place, waiting, or aftermath. Distinguish location references from footage, with a cinema example and sound boundaries.

answer.zh: 空镜不是删掉人物后堆“电影感”。先写观众要通过这个无人画面知道或感受什么，再确定地点、可见物、变化、声音与结束状态。场景参考图负责可复用布局，视频空镜负责此刻的观看；无人物时不套表演弧，也不凭空增加脚步、对白或神秘访客。静止与留白可以成立，是否保留按叙事和风格判断。
answer.en: An empty shot needs more than removing people and adding “cinematic.” Define what viewers should learn or experience, then specify location, visible objects, change, sound, and the ending. A location reference supplies reusable geography; footage supplies this moment’s viewing experience. Without people, omit acting arcs and do not invent footsteps, speech, or mysterious visitors. Stillness and negative space are valid when they serve the story and style.

heading.zh: 空镜先有用途，再有画面
heading.en: Purpose before a pretty image

body.zh:
空镜可以交代下一场的地点，让观众与人物一起等待，或在人物离开后保留物件与空间的余味。没有人物不等于没有作用，也不等于每次都必须摇镜、下雨或让窗帘动。

| 用途 | 先明确什么 |
|---|---|
| 建立地点 | 入口、出口和关键区域的关系；是否能接住下一镜机位。 |
| 等待 | 正在等什么、哪些物件承载期待、这一刻还未发生什么。 |
| 后果或余味 | 前一场已建立哪个选择，留下的空间或物件怎样让人继续感受。 |
| 纯粹氛围 | 氛围是不是作者有意的段落功能；与节奏、声音和后续转场怎样相接。 |

快节奏对白场里，无台词、无动作又没有职责的空镜可以删；有意保留静止观察时，不为满足“必须变化”硬加剧情。空镜也不必强行承担悬疑。
body.en:
An empty shot can establish the next location, sustain waiting, or retain objects and space after departure. No people does not mean no function, nor compulsory pans, rain, or moving curtains.

| Purpose | Define first |
|---|---|
| Place | Entrances, exits, and key zones, with a usable next-shot camera relation. |
| Waiting | What is awaited, objects carrying expectation, and what has not happened yet. |
| Aftermath | Which established choice leaves a space or object that continues the experience. |
| Atmosphere | The author’s intended pause and its relation to rhythm, sound, and the next transition. |

In a fast dialogue scene, an inactive empty insert with no responsibility may be removed. Deliberate still observation does not need invented plot to satisfy a change quota. Empty shots need not manufacture suspense.

heading.zh: 空场参考图和视频空镜分开写
heading.en: Separate location plates from footage

body.zh:
空场参考图通常不放演员，目的是把门窗、通道、物件布局和光源交清楚，方便后面复用。它不会自动替你确定故事此刻的人物离场、门已开或某件物品已归还。

视频空镜则从已定剧情状态开始。剧本中的票留在托盘，起始图就不能让票已经被人拿走；镜头中没有人，画外声音仍可能意味着有人到来，要按已有声音安排处理。

真实参考图可省掉已确定外观的重复说明，仍要写本镜变化与声音；没有图片输入时，把布局、物件与光态写入正文。只看文件名不能断言画面无人、没有文字或布局正确。
body.en:
An empty location plate usually excludes performers so doors, paths, objects, and light sources remain reusable. It does not establish that someone has left, a door has opened, or an object has been returned in the story.

Footage starts from the agreed story state. Tickets remaining in a tray cannot disappear in the starting image. Offscreen sound can imply arrival even with nobody visible, so follow the established sound plan.

A real reference may remove repeated appearance descriptions, but still specify motion and sound. Without image input, include layout, objects, and light state in the prompt. A filename cannot prove an image is empty, text-free, or geographically correct.

heading.zh: 原创案例：两张还没被取走的票
heading.en: Original example: two uncollected tickets

body.zh:
老放映厅最后一晚，许棠在前一场把两张留给旧友的票放进入口托盘，开启已经装好的放映机，随后走出这个机位的画面。朋友是否会来仍未揭晓。票的意义已由前场说明，不靠本镜读清印字。门厅灯常亮，内厅投影的光能落到半开的内门上。

空镜职责是让观众看见放映已经继续，门厅托盘中的两张票仍在；它只能说明这个观察区间内没有人取票，不能证明朋友永远没来。

| 项目 | 本镜具体安排 |
|---|---|
| 构图 | 入口门厅固定中景，前景托盘中两张票，后景半开内门；保留已建立布局。 |
| 可见变化 | 内厅投影的明暗在门面上缓慢变换；托盘和两张票保持原位，没有手入画。 |
| 声音 | 延续前镜已开启放映机的声音，保留门厅底声；不新增敲门、脚步或说话。 |
| 终点 | 两张票还在托盘，内门仍半开，放映仍在进行；下一镜按此状态承接。 |

真正提供时间感的是放映与等待并存，不需要额外雨、飘尘和惊雷。若剧情选择朋友此时到来，那是下一项事件，要另修场面与声音，不能作为“丰富氛围”顺手加入。
body.en:
On an old cinema’s final evening, Xu Tang previously placed two tickets for old friends in the entrance tray, started the loaded projector, and moved outside this camera’s view. Whether her friends will arrive remains open. The previous scene establishes the tickets’ meaning; this shot need not read their lettering. Lobby lights stay on; projection light reaches the half-open inner door.

The empty shot shows the screening continuing while both tickets remain. It establishes no collection within the observed interval, not that the friends never arrive.

| Item | This shot’s arrangement |
|---|---|
| Composition | Fixed medium view of the lobby; tray and two tickets foreground, half-open inner door behind; preserve the established layout. |
| Visible change | Projection brightness changes slowly across the door; tray and tickets remain in place, with no hand entering. |
| Sound | Continue the established projector sound and lobby ambience without new knocks, footsteps, or speech. |
| End | Both tickets remain, inner door half-open, screening continuing; the next shot inherits this state. |

Projection and waiting supply time without extra rain, dust, or thunder. If friends arrive now, that is another event requiring scene and sound revision, not an atmospheric embellishment.

heading.zh: 可复制的空镜提示词
heading.en: An empty-shot prompt

body.zh:
本例是写作示例，尚无生成结果。项目的画幅、镜长与参考图另按已有设定选择。

> 老放映厅入口门厅，沿用已确认的门口、托盘与内门布局。固定中景，前景托盘内有两张未取走的票，后景内门半开；门厅灯常亮，内厅放映的光在门面上缓慢变化。整镜无人或手进入，托盘与两张票不移动，内门不开合。延续前一镜已经启动的放映机声音与门厅底声，无新增脚步、敲门或对白；无旁白，不在本镜新起配乐。票面不要求读清文字，不新增字幕或标题。结尾仍保留两张票、半开的内门与正在放映的状态。

“整镜无人”限定可见画面，不否定已经存在的放映机声。若项目采用完全无声的风格，另明确改变声音方案；不要用笼统“无声音”同时擦掉必须承接的声源。
body.en:
This is a writing example without generated footage. Use the project’s established aspect ratio, duration, and references.

> Entrance lobby of the old cinema, preserving the approved entrance, tray, and inner-door layout. Fixed medium view: two uncollected tickets in the foreground tray, inner door half-open behind. Lobby lamps stay on while projection brightness slowly changes across the door. No person or hand enters; tray and tickets remain still, and the inner door does not move. Continue the projector already started in the preceding shot and lobby ambience. Add no footsteps, knocks, or speech. No voiceover or new score within this shot. Ticket lettering need not be legible; add no subtitle or title. End with both tickets, the half-open door, and ongoing projection.

“No person enters” limits visible content without suppressing the established projector. A fully silent style needs a separate sound decision rather than broad “no sound” that also erases required continuity.

heading.zh: 回看片段，检查空场与知情范围
heading.en: Review emptiness and knowledge scope

body.zh:
回看实际输出，不只看首帧：

- 人或手是否中途出现，是否偷偷取走票；玻璃反射、门内和前景遮挡也要查。
- 票的数量、位置与门的开合是否从始至终符合本镜。
- 画外声音是否凭空引入到来、离开或新事件。
- 关键区域在手机画面上是否可读；票无需逐字读清，却不能小到看不出仍有两张。
- 与前后镜相接时，光态、物件和放映机底声是否有无原因的改变。

观众看见这个机位无人，不等于全栋楼无人。角色是否知道托盘里的票还在，也要有看见或其他信息来源；空镜向观众展示不自动成为人物记忆。
body.en:
Inspect the actual clip, not only its first frame:

- Does a person or hand appear or collect tickets, including reflections, doorway depth, and foreground occlusion?
- Do ticket count, position, and door state remain correct throughout?
- Does offscreen sound invent an arrival, departure, or event?
- Are relevant objects readable on a phone? Lettering is unnecessary, but two tickets must still be discernible.
- Do adjacent shots introduce unexplained changes to light, props, or projector ambience?

Nobody in this view does not mean nobody in the building. A character needs observation or another source to know tickets remain. Information supplied by an empty shot does not automatically become character memory.

heading.zh: 空镜常见失败怎样修
heading.en: Fixes for common empty-shot failures

body.zh:
| 观察到的问题 | 有范围的修订 |
|---|---|
| 自动塞进路人 | 先查参考图空场状态，再限定允许出现的内容；不能只把“无人”重复十遍。 |
| 静止段落太长 | 判断等待或余味是否仍成立，截短或重新组织交接；不一律加镜头运动。 |
| 各背景物同时乱动 | 保留真正承担时间感的变化，其余指定保持；必要时简化场景或调整制作。 |
| 神秘声音带错剧情 | 恢复已有声源和进入时机，删去无来源事件；再听前后镜。 |
| 只有漂亮景色 | 写清建立空间、等待或余味的用途；确实没有作用时删。 |

有意静止、纯环境纹理或抽象视觉也可以是导演选择；审查它与这段叙事的关系，不用“每镜必有人物反应”否定空镜。
body.en:
| Observation | Scoped repair |
|---|---|
| An unintended passerby appears | Check the reference’s empty state, then specify permitted content rather than repeat “nobody.” |
| Stillness lasts too long | Judge waiting or aftermath, shorten or reorganize the handoff, without compulsory movement. |
| Every background element moves | Retain the change carrying time; hold others, simplify, or change production when needed. |
| Mysterious sound invents plot | Restore established sources and timing, remove unsupported events, then listen across the cut. |
| Only attractive scenery remains | Identify place, waiting, or aftermath; remove the shot if it serves none. |

Intentional stillness, environmental texture, or abstraction can be a director’s choice. Review its narrative relationship rather than require a character reaction in every shot.

q.zh: 空镜一定不能有画外声音吗？
q.en: Must an empty shot exclude offscreen sound?

a.zh: 可以有。只要声源与剧情已经建立，画外声能承接空间和时间；新增脚步或对白可能改变知情与事件，不能当作装饰随意加入。
a.en: No. Established offscreen sound can carry space and time. New footsteps or speech can change knowledge or events and should not be added as decoration.

text.zh: 用 $short-drama-video-prompts 写这个已定空镜：先列观众用途、地点、物件状态和既有声音，再写固定或运动、可见变化与终点。无人物时省略表演弧，不新增人、文字或剧情事件；提供手填通用提示词，不生成视频。
text.en: Use $short-drama-video-prompts for this agreed empty shot: state viewing purpose, location, object states, and existing sound; then write camera, visible change, and ending. Omit acting arcs without people. Invent no people, text, or story events. Provide a manual natural-language prompt without generating video.

label.zh: 镜头职责与视觉选择
摄影机与环境声音连续性
无人物镜头省略表演弧

title.zh: 小说悲伤场景怎么写：具体失去与人物反应
title.en: How to Write a Sad Scene in Fiction

seo_title.zh: 小说悲伤场景怎么写：具体失去与人物反应
seo_title.en: How to Write a Sad Scene in Fiction

description.zh: 小说悲伤场景怎么写才动人：先让读者认识值得留恋的关系与日常，再写具体失去怎样发生、人物怎样回应。附告别场景、改前改后、检查表与提示词，不靠堆叠死亡和哭喊。
description.en: Write a sad scene through a specific bond, a loss, and a response. Use an original farewell example, revision checks, and a bounded writing prompt.

answer.zh: 写悲伤场景，先让读者知道人物会失去什么具体的相处、机会或生活，再让这份失去在场景里发生，并留下可信的反应。角色可以哭、沉默、说笑或继续做事；要检验的是这些反应是否符合这个人，是否让读者感到此前的日常已经改变。悲伤不必来自死亡，也不必以立刻振作收束。
answer.en: A sad scene gives readers a specific relationship, opportunity, or routine to care about, lets the loss occur, and follows the character’s response. Crying, silence, humor, and ordinary work can all fit. Test whether the response belongs to this person and makes the changed life felt. Death is optional, and immediate recovery is not required.

heading.zh: 先写清失去的是什么，不先安排哭法
heading.en: Name the loss before choosing the reaction

body.zh:
“她很难过”告诉读者情绪名称，还没交代这份难过为什么属于她。先补一句：过去她能和谁做什么，现在哪一部分不能照旧？可能是朋友每周来排练、父亲还没听过的新曲、两个人曾经计划的旅程。只选本场真正相关的部分，不必把人生所有遗憾一起搬来。

Oh Story 的情感方法先问承载对象、为什么是现在、此前为什么仍悬着，以及人物能做什么。用于悲伤场景时，可把这些问题写成一张简表：

| 要回答的事 | 本场写下什么 |
|---|---|
| 值得留恋什么 | 一段已被展示的相处、投入或可能性 |
| 什么现在改变 | 离开、错过、关系结束或事实被确认；分清暂时失约与不可照旧 |
| 人物知道多少 | 谁已知结果，谁仍在期待；不把读者的信息自动给角色 |
| 人物如何回应 | 试着留住、接受一部分、拒绝谈、继续办事，或暂时没有决定 |
| 场后还剩什么 | 新的生活安排、尚未说完的话、不能立即修好的缺口 |

这是场景诊断，不是必须凑齐五个剧情事件。悲伤也不需要添加坏人；双方都作了合理选择，告别仍可能难受。
body.en:
“She was sad” names a feeling without explaining why it belongs to her. Ask: what could she do with someone before, and what cannot continue in the same way? A weekly rehearsal, a song her father never heard, a trip two people planned. Use what matters here rather than gathering every regret in her life.

Oh Story’s emotional method asks what carries the feeling, why now, why the situation remained unresolved, and what the character can do. For a sad scene, use this worksheet:

| Question | What to establish |
|---|---|
| What matters? | A relationship, investment, or possibility readers have seen |
| What changes now? | A departure, missed chance, ending, or confirmed fact; distinguish a temporary absence from a changed life |
| Who knows? | Who knows the outcome and who still expects otherwise; reader knowledge is not character knowledge |
| How do they respond? | Try to hold on, accept part of it, avoid talking, continue working, or remain undecided |
| What remains? | A changed routine, unfinished words, or a gap that cannot immediately be repaired |

This diagnoses a scene; it does not require five separate plot events. A sad farewell can involve two reasonable choices without needing a villain.

heading.zh: 让相处先有质感，再选择揭示顺序
heading.en: Give the bond texture, then choose the reveal

body.zh:
铺垫不必很长，却要让关系区别于“他们是好朋友”。一次共同练习中谁替谁留位置，一句只有两人懂的提醒，一件认真完成过的小事，都能给失去一个可辨认的对象。物件和习惯可选，不要求固定出现三次。

**读者预先知道告别**时，可以照常写最后一次相处：角色仍在说笑，读者知道这次之后日常会变。**人物与读者一起得知结果**时，要留出接收信息、理解它和回应的空间，别让一句消息立刻跳到结尾感悟。前者是 skill 中“先知坏结果，再看美好事物、结果发生、人物反应”的一种用法；后者不用为了套这个顺序提前剧透。

反应按人物来选。一个爱说话的人突然认真问下一次联系时间，和一个寡言的人直接哭出来，都可能比套式的攥拳更准确。直写心理也可以；若沉默需要读者知道原因，就保留必要的认知。
body.en:
A bond does not need a long introduction, but it should mean more than “they were friends.” Who saves a place at rehearsal? What reminder belongs only to them? What small task have they completed together? Objects and routines are options, without a fixed repetition count.

When **readers know the farewell is coming**, the last ordinary encounter can hurt while the characters still joke. When **the character and readers learn together**, allow room to receive, understand, and respond before a concluding reflection. The first uses the skill’s sequence of anticipated loss, valued experience, loss, and response; the second need not reveal the outcome early to fit that sequence.

Choose the response for this person. A talkative character asking precisely when they will speak again, or a quiet character openly crying, may be more accurate than a stock clenched fist. Interior thought is also valid. Keep the necessary understanding when silence alone cannot communicate its reason.

heading.zh: 原创范例：最后一次合唱与下一周的空位
heading.en: Original example: a last duet and next week’s empty place

body.zh:
**已有事实**：许沛与温禾每周六在社区合唱团练二重唱。温禾已接受外地的学习机会，周日坐车离开；两人和读者都知道。许沛替她高兴，也不想失去这段周末日常。合唱团负责人已知她要走，下周由许沛试唱这首歌的独唱版本，不假装临时缺席。

**容易失败的写法：**

> 温禾离开时，许沛心如刀绞，泪如雨下。她们都明白，人生有太多无可奈何，友情会永远留在心中。

情绪很重，但读者不知道这两人具体失去了什么，告别也只在概述中发生。

**场景版本：**

> “第二段别抢我。”温禾把谱架往许沛这边挪了挪。
>
> “你每次都这么说。”许沛翻到那一页，两个人的铅笔记号挤在同一行。
>
> 她们唱完最后一遍。温禾去拿外套，许沛还按着谱页：“下周六，你那边能打电话吗？”
>
> “下午有课。晚上我给你打。”
>
> 许沛松开手，帮她把落在椅背上的围巾递过去。“那你记得。别只给我发学校照片。”

温禾周日确实离开。**转到下一周**，不要把两个时点剪成同一次排练：

> 第二段开头，许沛照旧停了一拍。谱架旁没有人接。她看了一眼自己的铅笔记号，从那一行重新唱起。结束后，她给温禾发了条消息：“今天没抢你。晚上给你听。”

最后一次共同演唱、约定通话、实际离开和下周改变都有交代。温禾获得机会没有被写成背叛，通话也没有恢复每周并肩排练。许沛继续唱，不等于她已经不难过；故事若需要通话兑现，后文再写温禾实际接通，而不是把约定算作完成。
body.en:
**Established facts:** Xu Pei and Wen He rehearse a duet at the community choir every Saturday. Wen He has accepted a course in another city and leaves on Sunday. Both friends and the reader know. Xu Pei is glad for her and dreads losing their weekend routine. The choir director knows about the departure; Xu Pei will try a solo arrangement next week, rather than treating Wen He as temporarily absent.

**A weak version:**

> When Wen He left, Xu Pei’s heart shattered and tears poured down. They understood that life was full of helpless sorrow and friendship would live forever in their hearts.

The language is intense, but readers have no specific shared life to miss, and the farewell is only summarized.

**A scene version:**

> “Don’t steal my entrance in the second verse.” Wen He nudged the music stand toward Xu Pei.
>
> “You say that every time.” Xu Pei found the page. Their pencil marks crowded the same line.
>
> They sang it once more. Wen He reached for her coat; Xu Pei still held the page. “Can you call next Saturday?”
>
> “I have class in the afternoon. I’ll call that evening.”
>
> Xu Pei let go and handed over the scarf left on the chair. “Remember. Don’t just send me campus photos.”

Wen He leaves on Sunday. **Move explicitly to the following week**, rather than blending two dates into one rehearsal:

> At the second verse, Xu Pei left the usual beat. Nobody entered beside the stand. She looked at her pencil mark and started again from that line. Afterward, she messaged Wen He: “Didn’t steal your entrance today. I’ll sing it for you tonight.”

The last duet, promised call, actual departure, and changed rehearsal are present. Wen He’s opportunity is not betrayal, and a call does not restore singing side by side each week. Continuing to sing does not mean Xu Pei has stopped missing her. If the call matters later, write it actually happening; an agreement is not fulfillment.

heading.zh: 修稿检查与可复制提示词
heading.en: Revision checks and a copyable prompt

body.zh:
| 读起来不动人的原因 | 优先修哪里 |
|---|---|
| 只有哭喊，没有值得失去的具体相处 | 回到前文关系与投入，不临时插入一大段完美回忆 |
| 每段反应都在重复“很难过” | 保留不同作用的反应，合并纯复述；哭本身不是问题 |
| 为加强悲伤突然加死亡、疾病或背叛 | 检查已有失去是否尚未被写清，不先升级灾难 |
| 角色一笑或开始办事就被宣布走出来 | 分清当下行动与整段情绪弧线，不强迫即时恢复 |
| 每次都用不流泪显得高级 | 让克制、失控或复杂感受服从人物与文风 |
| 结尾把主题解释完 | 选择准确的动作、对白、内心或意象留下余韵；作者明确选择的评论可保留 |

**提示词：**

> 检查下面悲伤场景。先列出已有关系与投入、具体失去、人物与读者的知情范围、失去发生的时点和人物反应。指出原句中空泛或重复之处，再给有限修订。不新增死亡、疾病、背叛、回忆事件或原文没有的机会；保留作者文风与有功能的哭、沉默、心理直写。缺少铺垫时标为待作者补充，不代造。对照列出改变的句子和待确认处。正文：〔粘贴〕

采用前对照原文事实，再连读前后两场。预先悲伤、当场反应和后来的生活不必相同；只要变化有来处，就不用按固定情绪阶段排队。

本页安排一场悲伤如何发生。词句、身体反应与直写的取舍见[情绪描写](/oh-story/emotion-on-the-page)；整篇关系撕裂与虐文推进见[虐文写法](/oh-story/angst-fiction)。
body.en:
| Why the scene falls flat | First repair |
|---|---|
| Crying without a specific bond to miss | Return to established relationship and investment rather than inventing a perfect-memory flashback |
| Every reaction repeats sadness | Keep responses with different functions and merge restatement; tears are not the fault |
| Sudden death, illness, or betrayal added for force | Check whether the existing loss has actually been made clear |
| A smile or ordinary task declared complete recovery | Separate present action from the larger emotional arc |
| Restraint treated as automatically superior | Let control, open distress, or mixed feelings fit character and voice |
| A conclusion explains the entire theme | Leave an accurate action, line, thought, or image; keep commentary the author deliberately chose |

**Prompt:**

> Review this sad scene. List the established bond and investment, specific loss, character and reader knowledge, when the loss occurs, and the response. Identify vague or repetitive lines, then offer bounded edits. Add no death, illness, betrayal, past event, or opportunity absent from the original. Preserve the author’s voice and functional tears, silence, and direct thought. Flag missing setup for the author rather than inventing it. List changed lines and uncertainties. Text: [paste]

Compare the facts before adopting the edit, then read the adjoining scenes. Anticipation, immediate response, and later life need not feel alike. Let changes have causes instead of assigning fixed emotional stages.

This page shapes how sadness unfolds in a scene. For prose carriers, bodily responses, and direct statements, use [emotion on the page](/oh-story/emotion-on-the-page). For relationship rupture across a whole story, use [angst fiction](/oh-story/angst-fiction).

q.zh: 悲伤场景一定要有人死，或最后振作吗？
q.en: Does a sad scene require death or recovery?

a.zh: 不需要。告别、机会错过、关系结束或一个日常不能照旧，都能承载悲伤。哭与不哭、继续做事与暂时停住，按人物和作品来选；不要把一个当下动作当作悲伤已结束的证明。
a.en: No. A farewell, missed opportunity, ended relationship, or changed routine can carry sadness. Tears, restraint, work, and a pause depend on the character and work. One present action does not prove the feeling is over.

text.zh: 用 story-long-write 检查一个已有悲伤场景：提供前后文、不可改的事实和本书文风，只核对具体投入、失去时点与反应；先给修改建议，不扩写新的不幸。确认取舍后再改正文。
text.en: Use story-long-write on an existing sad scene with surrounding context, fixed facts, and the book’s voice. Ask for checks on specific investment, the timing of loss, and response, with suggestions first and no invented misfortunes. Adopt chosen edits afterward.

label.en: Emotional investment, changed meaning, and aftermath

label.en: Anticipated loss, scene response, and direct thought

title.zh: 横屏和竖屏视频怎么拼在一起：先定画幅，再保住画面里的信息
title.en: How to Combine Landscape and Portrait Videos

seo_title.zh: 横屏和竖屏视频怎么拼在一起：先定画幅，再保住画面里的信息
seo_title.en: How to Combine Landscape and Portrait Videos

description.zh: 多种画幅一起剪，先确认素材实际显示方向，再选择成片画幅和完整保留或裁切。附双人交接案例，检查人物、物件、字幕与接点。
description.en: Choose a canvas for mixed video orientations, distinguish fitting from cropping, and check people, objects, subtitles, and cuts with a worked example.

answer.zh: 横屏和竖屏视频拼在一起，先确认每份素材播放时的实际方向，再确定成片画幅。等比缩小并留边能保住全幅，但人物和文字可能太小；放大填满要裁掉边缘，须逐镜确认关键人物、物件和动作仍在。Video Recap 的多源剪切会统一画幅并等比留边，自动选出的中间画幅仍需核对是否符合你的成片目标。
answer.en: First confirm each source’s displayed orientation and choose the finished canvas. Fitting the whole image preserves its edges but may make people and text small; filling the canvas requires cropping, so check essential people, objects, and actions shot by shot. Video Recap’s multi-source cut normalizes geometry with proportional fitting and padding. Its automatically selected intermediate canvas still needs to be checked against your delivery goal.

heading.zh: 先确认实际方向，再定成片画幅
heading.en: Confirm Displayed Orientation Before Choosing the Canvas

body.zh:
先在播放器里打开各份素材，记下横屏、竖屏或方形，以及成片必须保住的内容。手机拍的视频可能靠旋转信息正确显示，编码宽高不能单独代表观众看到的方向。skill 的读取方法同时检查旋转和像素比例，用实际显示几何来统一素材；编辑判断仍要回到画面。

如果作者已经指定竖屏交付，先按这个要求检查每段能否装下。没有指定时，比较完整内容在哪种画幅更容易看懂：主体主要在中间，还是必须同时看见左右两人？不要因为文件列表的第一段是竖屏，就默认整片都适合竖屏。

这里的“画幅”是成片宽高比例，“留边”是为了保留完整源画面而出现的空白区域；它们与[多个视频讲同一条故事](/video-recap/multi-video-story-edit)的选段问题分开处理。
body.en:
Open each source in a player and note its displayed orientation and essential content. A phone recording may rely on rotation metadata to appear upright, so encoded width and height alone do not establish what viewers see. The skill reads rotation and pixel aspect information when deriving displayed geometry; the editorial decision still requires looking at the picture.

If the creator specifies portrait delivery, check whether each selected shot can fit that requirement. Otherwise compare which canvas makes the content easiest to read: is the subject central, or must both people at opposite sides remain visible? The orientation of the first file in a list should not decide the whole film.

“Canvas” here means the finished image’s width-to-height ratio. “Padding” is the space left around a fitted source to preserve its whole image. These decisions are separate from [selecting one story across several videos](/video-recap/multi-video-story-edit).

heading.zh: 留边和裁切分别牺牲什么
heading.en: Compare What Fitting and Cropping Lose

body.zh:
不要把源画面直接拉伸成另一比例。先比较两种取舍：

| 做法 | 检查 |
|---|---|
| 等比缩小、留边 | 源画面四边能保留，但横屏装进竖屏时，画面可能很小。检查脸、手部动作和源画面文字还能否辨认 |
| 放大填满、裁边 | 主体可以更大，但两侧或上下内容会消失。检查人物移动后是否出框，递物的手、反应者和结果是否被裁掉 |

同一成片可以逐镜采用不同取舍，前提是观众仍能理解位置和动作。源素材没有适合裁切的空间时，可以换一个已拍到的近景、保留全幅留边，或调整交付画幅。重新选镜头不能凭空补出未拍到的反应。

这张表是编辑比较表。当前 skill 的多源剪切使用等比缩放和留边，不会自动替你跟踪人物或选择叙事裁切。
body.en:
Do not stretch a source into a different aspect ratio. Compare two tradeoffs:

| Approach | Check |
|---|---|
| Fit proportionally with padding | Preserves the source edges, but a landscape shot inside a portrait canvas can become small. Check faces, hand actions, and text already in the image |
| Enlarge to fill and crop | Makes the subject larger but removes side or vertical content. Check whether movement leaves the frame and whether a receiving hand, reacting person, or visible outcome disappears |

A film can use different choices by shot if position and action remain understandable. When a source cannot support the crop, use an available close-up, retain the full image with padding, or reconsider the delivery canvas. Choosing another shot cannot supply a reaction that was never filmed.

This is an editorial comparison. The current skill’s multi-source cut uses proportional scaling and padding. It does not automatically track people or decide a narrative crop for you.

heading.zh: 原创示例：桌子两端的一次交接
heading.en: Worked Example: A Handoff Across a Table

body.zh:
以下是虚构剪辑练习，没有实际渲染。成片要求竖屏，已有三段素材：横屏双人镜头拍到陈禾在左、林夏在右，陈禾把带蓝绳的资料夹递到林夏手中；竖屏近景拍到林夏收到后检查封面；另一段横屏拍到她把资料夹放入桌边箱子。故事要交代“实际收到并放好”，不只展示一个漂亮封面。

| 片段 | 这一版的取舍 |
|---|---|
| 双人交接 | 先比较竖屏居中裁切：若任一人的手或接到资料夹的瞬间出框，就保留完整横屏并留边。全幅仍太小、无法看懂交接时，回到已有素材找可见接收结果；没有便调整成片要求，不用封面近景冒充交接 |
| 检查封面 | 使用竖屏近景，让封面成为此刻焦点；它交代拿到什么，不重复证明上一镜如何交接，也不让字幕盖住要辨认的内容 |
| 放进箱子 | 检查资料夹离手、进入箱子的完整范围。只截到她开始伸手不能当“已经收好”；若填满裁切会丢掉箱子，则保留全幅或换已有有效角度 |

留边让第一镜人物较小，近景让第二镜人物较大，这是两种不同景别的选择。要判断的是接点能否顺着同一物件与动作看懂，不要求每个人始终占屏幕同样高度。若成片无法在手机上读清封面，缩小文案承诺或换清楚素材，不靠放大模糊细节宣称已经可读。
body.en:
This is a fictional editing exercise; nothing has been rendered. The required delivery is portrait. Three clips exist: a landscape two-shot with Chen He on the left and Lin Xia on the right, showing Chen handing a blue-cord folder into Lin’s hands; a portrait close-up of Lin checking its cover after receiving it; and another landscape shot of Lin placing it in a box beside the table. The story must show actual receipt and storage, beyond an attractive cover.

| Clip | Decision for this version |
|---|---|
| Two-person handoff | Compare a centered portrait crop. If either hand or the receipt disappears, retain the whole landscape image with padding. If the fitted image is too small to understand, look for an existing shot showing the receipt. If none exists, reconsider delivery requirements; a cover close-up cannot stand in for the handoff |
| Cover check | Use the portrait close-up to focus on the cover. It shows what was received, rather than proving how the previous handoff happened. Keep subtitles away from content viewers need to identify |
| Placement in the box | Keep the full interval from the folder leaving her hand to entering the box. Starting a reach does not prove storage. If filling the canvas removes the box, fit the whole image or choose an existing valid angle |

Padding makes the people smaller in the first shot; the close-up makes Lin larger in the second. These are framing choices. Check whether viewers can follow the same object and action across the cut, without requiring every person to occupy a fixed screen height. If the cover remains unreadable on a phone, narrow the script’s claim or choose clearer material rather than treating enlarged blur as readable evidence.

heading.zh: skill 自动统一了什么，还要确认什么
heading.en: Understand the Skill’s Automatic Canvas Choice

body.zh:
所引版本的多源剪切会检查实际用到的来源，按选段时长比较横屏、竖屏和方形；主方向内再选显示面积较大的来源作为画幅，帧率也按用到的时长归类选择。它不是固定采用列表第一份，也不是自动按某个平台决定竖屏。

随后，各段等比缩放到同一画布内并留边，统一像素比例、帧率与像素格式，再拼接。统一参数解决素材能否拼起来的问题，不证明人物、道具和文字已经看清。

剪切产生的是 `edited_source.mp4` 中间文件，旁白、字幕和最终包装在后续阶段处理。若自动画幅与作者指定的交付不同，先指出差异、确认后续能否得到可读构图；不要声称 `/video-recap` 已有某个未列出的自动裁切或锁定画幅参数。
body.en:
In the cited version, multi-source cutting checks sources actually used in the selected clips. Used duration determines the leading landscape, portrait, or square orientation; within that orientation it selects a source with a larger displayed area. Frame-rate buckets are also weighted by used duration. It does not simply take the first listed file or choose portrait for a platform automatically.

Each segment is then scaled proportionally into one canvas with padding, and pixel aspect, frame rate, and pixel format are normalized before concatenation. Compatible parameters make the segments joinable; they do not establish that people, props, or text are legible.

The cut produces the intermediate `edited_source.mp4`. Narration, subtitles, and final packaging follow later. If its automatic canvas differs from the creator’s required delivery, identify that difference and check whether later framing can remain readable. Do not assume `/video-recap` exposes an undocumented automatic crop or canvas-lock option.

heading.zh: 最后用手机尺寸看完整段落
heading.en: Review the Sequence at Phone Size

body.zh:
在实际交付尺寸下正常速度看一遍，先查人物和物件有没有被拉宽、旋转错误或裁掉，再查跨镜动作、源画面文字和字幕。保留完整源画面并不意味着它已经足够大；裁切后填满也不意味着证据仍完整。

检查每个接点前后：画幅改变是否分散注意，关键动作是否重复或漏掉，突然放大有没有改变观众对人物位置的理解。字幕加入后再看一次，尤其是留边较多的段落，不能让字幕或 Logo 挡住刚好留下的接收动作。字幕自身的排版见[断句与样帧检查](/video-recap/subtitle-layout-and-line-breaks)。

把返修写具体：“第一镜保留两人的手和资料夹进入林夏手中的结果；第三镜不能裁掉箱子。”这比“全部改得更饱满”更容易执行和核对。
body.en:
Watch the actual delivery at phone size and normal speed. First check for stretched people or objects, incorrect rotation, and missing content. Then check action across cuts, text in the source, and subtitles. A complete fitted source may still be too small; a filled canvas may still have lost essential evidence.

Replay each cut: does a framing change distract, repeat or omit an action, or alter the understood positions? Review again after adding subtitles, especially padded segments. Subtitles and logos must not obscure the receiving action you preserved. See [subtitle line breaks and frame review](/video-recap/subtitle-layout-and-line-breaks) for subtitle layout.

Write a concrete revision: “In shot one, retain both hands and the folder entering Lin’s hands; in shot three, keep the box visible.” This is easier to implement and check than “make every shot fuller.”

q.zh: 横屏转竖屏一定要裁切吗？
q.en: Must landscape footage be cropped for a portrait video?

a.zh: 不一定。等比留边可以保留完整画面，裁切可以让主体更大，但会丢掉边缘。根据每镜必须看见的人物、物件和动作选择，再用手机尺寸验证；没有合适素材时可以调整选段或交付画幅。
a.en: No. Proportional fitting preserves the whole image, while cropping can enlarge the subject but loses edges. Choose by the people, objects, and actions each shot must show, then review at phone size. When suitable material is unavailable, change the selection or reconsider the delivery canvas.

text.zh: 在已安装 Video Recap Skills 的宿主中调用 `/video-recap`，提供你有权使用的横屏和竖屏素材，说明成片要求的画幅，以及必须完整看见的人物、物件和动作。先检查实际显示方向，逐段比较等比留边和裁切后的可读性，并说明当前多源剪切自动选画幅的结果；不要把未执行的构图或渲染称作已验证成片。
text.en: In a host with Video Recap Skills installed, invoke `/video-recap` with landscape and portrait sources you may use. Specify the required delivery canvas and people, props, and actions that must remain visible. First check displayed orientation and compare fitted versus cropped readability by clip, including the current multi-source cut’s automatic canvas choice. Report proposed framing and actual rendered checks separately.

label.zh: 多源剪切职责与中间文件
显示方向与自动画幅选择
等比缩放、留边与拼接
动作证据与真实观看

title.zh: 小说封面书名被裁掉怎么办：检查原图、上传版和最终预览
title.en: How to Fix a Book Cover Title That Gets Cropped

seo_title.zh: 小说封面书名被裁掉怎么办：检查原图、上传版和最终预览
seo_title.en: How to Fix a Book Cover Title That Gets Cropped

description.zh: 封面出图完整，上传后书名或笔名却少了一截？先找裁剪发生在哪一步，再调整画幅、文字位置和上传版，保留原图并检查缩略预览。
description.en: Locate cropped cover lettering in the original, upload file, and preview. Adjust the canvas or text, preserve the original, and check thumbnail readability.

answer.zh: 小说封面书名被裁掉，先分别检查生成原图、导出的上传版和实际上传预览，找出损失发生在哪一步。输出尺寸与上传要求比例不一致时，居中填满裁剪可能去掉上下或两侧；提示词写了安全区也不保证成图遵守。保留原图，按已确认要求调整画幅或移动文字，另存上传版，再逐字和缩略检查。
answer.en: Compare the generated original, exported upload version, and actual upload preview to locate the loss. When aspect ratios differ, filling and center-cropping can remove the top, bottom, or sides. A safe-area instruction does not guarantee the image follows it. Preserve the original, adjust the canvas or lettering to confirmed requirements, save a separate upload version, and check both exact text and thumbnail readability.

heading.zh: 先找出是哪一步裁掉文字
heading.en: Locate the Step That Removes the Text

body.zh:
把三份画面并排看：原图、准备上传的文件、实际发布界面预览。先辨认问题是文字本身写错、字号太小，还是完整字符被边缘截断。错字要修字，裁剪要修版式；不必为裁剪重写故事题材。

| 位置 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| 原图已经缺字 | 调整文字区、构图或准确字样后重做该版本；无字底图另行排字也是作者可选方案 |
| 原图完整，上传版缺字 | 检查导出是否填满并裁边，确认目标宽高和文字实际位置 |
| 上传文件完整，界面预览缺字 | 核对实际上传要求与当前预览框；调整给这一用途的版本，再看真实预览，不能只根据原图判断 |

目标宽高以作者确认的交付规格或发布时的官方要求为准。不同用途可能要不同版本；没有确认尺寸时，不把 skill 里的默认出图比例当所有平台的上传标准。
body.en:
Compare three images: the original, the file prepared for upload, and the actual publishing preview. Distinguish incorrect lettering, type too small to read, and complete characters cut off at an edge. Fix spelling as spelling and crop loss as layout; there is no need to change the book’s genre for a crop problem.

| Location | Response |
|---|---|
| Text is incomplete in the original | Revise the lettering area, composition, or exact text for another version. A text-free background with separate lettering is also an author-selected option |
| Original is complete; exported file is cropped | Check whether export filled the canvas and cropped its edges, along with target dimensions and actual text positions |
| Upload file is complete; interface preview is cropped | Check the confirmed upload requirement and current preview frame. Revise the version for that use and inspect the real preview rather than relying on the original |

Use the creator’s confirmed delivery dimensions or official requirements at publication time. Different uses may need different versions. An unconfirmed target cannot be replaced with the skill’s default image ratio as a universal platform standard.

heading.zh: 为什么提示词留了安全区还会被裁
heading.en: Why a Safe-Area Prompt Can Still Fail

body.zh:
`story-cover` 会把比例和文字安全区写进提示词；在需要固定上传像素时，还会导出居中裁剪、缩放的上传版。生成工具实际返回的尺寸可能不同，文字也可能没有留在要求的位置。因此“已写安全区”和“最终未被裁”是两项不同事实。

居中填满保持比例，代价是裁去超过目标画布的边缘；直接拉伸虽能装进尺寸，却会让人物与字形变形。不能只看文件宽高已经正确，就认定封面合格。

先在原图上看出目标比例会留下的范围。书名、笔名和关键主体都应落在实际保留范围内，并有可读的留白。skill 的中心安全区是起点，最终仍检查实际字符位置；不把某个百分比承诺为所有尺寸都安全。
body.en:
`story-cover` requests an aspect ratio and safe lettering area in its prompt. When fixed upload pixels are needed, it also exports a resized, center-cropped upload version. Returned dimensions may differ, and lettering may not occupy the requested area. Requesting a safe area and preserving the final text are two different facts.

Filling proportionally preserves shape but crops content extending beyond the target canvas. Direct stretching can meet dimensions while distorting people and letterforms. Correct file dimensions alone do not establish a usable cover.

Inspect the region the target ratio will actually retain. Keep the title, byline, and essential subject inside it with readable space. The skill’s central safe-area instruction is a starting point; verify actual character positions rather than treating one percentage as safe for every target.

heading.zh: 原创尺寸练习：完整原图不等于完整上传版
heading.en: Worked Size Example: A Complete Original Can Produce a Cropped Export

body.zh:
以下是纸面尺寸练习，没有生成图片或实际上传。练习要求上传文件为 600×800，原图为 1200×1800；这组数字是本例给定规格，不代表某平台当前要求。

如果等比填满目标，原图会先缩到 600×900，再居中去掉顶部和底部各 50 像素。原图中靠近上沿的标题与靠近下沿的笔名，就可能落在被去掉的部分；写进提示词的预留要求不能代替对实际位置的检查。

| 候选修法 | 取舍与检查 |
|---|---|
| 保留已有图，重新排字 | 有无字底图或可单独编辑的文字层时，把完整书名与笔名移入最终保留范围；检查原文字是否仍残留。只有扁平图片时，不能声称文字层可直接移动 |
| 重做构图与画幅 | 明确给定 3:4 目标，保留故事主体，把标题和笔名安排在真实可读区域；新图仍须核对尺寸与每个字 |
| 另做带留边的版式 | 作者接受留边且目标用途允许时，等比缩小保全图，再统一背景与文字；这是一种主动的排版选择，当前 skill 的居中填满导出不会自动采用它 |

确定一版后另存上传文件，不覆盖原图。在该版实际 600×800 文件上检查书名、笔名和主体，再缩到真实使用的缩略大小；缩略时至少应能认出书名与核心画面，笔名保留完整且符合交付需求。任何版本仍缺字，就回到发生损失的那一步。
body.en:
This is a paper geometry exercise, with no generated image or real upload. The exercise requires a 600×800 upload file from a 1200×1800 original. These are given dimensions, not a claim about a platform’s current requirements.

Proportional filling first scales the original to 600×900, then center-crops 50 pixels from both top and bottom. A title near the original top or byline near the bottom can fall in those removed areas. Requested margins cannot substitute for checking actual positions.

| Candidate fix | Tradeoff and check |
|---|---|
| Keep the art and lay out lettering again | With a text-free background or separately editable type, move exact title and byline inside the retained region. Check for leftover old lettering. A flattened image does not provide movable type layers automatically |
| Revise composition and canvas | Specify the given 3:4 target, preserve the story’s main subject, and place lettering in an actually readable area. Check dimensions and every character again |
| Make a padded layout | If the creator accepts padding and the intended use allows it, fit the whole picture and unify background and type. This is a deliberate layout alternative; the current skill’s center-fill export does not adopt it automatically |

Save a separate upload file without overwriting the original. Inspect title, byline, and subject in the actual 600×800 version, then at the intended thumbnail size. The thumbnail should identify the title and main image; the byline must remain complete and meet the delivery need. If text is still missing, return to the step that removed it.

heading.zh: 保留原图，另存上传版再检查
heading.en: Preserve the Original and Check a Separate Upload Version

body.zh:
明确哪张是生成原图、哪张是为某个尺寸导出的版本，保留对应提示词和修改说明。skill 会保存版本并在导出时另存上传版；原图里文字完整，不能代替导出后的复查。

检查顺序可以是：准确书名和笔名 → 文件宽高与比例 → 四边是否截字 → 主体与文字是否互挡 → 缩略图辨识 → 实际上传预览。预览改变后，检查你正在使用的这一版，避免只拿旧截图作证。

如果还没生成或上传，交付应说明这是拟定版式或导出方案。只有看过实际文件和当前预览，才能报告文字完整。
body.en:
Identify the generated original and each size-specific export, preserving its prompt and revision notes. The skill saves numbered versions and a separate upload export. Intact text in the original does not replace checking the export.

A useful sequence is exact title and byline, dimensions and ratio, cropped edges, subject–text overlap, thumbnail recognition, and the actual upload preview. When the preview changes, inspect the version now in use instead of relying on an old screenshot.

Before generation or upload, describe the layout or export as proposed. Report complete lettering only after inspecting the actual file and current preview.

q.zh: 小说封面尺寸正确，就不会裁字了吗？
q.en: Does a correctly sized cover guarantee the title will not be cropped?

a.zh: 不保证。文件可以达到正确宽高，同时已经在导出时裁掉字；实际预览也可能使用不同显示框。分别看原图、上传文件和预览，核对完整字样、画幅与真实留白。
a.en: No. An export can have the correct dimensions after already cropping lettering, and a preview can use a different frame. Check the original, upload file, and preview separately for exact text, ratio, and actual margins.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 `/story-cover`（Codex 中用 `$story-cover`），提供准确书名、笔名、目标用途、已确认的上传规格、输出目录，以及原图或参考图。说明哪一步出现裁字，要求保留原图并另存修订/上传版；按实际保留范围安排文字，完成后逐字、缩略并在实际上传预览中核对。若暂未上传，先报告文件检查结果和仍待预览的部分。
text.en: Use `/story-cover` in Claude Code or `$story-cover` in Codex with the exact title, byline, intended use, confirmed upload dimensions, output directory, and original or reference image. Identify where cropping occurs and preserve the original while saving a revised/upload version. Place lettering within the retained area, then check exact text, thumbnail appearance, and the actual upload preview. Before upload, report file checks separately from preview checks still pending.

label.zh: 封面安全区、上传导出与质量检查
label.en: Safe area, upload export, and quality review

label.zh: 文字与视觉风格

title.en: How to Write a Scary Scene That Builds Dread
title.zh: 恐怖场景怎么写有压迫感：先限制选择，再兑现威胁

seo_title.en: Write a Scary Scene
seo_title.zh: 恐怖场景怎么写

description.zh: 用熟悉的声音、可观察的异常和人物选择写恐怖场景。含旧影院原创片段、信息投放表与修改提示词，不靠形容词和跳吓堆恐惧。
description.en: Build dread through a familiar detail, an observable anomaly, and a character’s choice, with a cinema scene and a revision worksheet.

answer.zh: 先让读者知道人物想保住什么，再选一项熟悉细节发生偏差。按“发现异常—尝试解释—获得新回应—改变选择”安排场景，让人物能离开、求助或试探，而每种做法都有作品已经建立的条件。限定视角只写当时能感知的事；恐惧的兑现可以是被观察、界限被侵入或一次真实受阻，不必死亡，也不必把所有谜底说完。
answer.en: Establish what the character cares about, then disturb a familiar detail. Arrange an anomaly, a plausible explanation, a new response, and a changed choice. Preserve available exits and help instead of making the character foolish. Write within the chosen viewpoint; dread can land through unwanted observation or an invaded boundary without death or a complete explanation.

heading.zh: 先定这一场怕什么，而不是先堆阴森词
heading.en: Choose the Fear Before Adding Ominous Language

body.zh:
“黑暗、冰冷、诡异”只能告诉读者应该害怕，还没有给他们一件值得担心的事。先写一句具体恐惧：熟悉的人像在关心我，却知道不该知道的事；我能走，但要放弃刚拿到的东西；我以为回到人群就安全，异常却跟到了这里。选择适合这场戏的一项，不必全部出现。

 Oh Story 的情绪方法先连接投入、异常触发、人物应对和意义变化。本文把它用在原创旧影院场景：周珂来取父亲留下的工作本，想带走最后一份私人记录；父亲已经去世。她熟悉录音里的声音，却不接受“听着像”就等于父亲真的在场。温暖的旧声音开始回应她此刻的动作，私人纪念变成被窥视的压力。

人物有继续确认的理由，不代表必须冒险到底。楼梯仍通，管理员在一楼等她，离开一直是可行选择。这里限制的是能相信的解释与愿意付出的时间，不是临时把全部门锁死。
body.en:
“Dark,” “cold,” and “eerie” announce an emotion without supplying something to fear. State a specific concern: a familiar voice knows something it should not; leaving means abandoning an object; an anomaly reaches a place thought safe. Choose what belongs to the scene rather than using all three.

Oh Story’s emotion method connects investment, a trigger, a response, and changed meaning. In the original cinema example, Zhou Ke wants her late father’s work notebook, the last private record she can retrieve. She recognizes his recorded voice without treating resemblance as proof of his presence. When the familiar voice responds to her current movement, a keepsake becomes a source of unwanted observation.

A reason to investigate does not require staying indefinitely. The stairs remain accessible, and the caretaker waits downstairs. What narrows is the set of explanations she trusts and the time she is willing to spend, rather than every door becoming locked without setup.

heading.zh: 用正常基准和一次试探，让异常逐渐成立
heading.en: Establish a Baseline and Let a Test Change It

body.zh:
先给正常基准，读者才知道什么发生了偏差。基准可以是熟悉的房间、一次普通流程、物件惯常的位置或人物记得的一句录音。必要的基准用两三句交代即可，数量按故事需要，不是配额。

| 场景材料 | 本例安排 |
|---|---|
| 正常基准 | 父亲的工作本放在旧影院放映室桌上；一台录音机里有他的旧录音。周珂获准取本子，管理员在楼下等。 |
| 第一个异常 | 按停录音机后，父亲般的声音又从走廊传来。她只排除了眼前这台继续播放，没有排除其他声源。 |
| 应对 | 她故意说钥匙在右手，实际仍握在左手，试探这是否只是旧录音。 |
| 新回应 | 声音说“还在左手”。她把本子暂放回桌，换手后拿回本子，声音又说“这回是右手”。 |
| 选择与落点 | 她取到本子，拒绝声音的关灯要求，沿仍可通行的楼梯离开这一层。来源与身份尚未揭示，实时回应已经改变她对声音的理解。 |

这些是本文选定的剧情，不是普遍的超自然规则。试探可以让解释变得更困难，不必一次证明全部真相；停止一台设备也不能证明整栋楼没有别的设备。
body.en:
Give readers a normal baseline so they can notice a deviation: a familiar room, ordinary procedure, object position, or remembered recording. Establish only what the scene needs rather than enforcing a fixed number of sentences.

| Material | Example choice |
|---|---|
| Baseline | The father’s notebook lies on the projection-room desk; a recorder contains his old voice. Zhou has permission to collect the notebook, and the caretaker waits downstairs. |
| First anomaly | After she stops the recorder, a father-like voice comes from the corridor. This excludes continued playback by that device, not every possible sound source. |
| Response | She deliberately says the keys are in her right hand while holding them in her left, testing whether the voice is merely an old recording. |
| New reply | It says “Still in your left.” She sets the notebook down, moves the keys, and retrieves the notebook; the voice says “Now the right.” |
| Choice and landing | She obtains the notebook, refuses the request to switch off the light, and leaves the floor by the accessible stairs. Source and identity remain unresolved, but the current replies change how she understands the voice. |

These are the article’s story choices rather than universal supernatural rules. A test can make an explanation harder without establishing the entire truth; stopping one machine does not eliminate other equipment in the building.

heading.zh: 区分听见的事实、人物解释和暂不揭示的答案
heading.en: Separate Observation, Interpretation, and the Withheld Answer

body.zh:
有限视角的恐怖，不是把人物已经知道的事硬藏起来。读者可以跟周珂同时听见声音，也可以在另一视角先看见一个异常；先选叙述方式，再维持它。

| 信息 | 本例写法 |
|---|---|
| 当时能确认 | 录音机已停止；走廊传来声音；两次回答对应她此刻的持钥匙手。 |
| 人物的判断 | 她听着像父亲，也想到其他录音或有人在观察。这些是解释，不是叙述者替她确认的身份。 |
| 仍未知 | 声源位置、是否有人、如何回应、关灯要求的目的。留白不抹掉已经写出的回应。 |
| 后续需要承接 | 她拿走工作本，录音机留在桌上，钥匙最后在右手，灯未关；不在下一场把物件和知情重置。 |

不要先写“她完全没注意桌下的人”，又让限知叙述把那人的动作讲完。若想让读者先知道，可以明确切换视角；若跟人物一起发现，就让她通过声音、物件或可见痕迹取得信息。

本篇处理一场戏的恐惧，不代替[悬疑小说线索设计](/oh-story/mystery-novel)或[规则怪谈](/oh-story/rules-horror)的全书方法。
body.en:
Limited viewpoint does not mean hiding facts the character already knows. Readers can hear the voice with Zhou or encounter an anomaly first in another viewpoint. Choose the narration and maintain it.

| Information | Example treatment |
|---|---|
| Observable now | The recorder has stopped; a voice comes from the corridor; two replies match the hand currently holding the keys. |
| Interpretation | She recognizes a father-like sound and considers another recording or an observer. These are explanations rather than narrator-confirmed identity. |
| Unknown | Source location, presence of a person, means of responding, and purpose of the light request. Openness does not erase the replies already shown. |
| Later inheritance | She takes the notebook; the recorder stays on the desk; the keys end in her right hand; the light remains on. Later prose must inherit those states. |

Do not say she failed to notice someone under the desk and then describe that person’s movements through her limited viewpoint. To give readers advance knowledge, switch viewpoint clearly; to discover with her, let sound, objects, or visible traces supply the information.

This page handles fear within a scene. Use the separate [mystery guide](/oh-story/mystery-novel) for a book’s clue structure or [rules-horror guide](/oh-story/rules-horror) for rule conflicts.

heading.zh: 原创片段：旧录音开始回答眼前的动作
heading.en: Original Scene: A Recorded Voice Responds to the Present

body.zh:
前置事实采用上表；以下是本文原创片段。周珂此时左手握钥匙，右手空着，电话刚结束，手机已放回衣袋。

> 管理员在电话里说，他就在一楼门口，等她拿完本子一起锁门。周珂推开放映室，桌上的工作本还是父亲惯用的蓝封皮。录音机里，他正说着“周珂，该回家了”，后面接一声短咳。她按下停止键，转轴停住。
>
> 她拿起工作本，走廊又响起那声咳嗽。
>
> “钥匙在右手。”她说，左手仍攥着钥匙。
>
> “还在左手。”声音说。父亲已经去世两年，她知道这件事，比知道那声咳嗽更清楚。
>
> 她把本子放回桌上，将钥匙移到右手，再用左手拿起本子。
>
> “这回是右手。关灯再下来。”
>
> 楼梯口的灯还亮着。她没有去碰放映室的开关，带着本子走出房间，直到踩上第一阶楼梯，才回头看那扇开着的门。

前半句熟悉的催归是旧录音；后来的换手回应把亲情细节变成当下压力。她的停机、试探、换手和离开让场景有具体变化，最后没有为了惊吓自动照做。

这个片段没有证明声音就是父亲，也没有宣告她已到楼下或已经安全。它完成取本子与离开放映室，留下新的问题：谁在回应，为什么要求关灯？长篇后续要沿本次状态接写，不能只重复同一句异常来拖延。
body.en:
The scene uses the setup above. Zhou holds the keys in her left hand; her right is free. The call has ended, and her phone is in her coat pocket.

> The caretaker said he was waiting at the ground-floor entrance to lock up with her. Zhou entered the projection room. Her father’s notebook still had its familiar blue cover. From the recorder came his “Zhou Ke, time to go home,” followed by a short cough. She pressed stop. The spindles stopped turning.
>
> She picked up the notebook. The cough came again from the corridor.
>
> “The keys are in my right hand,” she said, still gripping them in her left.
>
> “Still in your left,” the voice said. Her father had been dead for two years. She knew that more certainly than she knew the cough.
>
> She set the notebook on the desk, transferred the keys to her right hand, and picked up the notebook with her left.
>
> “Now the right. Turn off the light before you come down.”
>
> The stair light was on. She left the projection-room switch alone and carried the notebook out. Only when she stepped onto the first stair did she look back at the open door.

The familiar call home begins as a recording; the later replies about her hands turn a family detail into present pressure. Stopping, testing, transferring, and leaving give the scene concrete changes without making her obey merely to obtain a scare.

This excerpt does not identify the voice as her father or claim that she has reached downstairs safely. It completes retrieval and departure from the room, leaving a new question about the observer and the light request. Continue from those states instead of repeating the same anomaly indefinitely.

heading.zh: 恐怖场景不吓人，先查哪处失效
heading.en: Diagnose a Scary Scene That Feels Flat

body.zh:
| 常见问题 | 修改方向 |
|---|---|
| 只有阴森形容词 | 留一项人物熟悉的细节，写它具体怎样偏离正常。 |
| 主角明明能走却无理由留下 | 补已经属于这个人的目标，或让他真的离开；不要临时毁掉电话和所有出口。 |
| 每次新声响都靠回头拖延 | 安排一次解释、试探或应对，再给有区别的新回应；需要停留时让氛围本身有体验。 |
| 人物停掉设备后旁白直接宣布鬼来了 | 只写排除的范围，把人物的推测留作推测。 |
| 反应全是心跳、冷汗、攥拳 | 优先写因此改变的选择、台词或操作；准确的感受与身体后果仍可保留。 |
| 最后讲完整怪物设定 | 先回答这场已提出、读者需要理解的一项问题；全局机制按作品节奏揭示。 |

惊吓和持续不安都能使用。突发声响可以打断一段等待，安静也可以承载压力；不要要求每段都升级、每次试探都受伤或每章都出现新规则。数量和声音强弱都不自动证明效果，改后读一遍人物为何留下、为何改变办法、最后发生了什么。
body.en:
| Problem | Revision |
|---|---|
| Ominous adjectives only | Choose a familiar detail and show the specific deviation. |
| The character could leave but stays without reason | Supply a goal belonging to them or let them leave; do not suddenly disable every exit and phone. |
| Every sound produces another delaying glance | Let an explanation, test, or response produce a different reply; atmospheric pauses can also offer an experience. |
| Stopping equipment leads to a narrator announcing a ghost | State what was excluded and leave inference as inference. |
| Reactions are only heartbeat, sweat, and fists | Prefer changed choices, speech, or operations; retain accurate feelings and consequential physical reactions. |
| The ending explains the entire monster system | Answer a local question readers need; reveal the wider mechanism at the story’s chosen pace. |

Use sudden scares or sustained unease as appropriate. A sound can interrupt waiting, and silence can carry pressure. Neither every paragraph escalating, every test injuring someone, nor a new rule every chapter is required. Reread why the character stays, changes approach, and reaches this outcome rather than counting effects.

heading.zh: 可复制的场景工作表与修改提示词
heading.en: A Scene Worksheet and Revision Prompt

body.zh:
先用两列表填：人物想保住什么、正常基准、第一次偏差、当前能取得的解释、试探或离开、实际新回应、选择变化、仍未知的答案。不适用的项省略；这只是作者工作表，不是原生卷纲、细纲或检测结果。

> 只整理或修改〔指定恐怖场景〕。列出已写事实、视角当时可感知的信息、正常基准与第一次偏差，说明人物继续、求助或离开的理由。先给异常、解释、应对和新回应的安排，再由我选定；只修改我批准的范围。保留既定物件、出口和后文知识边界，不为惊吓自动增加伤亡、封死所有路线或补全怪物身份。已发生结果和人物推测分别标明，不要求每段加身体反应。

在 Oh Story 项目里，把已选安排交给对应规划或章节流程；它仍需要实际书稿和设定。提示词不会让未提供的事实自动变成已知，检查通过也不保证所有读者都会害怕。
body.en:
Fill a two-column worksheet with the valued object or goal, normal baseline, first deviation, available explanation, test or departure, actual new reply, changed choice, and remaining unknown. Omit inapplicable fields. This is an editorial worksheet, not a native outline or a detector result.

> Plan or revise only [the specified scary scene]. Identify established facts, information available to the viewpoint, the normal baseline, and first deviation. Explain reasons to continue, seek help, or leave. Propose an anomaly, explanation, response, and new reply for my selection; change only the approved scope. Preserve objects, exits, and later knowledge boundaries. Do not automatically add casualties, close every route, or supply the monster’s identity for a scare. Separate outcomes from interpretation, without bodily reactions in every paragraph.

In an Oh Story project, give the selected plan to the corresponding planning or chapter workflow with the actual manuscript and setting. A prompt cannot supply unseen facts, and passing a check does not guarantee every reader will be frightened.

q.zh: 恐怖场景一定要写怪物或者死人吗？
q.en: Does a scary scene require a monster or death?

a.zh: 不一定。被观察、熟悉的人反常回应、正常流程不再可靠，都能形成不安。先确定人物投入、可观察偏差和应对后的变化；若作品需要怪物或死亡，让它遵循已建立的条件，不把它当自动加分项。
a.en: No. Unwanted observation, an altered familiar response, or an unreliable routine can produce unease. Establish investment, an observable deviation, and what changes after a response. If the story uses a monster or death, give it established conditions rather than treating it as an automatic improvement.

text.zh: 可以请 story-long-write 先只讨论这场戏：给已写事实、视角、想保住的东西与可用出口，规划异常、试探及实际回应，不写后续章节；选定后再进入相应章节写作。
text.en: Ask story-long-write to discuss this scene first from the manuscript’s facts, viewpoint, valued goal, and available exits. Plan the anomaly, test, and reply without continuing into later chapters; use the chapter workflow after selection.

label.zh: 投入、触发与意义变化
有限视角与可观察异常
悬念信息顺序
选择、物件与可选身体反应
label.en: Choices, objects, and optional physical reactions

title.zh: 小说章节名怎么起：突出本章重点，别提前揭晓
title.en: How to Name Novel Chapters Without Spoiling the Reveal

seo_title.zh: 小说章节名怎么起：突出本章重点，别提前揭晓
seo_title.en: How to Name Novel Chapters Without Spoiling the Reveal

description.zh: 从章节实际内容选章名，用重点动作、关键台词或意象形成期待。含修车店标题对照、剧透检查与文件同步方法。
description.en: Choose chapter titles from actual actions, lines, or motifs. Compare workshop examples, check spoilers and repeats, and preserve manuscript naming.

answer.zh: 先用一句话说清这一章让读者经历什么，再从关键动作、台词、矛盾或意象中提炼标题。检查正文是否兑现它、是否提前说破本章要保留的答案，以及与邻章是否重复。章名可以简洁平实，也可以带悬念；不要为起名补剧情，选定后按项目原格式同步标题与文件名。
answer.en: State what readers experience in the chapter, then extract a title from its action, line, conflict, or motif. Check delivery, spoilers, and repetition with nearby titles. Plain or suspenseful names can both work. Do not invent plot to justify a title; preserve the manuscript’s naming format when applying the choice.

heading.zh: 书名介绍整部作品，章名服务眼前这一章
heading.en: A Book Title Introduces the Work; a Chapter Title Serves This Chapter

body.zh:
[网文书名](/oh-story/novel-titles)需要表达整部作品的卖点；章名只需给本章一个准确的入口。给每章都写“全城震惊”“惊天秘密”，容易让不同内容变成同一承诺；安静的相处、整理线索或一次小选择也值得有自己的名字。

Oh Story 的章节名策略从本章有辨识度的台词、冲突信息取标题；章级钩子方法再按情绪和章节功能选择牵引。本文把两者用于作者选章名，不把项目里偏爽文的强标题建议当成所有文学风格的硬规则。全书统一用数字、地点或人物名也可以，只要作者已经选择这种形式。

先确认本书的习惯：是否每章都起名，标题偏叙事、意象还是直白信息，编号怎样写。不因 AI 能给二十个候选就改变全书格式。
body.en:
A [novel title](/oh-story/novel-titles) presents the whole work’s attraction. A chapter title supplies an accurate entrance to this chapter. Repeated promises of shocking secrets can flatten different chapters; quiet companionship, organizing clues, and a small decision can each have an appropriate name.

Oh Story’s naming strategy draws on a distinctive line or conflict in the chapter. Its hook method considers emotion and chapter function. This article applies those methods to title selection without making forceful web-serial titles mandatory for every literary style. Numbers, places, or character names can also work when the author chooses that form consistently.

Check whether the book names chapters, what style it uses, and how numbering works. Twenty AI suggestions are not a reason to change the whole manuscript’s format.

heading.zh: 从已写内容提炼，不从空泛词库拼标题
heading.en: Extract Material From the Chapter

body.zh:
先写一句本章作用，再圈能承担它的材料：

| 取材方向 | 怎样使用 |
|---|---|
| 关键动作 | 用本章真正发生的选择或阻力；“先检查”比只写“困难”更具体。 |
| 台词 | 选择有辨识度且确实出现的话，必要时缩短；改写后仍准确，不冒充逐字引用。 |
| 冲突信息 | 点出两种要求碰撞的地方，保留读者想看的解决过程。 |
| 意象或物件 | 用正文已经让读者理解的物件，不临时加一把刀来配标题。 |
| 时间、地点或人物 | 可以清楚定位；本书若惯用这类平实标题，保持一致。 |

这张表是作者取材卡，不是 skill 原生字段。无需每章用不同一类，也不把标题控制在统一字数；先看目录是否容易辨认，再看它与正文是否对应。一个好标题不负责替平淡章节编出高潮。
body.en:
Write one sentence describing the chapter’s function, then identify material that carries it:

| Material | Use |
|---|---|
| Key action | Name an actual choice or obstacle; “Check First” is more specific than “Difficulty.” |
| A line | Select recognizable speech that appears in the text. A shortened paraphrase must stay accurate without posing as an exact quote. |
| Conflict | Point to competing demands while leaving their resolution worth reading. |
| Motif or object | Use something already meaningful in the prose, rather than adding a knife to justify the name. |
| Time, place, or person | Orient readers clearly; keep this straightforward form if it is the book’s established style. |

This is an editorial selection card, not a native skill format. Neither rotating categories every chapter nor enforcing one title length is required. Check distinguishability in the contents and correspondence with the prose. A title cannot invent a climax for a quiet chapter.

heading.zh: 原创对照：同一章可以有不同准确入口
heading.en: Original Comparison: Different Accurate Entrances to One Chapter

body.zh:
沿用本文原创修车店章节安排：阿民想先取三辆车；罗宁要求基础检查，第二辆出现问题；罗宁复查首辆与第三辆并完成已要求的试车后，阿民接受先交这两辆。章尾准备离开时，他接到比赛地点变更电话。钥匙只是交付的物件，不是隐藏宝物。本表比较作者候选，没有实际重命名书稿。

| 候选 | 取舍 |
|---|---|
| 修车 | 准确但较宽；若全书用平实事务名，可以保留。想突出本章的交付矛盾时再具体化。 |
| 先检查，再拿钥匙 | 指向本章反复协商的条件，正文有兑现；不提前透露地点电话。 |
| 两辆，还是三辆？ | 把数量与交付选择放在标题里，适合希望读者关注谈判结果的安排。 |
| 先交两辆 | 提前说出局部结果。若看点是怎样达到这个结果，可以用；若本章悬念正是能交几辆，就选上一项。 |
| 刹车松了，比赛也换了地方 | 把发现和章尾变化一起说完；本例想保留电话的意外，就不选。 |
| 钥匙里的惊天秘密 | 正文没有这种秘密，不能靠标题制造虚假承诺。 |

本例选“先检查，再拿钥匙”：它承诺交付条件的碰撞，而不是事故真相或比赛新地点。选择是在这份已设章节内容中作出，不是所有修车题材都必须如此命名。
body.en:
The original workshop chapter has an established plan: Min wants three bikes; Luo requires basic checks, the second has a fault, and Luo rechecks the first and third and completes their required test rides. Min accepts those two first. As he prepares to leave, a call changes the race venue. Keys serve the handover rather than containing a hidden treasure. These are editorial candidates, not actual manuscript renames.

| Candidate | Decision |
|---|---|
| Repairs | Accurate but broad. Keep it if the book uses plain activity names; become more specific when the handover conflict is the emphasis. |
| Check First, Then Take the Keys | Names the condition negotiated in the chapter and fulfilled in the prose, without exposing the venue call. |
| Two Bikes or Three? | Foregrounds quantity and the receiving choice when the negotiation’s result is the attraction. |
| Two Bikes First | Reveals the local outcome. It can work when readers care how it happens; avoid it if the chapter’s central suspense is the number delivered. |
| Loose Brakes and a New Race Venue | Gives away both discovery and the closing change. Reject it when preserving the call’s surprise. |
| The Shocking Secret in the Keys | Promises a secret absent from the chapter; reject the invented attraction. |

The example selects “Check First, Then Take the Keys,” promising a collision over handover conditions rather than the old accident’s truth or new venue. This choice belongs to the established chapter, not a universal naming rule for repair stories.

heading.zh: 检查剧透、重名和目录里的辨识度
heading.en: Check Spoilers, Repetition, and the Contents

body.zh:
标题可以透露部分结果，不是每个信息都必须保密。先问：这一章的阅读兴趣在“会怎样”还是“怎样做到”？如果读者主要在猜投诉是谁递的，直接用“同事递的投诉”会提前替场景作答；如果正文从开头已告诉他们，就不必假装这个答案仍是秘密。

把候选放到前后几章的标题之间读。三个连续的“真相”“更大的真相”“最终真相”难以辨认，优先回到各章的实际材料；故意复现一个意象也可保留，区别由上下文与本章内容承担。

- [ ] 标题的动作、台词或物件在本章有依据
- [ ] 没有提前泄露作者本次想保留的身份或反转
- [ ] 没把另一章才发生的事借来招徕
- [ ] 与现有章名重名时，确认是有意重复还是需要修改
- [ ] 标题提出的期待，正文确实有相应内容

不宣称换标题就能提高追读。标题准确后，仍要读正文的事件、关系与节奏；不能只优化目录。
body.en:
A title may reveal part of an outcome. Ask whether the attraction is what will happen or how it happens. If readers are guessing who submitted a complaint, naming the coworker answers the scene early. If the opening already tells them, the title need not pretend that fact remains secret.

Read candidates among nearby chapter names. “The Truth,” “A Bigger Truth,” and “The Final Truth” may be hard to distinguish; return to each chapter’s material. Deliberate recurrence of a motif can remain when context and content provide the difference.

- [ ] The action, line, or object has support in this chapter.
- [ ] The title preserves the identity or turn the author wants withheld here.
- [ ] It does not borrow an event that occurs only in another chapter.
- [ ] A duplicate name is either intentional or revised.
- [ ] The prose contains what the title leads readers to expect.

Changing a name does not establish improved retention. Once the title is accurate, still review events, relationships, and pace rather than optimizing only the contents.

heading.zh: 选定后再同步章名，保留原编号与格式
heading.en: Apply the Choice Without Changing the Manuscript’s Format

body.zh:
Oh Story 的单章流程在标题预检发现重名或明显重复时，按核心事件调整，并同步细纲标题和正文文件名；长篇格式要求标题、编号和文件名服从项目既有格式。这里提供的是作者选名方法，不运行批量改名，也不假定替换文件名就已更新所有链接。

实际改已有章节时，先记录旧章号、标题和路径，再列出确实引用它的目录、链接或索引。按当前项目约定修改相关位置，检查是否还能打开正确章节；工具输出成功不代替这项检查。未接受的新标题留作候选，不改正文事件来适配它。

> 只为〔指定章节〕提出章名。先读取本章正文或已选细纲、现有章名和原格式，概括阅读重点；从实际动作、台词、矛盾或意象取候选，每项附正文依据、透露了什么和为何适合。不要补剧情，不替未写章节命名，不用相同的“惊天秘密”句式批量套。先给候选，等我选定后再按原编号和文件约定改相关位置。

书名、章名和章尾钩子可以配合，但各自解决不同问题；需要改故事承诺时回到[章尾钩子](/oh-story/chapter-ending-hooks)或[章节细纲](/oh-story/chapter-outline-template)，不用换章名掩盖正文缺口。
body.en:
Oh Story’s chapter workflow adjusts a duplicate or obviously repeated title from the core event and synchronizes the outline title and prose filename. Its long-form format follows the project’s established title, numbering, and file convention. This article selects names; it neither runs batch renames nor assumes renaming a file updates every link.

For an existing chapter, record the old number, title, and path. Identify actual references in contents, links, or indexes, update the relevant locations under the project’s convention, and check that the correct chapter still opens. An unaccepted candidate stays a proposal rather than changing events to fit its name.

> Suggest names only for [the specified chapter]. Read its prose or accepted outline, existing names, and format. State the reading emphasis, then draw candidates from actual actions, lines, conflicts, or motifs. Give evidence, what each reveals, and why it fits. Add no plot, name no unwritten chapters, and avoid one repeated shocking-secret formula. Present candidates first; apply the chosen name to relevant locations only after selection, preserving numbering and file conventions.

Book names, chapter names, and ending hooks can cooperate while serving different tasks. Return to [chapter hooks](/oh-story/chapter-ending-hooks) or the [chapter outline](/oh-story/chapter-outline-template) when the story promise needs work, rather than using a name to hide missing prose.

q.zh: 小说每一章都必须有标题吗？
q.en: Does every novel chapter need a title?

a.zh: 不必须。按作品和交付格式选择数字、人物名、地点或独立章名；先保持全书一致。要起名时从本章真实内容取材，不为满足“每章一个爆点标题”增加反转。
a.en: No. Choose numbers, character names, locations, or individual titles according to the work and its delivery format. Keep the book consistent and name actual chapter content without adding a twist to satisfy a dramatic-title quota.

text.zh: 可以请 story-long-write 先只讨论指定章名：提供正文或已选细纲、近邻标题和格式，取本章材料并说明剧透范围，不写正文；选定后再同步实际需要修改的位置。
text.en: Ask story-long-write to discuss names for specified chapters from prose or an accepted outline, nearby titles, and the existing format. Explain spoilers and stop before prose; apply the selected names only to locations that need updating.

label.en: Naming from chapter lines and conflict
