body.zh:
单听问题段，确认没有为了去静音截掉吸气、语尾或轻声字；连听前后句，确认间隔和音色自然；看当前成片，确认下一步信息没有抢在动作或原话之前。

更新实际放置记录和受影响字幕，保留未改内容。还没做候选时只记录拟改方案，做完后再写实际起止；同一组配置也不证明听感一致。

长停顿不一定坏。有意义的等待可以保留，机械空白才需要修；目标是该快的地方连贯，该让观众理解和感受的地方留得住。
body.en:
Listen to the segment for breaths, soft syllables, and tails lost by silence removal; listen across joins for pacing and voice; watch the current video for narration arriving before an action or original line.

Update actual placement and affected captions while retaining unchanged content. A proposed edit remains a proposal until a candidate exists; matching configuration does not prove matching listening quality.

Long pauses can work. Retain meaningful waiting and repair idle space so continuity and time for understanding coexist.

q.zh: 把pause_after_ms设成0就会没有停顿吗？
q.en: Does zero pause_after_ms remove every pause?

a.zh: 不会。WAV内部静音、作者窗口、入场延迟与收紧策略仍可能参与。看实际声音与放置，不只看字段。
a.en: No. WAV silence, authored windows, entry delay, and tightening may still matter. Inspect sound and placement, not just the field.

q.zh: 能把所有句子提前排紧吗？
q.en: Can I pull every line earlier?

a.zh: 先看原声、动作和信息揭示。需要保留的间隙不能被挤掉；重剪画面时也要重算声音与字幕。
a.en: Check source speech, action, and revelation first. Retain necessary gaps, and recalculate sound and captions when picture is recut.

text.zh: 请 video-recap 只排查下述配音或合成问题。先确认当前采用文件与具体时间，列出能观察的事实、缺失证据和最小修订；保留定稿、未受影响声音与画面。未生成或未听审的部分标待检查，不把元数据当实听通过。
text.en: Ask video-recap to diagnose this specified voiceover or assembly problem. Identify current media and time, observations, missing evidence, and a limited repair. Preserve approved text and unaffected sound and picture; mark ungenerated or unheard parts unchecked rather than treating metadata as listening approval.

label.zh: 分段窗口与段尾停顿契约
合成预算与分段记录
实际入场与段内收紧
声音分工与有意义的停留

title.zh: 导出视频没有声音怎么办：从原片、选段到合成逐层查
title.en: How to Fix a Video Export with No Sound

seo_title.zh: 导出视频没有声音怎么办：从原片、选段到合成逐层查
seo_title.en: How to Fix a Video Export with No Sound

description.zh: 先确认打开的版本，再查原片音轨、剪后中间片、分段配音与最终模式。静音补轨能保证拼接，不能恢复未录下的声音。
description.en: Check the current version, source streams, edited intermediate, voiceover segments, and final audio mode. A silence track cannot restore missing sound.

answer.zh: 先排除播放器选错版本、音轨或输出设备，再逐层对比原片、剪后中间片、分段配音与成片。文件有音轨不等于其中有可听声音；多源剪切会给无声素材补静音，合成模式又决定用原声、配音还是已采用混音。找到声音首次消失的一层，只修该层与必要依赖。
answer.en: First check version, player track, and output device, then compare source, edited intermediate, voiceover segments, and final video. An audio stream need not contain audible sound. Multi-source cuts pad silent material, and assembly mode chooses source, narration, or an adopted mix. Repair where sound first disappears and its necessary dependencies.

heading.zh: 先确认正在听哪份文件
heading.en: Confirm Which File You Are Hearing

body.zh:
打开当前采用版本，确认播放器音量、选中音轨和输出设备；用一份已知能正常听见的文件作对照。别把旧预览、只有画面的候选或另一路音轨当成当前交付。对照文件也无声时，先处理播放环境。

同一视频有多音轨时，要实际听目标轨内容。序号只是位置，不代表第0轨一定是对白。记录具体文件和时间；“能打开”“有audio字段”均不证明听到了目标声音。
body.en:
Open the adopted version and check player volume, selected track, and output device against a known audible file. An old preview, picture-only candidate, or another track is not the delivery. If the reference is also silent, address playback first.

Listen to the intended track in a multi-track file. An ordinal is a position, not proof track zero contains dialogue. Record file and time; opening it or finding an audio field proves no audible target sound.

heading.zh: 找声音第一次消失的位置
heading.en: Find Where Sound First Disappears

body.zh:
| 比较位置 | 查什么 |
|---|---|
| 原片 | 是否有目标音轨，选段处是否实际录到声音 |
| 剪后中间片 | 所用源与区间是否正确；某源无轨时是否补了静音 |
| 分段WAV或已采用完整混音 | 文件存在、声音内容完整，且本轮确实使用了它 |
| 当前成片 | 实际采用哪种声音模式、哪一路、是否被压低或遮盖 |

Video Recap 的源探测查询音轨并检查进程返回结果。探测执行失败与成功确认没有目标轨不是同一事实，先看错误；不要把无法读取直接写成原片没录音。[ffprobe 文档](https://ffmpeg.org/ffprobe.html)说明它查询媒体流信息，打开失败会返回错误。探到音轨也仍需实际播放。

原片没有录到的声音不能靠放大音量恢复。若可用原声完整而中间片丢了，修选段或路由；若WAV缺失、合成标未放置，先解决具体段，不再加音乐掩盖。
body.en:
| Comparison | Check |
|---|---|
| Source | Intended stream and actually recorded sound at the selected interval |
| Edited intermediate | Consumed source and interval; silence padding for a source without audio |
| Segment WAV or adopted full mix | Existing, complete content actually consumed this run |
| Current video | Actual mode, selected stream, and attenuation or masking |

Video Recap queries streams and checks the probe process result. Failed probing and successful confirmation of no target stream are different observations; inspect errors before declaring no recording. The [ffprobe documentation](https://ffmpeg.org/ffprobe.html) describes stream inspection and errors when input cannot be opened. A detected stream still needs playback.

Gain cannot recover unrecorded speech. Repair selection or routing if the source is complete but the intermediate loses it. Address a missing or unplaced WAV locally rather than adding music to hide it.

heading.zh: 纸面例：有一段无声，不等于整片丢声
heading.en: Paper Example: One Silent Source Is Not a Silent Whole

body.zh:
以下是假设素材与检查结果，没有渲染或听审。A选3秒，含已录对白；B选2秒，没有音轨；C选3秒，含已录环境声。按A、B、C拼接，共8秒。

| 输出区间 | 预期与待检查 |
|---|---|
| 0–3 | 来自A的对白；需回听所选源区间与中间片 |
| 3–5 | B的等长静音补轨；不会自动出现原本未录的声音 |
| 5–8 | 来自C的环境声；不能因B无声把C一并丢掉 |

所引多源剪切实现逐源处理：有音轨就截对应音频，没有就补该段长度的静音，然后拼接。最终可以有一条连续音轨，其中一段仍安静。

若实际整段0–8都无声，不能只归咎B；继续比较A、C原声、中间片与最终模式。若只缺B，要看原片是否有声音可用，或本场本就需要静默。需要另配声音时单独作创作决定，不冒充找回原录音。
body.en:
These are hypothetical sources and checks, without rendering or listening. A supplies three seconds with recorded dialogue; B supplies two with no audio stream; C supplies three with ambience. A–B–C totals eight seconds.

| Output | Expectation and pending check |
|---|---|
| 0–3 | A’s dialogue; listen to its selected source interval and intermediate. |
| 3–5 | B’s equal-length silence padding; unrecorded sound does not appear automatically. |
| 5–8 | C’s ambience; B being silent should not discard C. |

The cited multi-source renderer handles each source separately: trim existing audio, or create equal-length silence, then concatenate. A continuous audio track can contain a silent passage.

If all 0–8 is actually silent, B alone is not the explanation. Compare A/C source audio, the intermediate, and final mode. For B alone, check available source sound or intended silence. Newly designed sound is a separate decision, not recovered recording.

heading.zh: 核对实际模式，再听最终文件
heading.en: Check the Actual Mode, Then Hear the Delivery

body.zh:
旁白模式需要有效分段并放入时间线；原声混音不生成旁白，但会处理选中原声；已采用AAC音轨复制有编码、区间与输入限制，选错轨会复制错内容。无旁白模式必须显式选择，不能把空TTS当成完成配音。

已采用音轨复制遇到错误不自动改成原声混音；新画面要配旧完整混音时走明确配对，再核对输出轨。模式切换可能改变声音处理，不能只改名字后声称旧混音仍完整保留。

修复后单听目标区间，再连听每个接点和尾部，最后看完整成片。记录哪一层的问题被实际修好，哪些仍待听；流检查、包复制和正常播放分别证明不同的事。
body.en:
Narration needs valid placed segments. Source-mix creates no narration but processes the selected source audio. Adopted AAC copy has codec, interval, and input constraints; a wrong selected stream copies wrong content. Choose no-narration explicitly rather than using empty TTS as completed speech.

A copy failure does not authorize a silent switch to mixing. Pair new picture with an old complete mix explicitly, then check output selection. Changing modes may change processing; a renamed mode proves no retained mix.

After repair, listen to the target interval, joins, and tail, then watch the full video. Record which layer was repaired and what remains unheard. Stream inspection, packet copying, and playback prove different things.

heading.zh: 完整返修例：误发画面预览，保住八秒原声
heading.en: Complete repair: replace the silent preview and retain source sound

body.zh:
沿用A三秒、B两秒、C三秒原例，展开一个具体分支：假定核查确认`edited_source.mp4`的音频序号0已包含A完整对白、B等长静音、C环境声；旧交付误发只有画面的预览。本版选择原声，未选旁白、额外BGM或新字幕。

完整修订单：

> 改用核过的八秒剪后文件作输入，保留A对白、B静音和C环境声。本轮不生成旁白或添配乐。实际核音轨与画面时钟满足复制条件后，显式采用adopted-packet-copy和音频序号0，用新工作/交付目录保留旧预览。打开本次交付，先听A、B、C各区间，再听两个接点和全八秒，核画面次序仍相同。

从已安装`video-assemble`技能目录运行，本纸面命令为：

> `python3 scripts/assemble.py /project/edited_source.mp4 --work-dir no-sound-repair --output-dir no-sound-delivery --recap-stem no-sound-candidate --audio-mode adopted-packet-copy --audio-stream-index 0 --no-burn-subtitles`

换成实际路径，两目录本次用新名称。复制要求选中AAC及相容区间，不读取TTS，不能带额外BGM或显式TTS设置。关闭新烧录符合本例无新字幕的选择，源硬字仍在画面；需要字幕另定交付，见[字幕缺失排查](/video-recap/fix-subtitles-missing-from-video-export)。

复制针对实际剪后输入音轨，不承诺A、C原始AAC包未经处理直达成片；此前多源剪切已经处理和拼接。剪后若本身少A或C，先修上游声音再复制。

方案未执行或试听。B安静是所选来源事实，A、C完整可听仍须复查，不能给B填音乐冒充找回全片声音。
body.en:
Keep A’s three seconds, B’s two and C’s three. This branch assumes checks establish that audio ordinal 0 in `edited_source.mp4` already contains A’s complete dialogue, B’s equal-duration silence and C’s ambience. A picture-only preview was mistakenly delivered. The selected version uses source sound, without narration, extra BGM or new captions.

Complete repair request:

> Use the checked eight-second cut as input, retaining A, B’s silence and C. Generate no narration or added music. Verify copy-compatible audio and picture clocks, then explicitly adopt adopted-packet-copy with audio ordinal 0. Use new work/delivery directories and retain the old preview. Open the new delivery, listen to all three intervals, both joins and eight seconds, and compare picture order.

From the installed `video-assemble` directory, the paper command is:

> `python3 scripts/assemble.py /project/edited_source.mp4 --work-dir no-sound-repair --output-dir no-sound-delivery --recap-stem no-sound-candidate --audio-mode adopted-packet-copy --audio-stream-index 0 --no-burn-subtitles`

Replace the path and use new directories. Copy requires selected AAC and compatible intervals, does not read TTS and rejects extra BGM or explicit TTS settings. No new burn-in follows this example’s caption choice; source-burned pixels remain. Choose any new captions separately; see [missing-caption diagnosis](/video-recap/fix-subtitles-missing-from-video-export).

Copy applies to the actual cut’s audio, not untouched original AAC packets from A and C: multi-source cutting has already processed and joined sound. If the cut lacks A or C, repair it before freezing the audio.

No execution or listening occurred here. B is deliberately silent; review A and C for complete audibility. Music in B does not recover the whole soundtrack.

q.zh: 文件显示有音轨，为什么还是没声？
q.en: Why can a file have an audio stream yet sound silent?

a.zh: 音轨可能包含静音、不是目标内容，或被播放/混音设置影响。检查选中轨并实际听，再定位源与输出差异。
a.en: It may contain silence or different content, or playback/mix settings may affect it. Listen to the selected track and compare source with output.

q.zh: 多视频中一段没有声音，会让其他段也静音吗？
q.en: Does one silent source silence every clip?

a.zh: 所引多源实现分别处理，各段无声时补等长静音。有声来源仍应保留；实际整片无声需继续查区间、探测与合成模式。
a.en: The cited multi-source implementation pads each missing-audio segment separately. Other audio should remain; a fully silent result still needs interval, probe, and mode checks.

text.zh: 请 video-recap 只排查下述配音或合成问题。先确认当前采用文件与具体时间，列出能观察的事实、缺失证据和最小修订；保留定稿、未受影响声音与画面。未生成或未听审的部分标待检查，不把元数据当实听通过。
text.en: Ask video-recap to diagnose this specified voiceover or assembly problem. Identify current media and time, observations, missing evidence, and a limited repair. Preserve approved text and unaffected sound and picture; mark ungenerated or unheard parts unchecked rather than treating metadata as listening approval.

label.zh: 音轨探测返回条件
逐源声音与静音补轨
原声、旁白与音轨复制模式
label.en: Source, narration, and copied audio modes

label.zh: 缺WAV与实际放置状态
合成命令与字幕选择
剪后音轨与新目录路由

title.zh: 小说写到一半想改大纲怎么办：先分清已写事实和后续计划
title.en: How to Revise a Novel Outline Mid-Draft

seo_title.zh: 小说写到一半改大纲怎么办
seo_title.en: Revise a Novel Outline Mid-Draft

description.zh: 把中途改纲拆成保留、替换和需要重写的部分。附十八章后的改纲示例、后续场面和给AI的范围说明。
description.en: Separate established facts from future plans before changing an outline. Includes a mid-draft example, a candidate scene, and a bounded AI request.

answer.zh: 先说清想改什么：后续走向、人物用途，还是已写事件。把正文已经发生的事、读者仍在等的承诺和尚未发生的计划分开，再调整受影响的后续段落。若新走向与已写事实冲突，选择保留事实并另找路径，或明确重写哪些前文章节；不要让新大纲悄悄改掉过去。
answer.en: Define whether you want to change a future direction, a character’s role, or a written event. Separate established facts, outstanding reader promises, and unexecuted plans before revising dependent beats. When the new direction conflicts with the draft, preserve the facts and find another route, or explicitly select earlier chapters for revision. A new outline cannot silently rewrite the past.

heading.zh: 先判断是小调整，还是需要回头改正文
heading.en: Distinguish a Future Adjustment from a Draft Rewrite

body.zh:
角色写活以后，原大纲不再合适很常见。需要判断的是新版本怎样接上现有故事，而不是证明自己开书时就想对了。

- **只改尚未写到的路径：**原来准备靠一封信揭谜，现在改成两人当面核对。检查这封信是否已经出现在正文、它的存在是否还需要解释，再重排后面的场景。
- **改变人物用途：**原计划让朋友成为幕后人，现在想保留合作关系。过去的行为可以重新解释，但已写的明确事实不能无声消失；留意哪些可疑细节仍需要交代。
- **改变核心前提或结局：**会牵动更多章节。先标出牵动范围，再决定继续草稿、局部返修或整体重构。不是每次改纲都要推翻全书。

技能的中途补纲流程限制本次请求范围，并保护已有正文区间对应的规划；这里把它转成作者可用的编辑办法。**保护旧内容不等于作者不能重写**，而是改未来和改过去应当成为两项明确选择。
body.en:
Once characters develop on the page, the original plan may stop fitting. The task is to connect the new direction to the existing story, not to prove that your first plan was perfect.

- **Change an unwritten route:** replace a planned letter with an in-person inquiry. Check whether the letter already exists in the prose or its existence still needs explaining, then rearrange future scenes.
- **Change a character’s role:** a planned culprit becomes a continuing ally. Earlier behavior may receive a different interpretation, but explicit facts cannot disappear. Suspicious details may still need an explanation.
- **Change the premise or ending:** identify the wider consequences before choosing to continue, revise selected passages, or rebuild. A local change need not overturn the whole novel.

The skill’s expansion workflow bounds the request and protects planning associated with written sections. This page translates that into an editorial method. **Protection does not forbid an author from rewriting.** Changing the future and changing the past should be explicit, separate choices.

heading.zh: 用一页说明新方向怎样接住旧内容
heading.en: Make a One-Page Change Note

body.zh:
| 要写清的事 | 本次改纲说明 |
|---|---|
| 为什么改 | 读者体验或人物选择有什么具体改善，避免只写“更精彩” |
| 已写事实 | 谁做过什么、实际知道什么、物件在哪里；引用章段 |
| 仍在等的内容 | 已提出的问题、承诺或伏笔；决定兑现、改变理解或明确放弃 |
| 新的后续 | 哪些未写场景替换、保留或推迟，怎样接到当前状态 |
| 牵动范围 | 本次改哪几章；结局、其他卷或已写正文是否需要另作选择 |

这是本页的编辑说明，不是技能原生文件格式。不需要罗列整部小说的每个细节，只抓本次变动会碰到的依赖。还没决定的地方写“待选”，不要让AI为补齐表格编一个既成事实。
body.en:
| Question | Change note |
|---|---|
| Why change? | Name the improvement to reader experience or character choice rather than “make it better.” |
| Established facts | Cite who acted, who knows what, and where relevant objects are. |
| Outstanding promises | List affected questions, commitments, or clues; choose payoff, reinterpretation, or explicit abandonment. |
| New future | Identify unwritten scenes to replace, retain, or defer and how they follow the current state. |
| Scope | Name affected chapters and any separate choice involving earlier prose, other volumes, or the ending. |

This is an editorial worksheet, not a native skill file format. Include dependencies touched by this change rather than the entire book. Mark undecided points as choices instead of asking AI to invent established facts to complete a table.

heading.zh: 原创示例：不再让朋友成为幕后人
heading.en: Original Example: Keeping the Friend as an Ally

body.zh:
假设《旧车站来信》写到第十八章。阿澄和朋友闻宁查一批遗失的旧照片。第十二章，闻宁实际陪她看过废站的照片箱；第十七章，他收到过保管人的电话，说有一张照片被单独封存。阿澄听见电话响，但不知道通话内容。第十八章结尾，两人约好第二天到站务室继续查。

旧大纲打算第二十二章揭示闻宁偷藏照片，第二十五章两人决裂。作者现在觉得合作调查更适合这本书，希望把闻宁改成愿意帮忙、却因答应保管人暂不外传而沉默的朋友。**这个承诺是作者选择新增的后续解释，不是第十七章正文已经证实的事实。**

| 内容 | 本次如何处理 |
|---|---|
| 第十二章共同查箱 | 保留；两人真的去过，不改成闻宁从未到场 |
| 第十七章电话 | 保留接听与阿澄不知内容；未写的内容可在后文解释 |
| 闻宁偷藏照片 | 只是旧计划，撤下；若原稿已经写他拿走照片，就要另选归还、动机解释或前文重写 |
| 第十九章会面 | 保留既有约定；让闻宁解释隐瞒，再由保管人实际回应 |
| 第二十二至二十五章 | 换成查封存缘由和取得有限查看机会；查看不自动证明谁遗失整批照片 |

新方向留下朋友隐瞒造成的不满，也留下照片去向的问题。它撤下的是未发生的偷藏和决裂，不是把阿澄已有的疑惑改成“她一直信任他”。
body.en:
Suppose “Letters from the Old Station” is drafted through chapter eighteen. Cheng and her friend Ning are investigating missing photographs. In chapter twelve he accompanies her to inspect a box at the disused station. In chapter seventeen he receives a call from the keeper saying that one photograph is separately sealed. Cheng hears the phone ring but not the conversation. Chapter eighteen ends with an appointment to visit the station office together the next day.

The old outline makes Ning the thief in chapter twenty-two and ends their friendship in chapter twenty-five. The author now prefers a cooperative investigation: Ning has stayed silent because he promised the keeper not to circulate the information yet. **That promise is a newly chosen future explanation, not a fact already established by chapter seventeen.**

| Element | This revision |
|---|---|
| Joint box inspection | Retain the visit; do not make Ning absent from it. |
| Phone call | Retain the call and Cheng’s ignorance; later scenes may reveal its unwritten content. |
| Theft by Ning | Remove an unexecuted plan. If the draft already shows him taking the photograph, separately choose return, explanation, or earlier revision. |
| Chapter nineteen meeting | Keep the appointment; let Ning explain and the keeper actually respond. |
| Chapters twenty-two to twenty-five | Investigate the sealing and obtain limited viewing. Viewing does not prove who lost the entire collection. |

The new direction retains resentment over withheld information and the mystery of the photographs. It removes a planned theft and rupture; it does not make Cheng “always have trusted him.”

heading.zh: 再写一小段，试新方向能不能落地
heading.en: Test the Direction in a Candidate Scene

body.zh:
作者选定保管人可当面核对自己经手的事，并允许约定一次查看。下面是候选第十九章片段，不表示真实项目已经写到这里：

> 到站务室门口，闻宁停下来。“那天电话是说一张照片被封存了。我答应等当面问清楚再说，可我也该告诉你，我有事瞒着。”
>
> “你可以说不方便讲，”阿澄说，“别让我猜你又查到了什么。”
>
> 保管人开门后，闻宁问起那通电话。对方说：“是我让你暂不外传。照片没给你，一直在我保管的封袋里。”
>
> “我想看照片和封存那天的记录。”阿澄说。
>
> “今天我找记录，明天下午给你们看这张。其他封袋不能动。”
>
> 阿澄记下时间。“好。先看这一张。”她把本来要问闻宁“你藏在哪里”的那一行划掉，另写了封存日期。

这段把旧约定接上、把隐瞒说出、给对方真实回应，并留下下一步。保管人的说法仍需要核对；看照片还是明天的计划，两人还没有拿到照片或查明整批去向。若作者希望阿澄暂不接受解释，可保留她的拒绝或更强的不满，不强行完成和解。
body.en:
The author chooses that the keeper can answer for his own handling and arrange a viewing. This is a candidate for chapter nineteen, not a report that a real project has reached it:

> Outside the office Ning stopped. “The call was about a sealed photograph. I promised to wait until we could ask in person. I still should have told you I was withholding something.”
>
> “You could have said you couldn’t discuss it,” Cheng said. “Don’t leave me guessing what else you’ve found.”
>
> When the keeper opened the door, Ning asked about the call. “I asked you not to circulate it yet,” the keeper said. “I never gave you the photograph. It’s remained in a sealed envelope with me.”
>
> “I’d like to see it and the record from the day it was sealed,” Cheng said.
>
> “I’ll find the record today. Tomorrow afternoon you can see this photograph. Not the other envelopes.”
>
> Cheng wrote down the time. “All right. This one first.” She crossed out the question “Where did you hide it?” and wrote the sealing date instead.

The passage honors the appointment, exposes the concealment, gives the keeper a response, and establishes a next step. His account still needs checking. Tomorrow’s viewing is a plan: they neither possess the photograph nor know the collection’s full destination. An author may instead keep Cheng’s refusal or stronger resentment; reconciliation is not compulsory.

heading.zh: 改完后检查什么，什么时候停
heading.en: Check the Dependencies and Stop at the Agreed Layer

body.zh:
先看新后续是否从第十八章的真实状态出发，再查旧计划是否残留在人物卡、卷纲或后续细纲中。只改受影响的记录，别把整个书库都重做。

**三种常见失败：**新纲给阿澄提前知道通话内容，回到她实际获知的场面；旧纲仍写“第二十二章闻宁承认偷藏”，撤下或明确选另一条路线；为了补一个场景把整卷多扩二十章，先说明体量改变，让作者决定扩卷还是压缩。

本次只要大纲，就停在大纲。若需要返修已写正文，先选具体章段，再按[前文改动后的后文检查](/oh-story/sync-later-chapters-after-a-revision)核依赖。规划文件中的“明天看照片”不会自动成为人物已经看过照片的记录。
body.en:
First check that the new future begins from chapter eighteen’s actual state. Then remove obsolete plans from affected character notes and outlines, without rebuilding unrelated records.

**Common failures:** Cheng knows the call’s contents too early—return to the scene where she learns them. An outline still says Ning admits theft in chapter twenty-two—remove it or explicitly choose that other route. One added scene expands the volume by twenty chapters—explain the size change before choosing expansion or compression.

Stop at the outline if that is the requested deliverable. Select earlier passages before revising prose, then use the [later-chapter dependency check](/oh-story/sync-later-chapters-after-a-revision). A planned viewing cannot become a record that a character already saw the photograph.

q.zh: 改大纲是不是说明前面白写了？
q.en: Does changing the outline waste the earlier draft?

a.zh: 不一定。人物、关系和已提出的问题可能仍有效。先保留新方向用得上的正文，再处理真正冲突的章段，不能仅因旧计划不再采用就认定所有前文无用。
a.en: Not necessarily. Characters, relationships, and outstanding questions may still work. Retain useful prose and identify actual conflicts instead of treating every passage as wasted because an old plan changes.

q.zh: 可以让AI直接重新生成整部大纲吗？
q.en: Can I ask AI to regenerate the entire outline?

a.zh: 可以在明确选择整体重构时这样做，但要给已写事实和保留范围。只想调整后续几章时，先限制请求；整部重生容易把旧计划、已发生事件和新设定混在一起。
a.en: Yes, when you explicitly choose a full rebuild and supply established facts and retained material. For a local adjustment, bound the request first; wholesale regeneration may mix old plans, actual events, and new inventions.

text.zh: 用 $story-long-write 帮我调整第十九至二十五章大纲。附已写到第十八章的状态、原计划、新方向、仍需兑现的线索和本书文风。先列保留事实、受影响的计划与需要我选择的冲突；只改点名范围，不修改已写正文，不把计划写成已发生。若结局或卷长也受影响，先说明牵动范围。
text.en: Use $story-long-write to revise the outline for chapters nineteen through twenty-five. Include the written state through chapter eighteen, old plan, new direction, outstanding clues, and book style. Identify retained facts, affected plans, and conflicts requiring a choice. Revise the named scope without changing existing prose or marking plans as events. Explain any dependency on the ending or volume length.

label.zh: 中途补纲、请求范围与规划事实
label.en: Mid-draft expansion, requested scope, and planned facts

label.zh: 已写区间的规划与卷尾追加
label.en: Planning for written sections and appending units

label.zh: 作者选择与事实边界

title.zh: 小说多线叙事怎么安排：切换时机、时间和信息差
title.en: How to Weave Multiple Storylines in a Novel

seo_title.zh: 小说多线叙事怎么安排
seo_title.en: Weave Multiple Storylines in a Novel

description.zh: 给每条故事线明确当下问题，再安排切换与汇合。附图书馆和印刷铺的完整双线片段、时间表与修订办法。
description.en: Give each storyline a present question, then choose returns and intersections. Includes a complete two-location passage and a timing worksheet.

answer.zh: 先确定每条线在这一段解决什么、读者为什么关心，再按行动与情绪的停点切换。各线可以快慢不同，不必每章轮流出场或字数平均。切回时交代人物、地点和必要时间；分清读者从另一条线看到的事与人物真正收到的信息。
answer.en: Give each thread a present question and a reason readers care. Switch at useful action or emotional stopping points. Threads may move at different speeds without equal word counts or rigid alternation. On returning, orient readers to character, place, and necessary time. What readers saw elsewhere is not automatically information the characters received.

heading.zh: 先决定读者为什么要跟每一条线
heading.en: Give Readers a Reason to Follow Each Thread

body.zh:
多线不只是多个人物轮流出现。先为这一段写清：谁在处理什么问题、处境会怎样变化、下次回来要看什么。可以有共同目标，也可以分别处理同一主题的不同难题。

一条线帮助另一条线取得资源、改变选择或发现信息时，可用[主线与支线汇聚](/oh-story/subplot-mainline-convergence)检查作用。若你选择的是平行叙事，例如两代人分别面对离乡，各线也可以靠主题和情绪互相照见，不必每条线立即送一个道具给主角。但读者仍需要理解它在这本书里的位置。

源框架建议多线错开推进，也给出升级题材的出场频率示例。本页只取“错开节奏”的方法，**不把战力、装备、情感或声望每段升级当成所有小说的配额**。生活、停顿和回收关系也可以是这一轮的内容。
body.en:
Multiple threads are more than alternating people. For this section, identify the problem each person handles, what may change, and what readers will return to see. Threads may share a goal or address different aspects of one theme.

When one thread changes another’s resources, choices, or knowledge, use the [main-plot and subplot convergence guide](/oh-story/subplot-mainline-convergence). Parallel narratives can also illuminate one another through theme and feeling—for example, two generations leaving home—without immediately handing the protagonist an object. Readers still need a reason for each thread’s place in the book.

The source framework staggers threads and includes progression-fiction frequency examples. This page uses the staggered rhythm, **not a quota requiring combat, equipment, romance, or reputation upgrades in every novel**. Everyday life, a pause, or a relationship’s return can carry a turn.

heading.zh: 在有理由的地方切，而不是机械ABAB
heading.en: Switch for a Reason Rather Than a Rigid ABAB Pattern

body.zh:
切换可以发生在一个选择之后、一次结果之前、一个小段落结束时，或情绪需要缓冲时。不是每次都要把人物留在危险里。

| 这一段的切换 | 读者带着什么回来 |
|---|---|
| A刚提出借展问题，转B | 想知道B能否带来可用资料；回来需有处理，不长期只吊问题 |
| B决定放弃原件，转A | 读者知道资料形式变了，等待A如何接受；A尚未收到消息时仍不能照新计划行动 |
| A完成展柜安排，再转B | 一个局部问题已收束，可以接另一线的关系或善后 |

不要把同一事件完整叙述两遍，只为轮到另一个视角。第二次若没有新的选择、理解或体验，压缩重复；若重看本身是作品需要，可保留。视角切换是否另起章节、用空行或标注时间，服从本书形式，关键是读者能跟上。
body.en:
A switch may follow a choice, precede a result, finish a local passage, or give emotion room. It need not always strand someone in danger.

| Switch | Reason to return |
|---|---|
| A raises the loan question; move to B | Can B obtain usable material? Return with meaningful handling instead of endlessly postponing it. |
| B gives up borrowing the original; move to A | Readers await A’s response to a changed format. A cannot act on news that has not arrived. |
| A finishes the display arrangement; move to B | A local question has closed, leaving room for B’s relationship or aftermath. |

Do not retell an entire event merely because another viewpoint gets a turn. Compress a second account without a new choice, understanding, or experience; retain repetition when it is an intentional effect. Chapters, breaks, and time labels follow the book’s form while keeping orientation clear.

heading.zh: 原创双线片段：展柜与旧印版
heading.en: Original Two-Thread Passage: A Cabinet and an Old Printing Plate

body.zh:
设定：图书馆当晚办旧街展览。陈瑜负责布展，林乔去印刷铺申请借一块旧印版，是否准借尚未确认。铺主可以决定原件借用和本次拍摄，拍摄件能在图书馆展出；陈瑜此前只知道林乔去问原件。两人手机可通话，林乔原来答应下午三点半前给答复。以下为本页原创示范：

> **下午三点十分，图书馆。**陈瑜把“印版原件，借展待确认”的便签贴在空柜上。
>
> 同事拿来另一组老街照片。“这个柜要是不用原件，我们就摆照片。”
>
> “三点半前定。”陈瑜留下便签，把照片放在旁边。
>
> **三点十二分，印刷铺。**林乔把借展说明递给铺主。铺主看完，把旧印版留在工作台上：“出门搬动不行。上回边角就磕过。你可以在这里拍，今晚展拍摄件，原件不借。”
>
> “那我拍完先给你看选哪张，标清是拍摄件，可以吗？”
>
> 铺主点头。“写上铺名。别把晚上的展出当成以后都能拿去用。”
>
> 林乔应下，拿手机拍了一张全貌。她先把照片给铺主看，对方确认这张可用。三点二十四分，她拨通陈瑜的电话。
>
> **图书馆。**陈瑜听完说：“好，展拍摄件。把确认过的照片发来，说明原件仍在铺里。”
>
> 林乔发送照片后，陈瑜打开消息，确认能看清图案，才对同事说：“柜里放老街照片，印版的照片在旁边展板上。标签写清拍摄件。”两人取下待确认便签，把老街照片放进展柜。
>
> **印刷铺。**电话挂断，林乔按铺主的要求记录这次使用范围。她没有带走印版，铺主把它盖好，仍留在工作台上。林乔收起手机：“展板做好后，我发一张给你看标签。”

B线先取得拍摄许可，读者先知道它；A直到实际接电话才知道借展结果，直到打开照片才知道成像是否可用。结尾A完成照片入柜，B记下使用范围；展板尚未做完，也没证明整场展览成功。
body.en:
Setup: a library is preparing an old-street exhibition that evening. Chen handles the display; Lin asks a print-shop owner to lend an old plate. Approval is pending. The owner can authorize this loan or this photographed display. Chen knows only that Lin is asking about the original. Both phones work; Lin promised an answer by 3:30. This is an original demonstration:

> **3:10 p.m., library.** Chen stuck a note on the empty cabinet: “Original plate—loan pending.”
>
> A colleague brought another set of street photographs. “If there’s no original, these can go here.”
>
> “We’ll know by half past.” Chen left the note and put the photographs beside it.
>
> **3:12 p.m., print shop.** Lin handed over the loan request. The owner read it but kept the plate on the bench. “No transport. The edge was chipped last time. You can photograph it here and display the image tonight. The original stays.”
>
> “Can I show you the image I select and label it as a photograph?”
>
> He nodded. “Name the shop. Tonight’s display doesn’t authorize every later use.”
>
> Lin agreed and photographed the whole plate. She showed the image to the owner, who approved that one. At 3:24 she called Chen.
>
> **Library.** After listening, Chen said, “Good. We’ll display the photograph. Send the approved image and note that the original stays at the shop.”
>
> Lin sent it. Chen opened the message and checked that the pattern was visible before telling her colleague, “Street photos in the cabinet; the plate image on the neighboring board. Label it as a photograph.” They removed the pending note and placed the street photographs in the cabinet.
>
> **Print shop.** After the call, Lin recorded the permitted use. She did not take the plate; the owner covered it on the bench. Lin put her phone away. “When the board’s ready, I’ll send you a picture of the label.”

Readers learn B’s permission first. A learns the loan outcome only by answering the call, and sees image quality only by opening the message. A finishes placing cabinet photographs; B records the permission. The board remains unfinished, and the whole exhibition’s success is not established.

heading.zh: 用时间和知情表查穿帮
heading.en: Check Time and Knowledge Across the Threads

body.zh:
| 时刻与人物 | 此刻实际发生、知道或持有的事 |
|---|---|
| 15:10陈瑜 | 知道借展待确认；留柜，还没有借展答复 |
| 15:12起林乔 | 得到拒借与本次拍摄许可；拍摄并给铺主确认，原件留铺 |
| 15:24起双方 | 实际通话，陈瑜接受改展拍摄件；照片发送后实际打开才核可用性 |
| 通话后 | 陈瑜和同事摆好柜内照片；林乔记下范围；展板与标签照片仍待做 |

这张表是编辑工具，不是必须出现在小说里的说明。正文可只在最初标明时间，后面靠电话承接；如果各线隔了数天，就需要更多时间提示。读者知道B获准拍摄，不等于A或其他同事已经知道；发出消息也不等于所有人已经读到。
body.en:
| Time, person | Actual state |
|---|---|
| 3:10, Chen | Loan pending; reserves cabinet without a loan answer yet. |
| From 3:12, Lin | Receives refusal and specific photography permission; takes and gets approval for an image. Plate remains at shop. |
| From 3:24, both | Actually speak; Chen accepts the changed display. She checks usability after receiving and opening the image. |
| After call | Chen and colleague place cabinet photographs; Lin records scope. Board and label photograph remain pending. |

This is an editing tool, not compulsory exposition. The prose may label time initially and use the call to connect the rest. Threads separated by days need more orientation. Reader knowledge of B’s permission does not give it to A or absent colleagues. Sending a message does not mean everyone has read it.

heading.zh: 切得太碎或一条线被遗忘，怎样修
heading.en: Repair Fragmented Switches and Neglected Threads

body.zh:
**每次只写几句就切：**先把同一条线的一次询问、选择或感受写到可停的位置，再切；不要为了展示“多线”把完整交流拆碎。

**一条线隔很久才回来：**返回时给人物、地点、距离上次的时间和当前问题一个简短锚点，不必重述整条线。如果等待期间什么都没有发生，可压缩时间或明确暂放；如果发生了变化，写出必要结果，别让人物永远停在上一章的姿势。

**两条线像两本无关的书：**明确共同问题、因果连接或主题联系，并让读者能感受到。不一定强行安排所有人最终会面。删去一条线会失去什么，是诊断问题；保留它可能为了体验和主题，而不只是运送主线资源。

**每条线都在章尾危急：**用局部完成、低压回收和关系交流改变节奏。技能里的特定高潮框架是选项，各线不必同步冲顶。
body.en:
**Switching every few sentences:** finish a useful question, choice, or feeling within one thread before leaving it. Do not fragment a complete exchange to advertise the structure.

**Returning after a long absence:** briefly orient readers to person, place, elapsed time, and the present problem. If nothing happened during the gap, compress or explicitly pause it. If something changed, include the necessary result rather than freezing a character in the previous pose.

**Threads feel like unrelated books:** make the shared question, causal connection, or thematic relationship perceptible. Everyone need not meet eventually. Asking what removal would lose is a diagnostic; experience and theme can justify a thread as well as resources for the main plot.

**Every line ends in peril:** vary rhythm with local completion, quiet returns, and relationship exchanges. Specific climax frameworks are options; threads need not peak simultaneously.

q.zh: 多线叙事一定要多视角吗？
q.en: Does a multi-thread story require multiple viewpoints?

a.zh: 不一定。一个视角人物也可以参与多条事情；多个人物的平行线则可按需要选不同视角。故事线回答“发生什么”，视角回答“读者从谁那里看见”，不要把两项当成同一件事。
a.en: No. One viewpoint character can participate in several threads; parallel characters may need different viewpoints. A thread concerns what happens, while viewpoint concerns whose experience presents it.

q.zh: 每条线都要一样长吗？
q.en: Must the threads be equally long?

a.zh: 不必。按它在本书的分量、当前阶段和读者等待决定篇幅。重要配角线也可能只在关键位置出现，不因轮到它就填一章无关内容。
a.en: No. Allocate space by importance, stage, and what readers await. Even an important secondary thread may appear only at key moments; its turn does not justify an irrelevant chapter.

text.zh: 用 $story-long-write 帮我安排这段多线叙事。附各线人物、地点、当下目标、已知信息、时间约束与既定结局。先提出切换和回归位置，说明每次切换让读者等待什么；核对消息发送、接收和人物行动。允许各线不同步，不要求每章全部出场或统一升级，不改既定事实。
text.en: Use $story-long-write to arrange these storylines with characters, locations, present goals, known information, time constraints, and the chosen ending. Propose switches and returns, naming what readers wait for. Check actual message sending, receipt, and action. Allow unequal pace without compulsory appearances or upgrades in every chapter; retain established facts.

label.zh: 多线错开推进与双线交替
故事线、信息差与批次边界
label.en: Storylines, information gaps, and scoped beats

label.zh: 视角选择与信息边界

title.zh: 小说谈判场景怎么写：目标、条件和实际让步
title.en: How to Write a Negotiation Scene in Fiction

seo_title.zh: 小说谈判场景怎么写
seo_title.en: Write a Negotiation Scene in Fiction

description.zh: 让人物围绕可交换条件谈判，保留各自限制。附修船铺完整场面、逐回合分析和谈妥后实际执行的边界。
description.en: Build negotiations around goals, conditions, and limits. Includes a complete repair-shop scene and the difference between agreement and action.

answer.zh: 先明确双方各要什么、能给什么、不能接受什么，再让每轮对白回应上一轮的条件。新信息、拒绝和让步要改变可选方案；结果可以是有限成交、暂停或谈崩。对方说了同意才算达成这一项，后续实际执行了多少也要单独写，不用一句主角宣言代替全部过程。
answer.en: Define what each side wants, can offer, and cannot accept. Make each reply address the previous condition. New information, refusals, and concessions should alter the options. The result may be a limited agreement, pause, or failure. Show acceptance before treating a term as settled, and distinguish subsequent action from the agreement. A protagonist’s declaration cannot perform the entire exchange.

heading.zh: 写目标，也写对方为什么不能照办
heading.en: Give Both Parties Goals and Limits

body.zh:
争吵可以围绕过去的委屈，谈判更集中于下一步怎样安排。两者可以在同一场戏里交织，但本场若要谈一笔交换，就先弄清资源、权限和条件。

| 人物 | 场前要弄清的事 |
|---|---|
| 提议方 | 想得到什么；能交换什么；若不成，接下来有什么可行选择 |
| 回应方 | 为什么考虑这笔交换；为什么会拒绝；实际有权承诺到哪一步 |
| 双方 | 哪些条件已知、哪些只是猜测；这次可以谈妥哪一部分 |

这是组合源方法的编辑表，不是原生谈判算法。角色未必把真实目的全部说出，但作者应当知道他们在保护什么。不要把提议方的需求当成对方必须满足的理由，也不要为了让主角赢，临时让对方放弃已经明确的限制。
body.en:
An argument may concern old resentment; a negotiation focuses on the next arrangement. They can coexist, but a scene about an exchange first needs resources, authority, and terms.

| Party | Establish before the scene |
|---|---|
| Proposer | Desired result, available offer, and feasible next choice if refused. |
| Responder | Reason to consider it, reason to refuse, and actual authority to promise. |
| Both | Known terms versus guesses and the portion this conversation could settle. |

This is an editorial combination of source methods, not a native negotiation algorithm. Characters need not disclose every motive, but the author should understand what they protect. One person’s need does not oblige the other to meet it. Do not discard an established limit merely to make the protagonist win.

heading.zh: 让每轮回应改变条件或理解
heading.en: Let Each Response Change the Terms or Understanding

body.zh:
一轮可以是提出需求→对方指出限制→缩小范围或改变交换→对方接受、拒绝或再加条件。这是可选的组织方式，不必每场严格四轮。

情绪也要承接。例如“你以前就答应过”会让对方开始核旧承诺；“我不要求你现在开工”回应的是档期限制。只反复说“你必须帮我”，而对方反复说“不可能”，如果没有新的关系体验或条件变化，就考虑压缩。

源方法把可见交换和战略让步作为保留人物选择的办法。让出一部分时间、资源或聚光灯可以换来更重要的机会，不等于主角输了。另一方也可以有合理收益。对白长短、直接说明条件或保留潜台词，按本书文风决定，不能用“短句者必胜”判定结果。
body.en:
One possible sequence is a request, a stated limit, a smaller scope or changed exchange, then acceptance, refusal, or another condition. It is an option rather than a compulsory four-round formula.

Feeling should connect too. “You promised before” prompts a response to the old promise. “I’m not asking you to start now” answers a scheduling limit. Repeated demands and refusals without new terms or meaningful relationship experience may be compressed.

The sources use visible exchange and strategic concessions to retain agency. Giving up some time, resources, or attention may secure something more valuable without making the protagonist a loser. The other party may reasonably benefit too. Dialogue length, explicit conditions, and subtext follow the book’s voice; “the shorter speaker wins” cannot establish an outcome.

heading.zh: 原创场景：先谈检查，再谈修船
heading.en: Original Scene: Agree on an Inspection Before Repairs

body.zh:
设定：季禾的旧渡船停在岸边，她希望修船铺尽快处理。铺主周师傅可以安排自己的检查时段，但已有两条船的修理承诺；季禾知道缺少一枚固定销，却不知道内部还坏了什么。作者选定本场只谈检查，价钱和修理时间留到检查后，不假设口头同意就能航行。

> “今天能给我修上吗？”季禾问。
>
> 周师傅指了指台架上的船。“这两条先来，已经答应明天交。不能让它们给你腾位。”
>
> “我不是要你停它们。我想先知道坏到哪一步。只缺一个销，还是里面也裂了？”
>
> “没看不能给你这个保证。”
>
> 季禾把带来的固定销放在桌边。“那先检查，修不修等检查完再定。我把船边堆的网收开，六点以后你过来能直接看。”
>
> “七点，”他说，“我先把这两条今天的活做完。今晚只查，不拆开修。查完告诉你需要什么；明天开不开工，现在不能答应。”
>
> “七点，只检查。你看完说清哪些是查到的，哪些还得拆才知道。”季禾把固定销收回，“那我去收网。”
>
> 七点前，她搬开船边的网。周师傅按时到了，查看能看见的部位，指出固定孔已经变形；里面的连接仍需拆开检查。他把查到的地方指给季禾看，没有当场宣布整船已经能修好。
>
> “先把你看到的写给我，”季禾说，“要拆和要换的，明天再谈。”周师傅记下检查结果交给她，收起工具。

这是虚构创作例。季禾得到的是当晚检查和一份有限结果，周师傅保留已有工作承诺；接下来修不修、多少钱、何时完工仍没有谈定。读者看到收网、到场、检查和交记录，不能据此推定已经修船或确认航行安全。
body.en:
Setup: Ji’s old ferry is moored ashore. She wants a repair shop to act quickly. Zhou controls his inspection schedule but has promised repairs on two other boats. Ji knows a retaining pin is missing; she does not know the internal damage. The author chooses an inspection agreement, leaving price and repair time for later.

> “Can you repair it today?” Ji asked.
>
> Zhou pointed at the boats on the stands. “These came first. I promised them tomorrow. They can’t give up their places for yours.”
>
> “I’m not asking you to stop them. I want to know how bad it is. Just the pin, or something cracked inside?”
>
> “I can’t promise without looking.”
>
> Ji placed the pin she had brought on the table. “Then inspect it first. We decide on repairs afterward. I’ll clear the nets beside the boat. After six you can get straight to it.”
>
> “Seven,” he said. “After today’s work on these. Inspection only tonight; no dismantling for repairs. I’ll tell you what’s needed. I can’t promise a start tomorrow.”
>
> “Seven. Inspection only. Tell me what you’ve seen and what you’d still need to open up to know.” Ji took the pin back. “I’ll clear the nets.”
>
> Before seven she moved the nets. Zhou arrived on time and inspected the accessible parts. He showed her a distorted retaining hole; the internal connection still needed dismantling to inspect. He did not announce that the whole boat could be repaired.
>
> “Write down what you’ve seen,” Ji said. “We’ll discuss opening it up and replacements tomorrow.” Zhou handed her his inspection notes and packed his tools.

This is a fictional writing example. Ji receives an evening inspection and limited findings; Zhou retains his existing commitments. Repair, price, and completion remain unsettled. Readers see clearing, arrival, inspection, and a handoff of notes—not a repaired boat or confirmation that it is safe to sail.

heading.zh: 看懂成交的范围，别把局部接受写成全赢
heading.en: Keep the Agreement’s Scope Visible

body.zh:
| 回合 | 实际变化 |
|---|---|
| 今天修船被拒 | 理由是既有承诺，不是铺主突然讨厌主角 |
| 季禾改求检查 | 缩小请求；收网使到场后可直接查看，但不让她取得插队修理权 |
| 周师傅给七点条件 | 明确只查、不拆修、明日开工未定 |
| 季禾回应接受 | 双方就这一项谈妥；固定销仍被她收回 |
| 晚间到场与交记录 | 本轮检查实际执行；内部情况和后续安排仍待谈 |

若本场需要谈崩，周师傅可以说今晚也没有时间，季禾选择换一家或等明日；这也是有效结果。若需要更大冲突，先给各方相应的关系、事实和限制，不把一句挖苦当成必需的高潮。
body.en:
| Exchange | Actual change |
|---|---|
| Today’s repair refused | Existing commitments explain refusal, rather than sudden hostility. |
| Ji requests inspection | Smaller scope; clearing access helps the visit without granting priority repairs. |
| Zhou offers seven | Inspection only, no repair dismantling, no promised start tomorrow. |
| Ji accepts | That limited arrangement is settled; she retains the pin. |
| Visit and notes | The inspection happens; internal condition and later arrangements remain open. |

For a failed negotiation, Zhou may refuse even tonight’s inspection and Ji may try another shop or wait. That is a valid outcome. Greater conflict needs supporting relationships, facts, and constraints; an insult is not a compulsory climax.

heading.zh: 三种谈判戏常见问题
heading.en: Repair Three Common Negotiation Problems

body.zh:
**只写主角讲条件，对方没回应：**补对方实际接受、提出限制或拒绝的回合。沉默可以有含义，但不默认等于全部同意。

**为了显聪明让对方突然变笨：**让改变条件有可理解的利益、新信息或缩小范围。聪明可以体现在准确识别“今晚只能检查”，而不是编出对方无法拒绝的神奇一句话。

**情绪只是攥拳和冷笑：**若气愤改变场面，就写撤回哪项提议、追问什么或暂停哪一步；若情绪只是人物的体验，可以直接写。不要每次强塞一个身体动作。

按既定剧情判断条件变化是否成立。人物可以被明确条件、新信息或可信回应影响，这不等于几句宣言就改掉全部信念。源参考的压制、短句和冲突升级都是表达选项，不能覆盖作者已经选定的平静协商。
body.en:
**Only the protagonist speaks terms:** add actual acceptance, a limit, or refusal. Silence may matter, but it does not automatically accept everything.

**Make the other party foolish to display cleverness:** motivate a change through understandable benefit, new information, or reduced scope. Recognizing that only an inspection is available can be intelligent without a magical irresistible sentence.

**Feeling is only clenched fists and sneers:** when anger changes the exchange, identify the withdrawn offer, question, or pause. When it is lived experience, direct emotion is available; do not require bodily gestures.

Evaluate changed terms against the chosen plot. Specific terms, credible replies, and new information may affect a choice without instantly replacing every belief. Source defaults for domination, short replies, or escalating conflict cannot override the author’s chosen calm negotiation.

q.zh: 谈判戏一定要主角赢吗？
q.en: Must the protagonist win a negotiation?

a.zh: 不一定。有限交换、暂缓和失败都可以推动故事或加深理解。写清本场人物真正争取到什么以及放弃什么，不把每次让步都当成失去主角高光。
a.en: No. Limited exchange, delay, and failure may move the story or deepen understanding. Show actual gains and concessions rather than treating every concession as lost agency.

q.zh: 条件说得清楚会不会没有潜台词？
q.en: Do explicit terms remove subtext?

a.zh: 不会。人物可以明确说七点只检查，同时把担心旧承诺被破坏留在语气和回应里。安排必须听得懂，隐藏目的可以另有层次。
a.en: No. A character can clearly say “inspection only at seven” while concern about old commitments shapes the response. Understandable arrangements and layered motives can coexist.

text.zh: 用 $story-long-write 检查这个虚构谈判场景。附双方目标、可交换条件、权限、已知事实和本场预定结果。找没有回应的条件、无理由让步和宣布胜利却未被接受的地方，按本书文风提出局部改法。保留各自选择，不用统一短句、侮辱或突然事故强迫成交。
text.en: Use $story-long-write to review this fictional negotiation with goals, exchangeable terms, authority, known facts, and the chosen outcome. Identify unanswered conditions, unjustified concessions, and declared victories that were never accepted. Suggest local changes within book style, preserving both parties’ choices without mandatory short replies, insults, or a sudden accident to force agreement.

label.zh: 各方议程与逐句回应
战略让步、可见交换与选择权
label.en: Strategic concessions, visible exchange, and agency

label.zh: 让情绪改变提议和选择
label.en: Feeling that changes offers and choices

label.zh: 谈话形式与事实边界

title.zh: 小说人物撒谎怎么写：真假信息、听者反应和后果
title.en: How to Write a Character Who Lies

seo_title.zh: 小说人物撒谎怎么写
seo_title.en: Write a Character Who Lies

description.zh: 先确定人物故意说错了哪项事实、为什么隐瞒，再写听者实际知道多少。附借书记录完整场面和谎言揭穿后的修法。
description.en: Define the deliberate falsehood and motive, then track what the listener actually knows. Includes a complete library exchange and repairs after discovery.

answer.zh: 先给作者自己一份真实发生的事，再确定人物故意说错或隐瞒哪部分、想保护什么。对白要回应听者的问题和双方关系，听者能否信、疑或揭穿，取决于已知信息和实际核对。不要靠避开目光、出汗或长篇解释就宣布撒谎；揭穿以后继续写回应与后果。
answer.en: Establish the underlying facts for yourself, then choose what the character deliberately falsifies or conceals and why. Shape replies around the listener’s questions and their relationship. Belief, suspicion, and discovery depend on available information and actual checking. Looking away, sweating, or speaking at length cannot by themselves establish a lie. After discovery, write the response and consequences.

heading.zh: 先分清撒谎、误记和没说完
heading.en: Distinguish a Lie from Error and Incomplete Disclosure

body.zh:
本页讨论人物知道某项事实，却故意给另一个人错误说法。记错时间、理解不同、误信消息，并不自动等于故意撒谎。说了部分真话而故意让人误解，也要具体看省略了什么、双方原来问的是什么。

先为作者写三行：

1. **真实事件：**昨天下午许闻把书借给了同事。
2. **人物说法：**今天对管理员说“书放在我家”。
3. **当前目的：**不想让同事被追问，也不想承认自己违背借阅约定。

动机让选择可理解，不等于虚报没有后果。角色之间的谎言也不必让叙述者一起骗读者：读者可以先看到真实事件，再看听者怎样回应；或按既定视角暂不知道真相，后面通过可回看的信息揭示。
body.en:
This page concerns a character who knows a fact but deliberately gives someone else a false account. Misremembering, interpreting differently, or trusting a false report does not automatically constitute deliberate lying. A partial truth intended to mislead needs a specific omission and conversational context.

Write three lines for yourself:

1. **Actual event:** yesterday Xu lent the book to a colleague.
2. **Stated account:** today he tells the librarian, “It’s at my home.”
3. **Present purpose:** protect the colleague from questions and avoid admitting a broken borrowing agreement.

A motive makes the choice understandable without removing consequences. A character’s lie need not make the narrator deceive readers too. Readers may see the actual event first and follow the listener’s response, or learn the truth later through fair, recoverable information within the chosen viewpoint.

heading.zh: 听者为什么相信或怀疑，要有来路
heading.en: Give Belief or Suspicion a Basis

body.zh:
听者可以因为既有信任先接受，也可以记得前后矛盾而追问，或因为没有材料而暂不判断。不要把作者知道的真相塞进听者脑中。

| 作者检查 | 应该写到什么程度 |
|---|---|
| 听者有哪些材料 | 已经听过的说法、看过的物件或实际记录；别凭空新增 |
| 这项材料能证明什么 | 出借条目可以与“书在家”冲突，不一定证明所有去向和隐藏目的 |
| 人物怎样回应 | 接受、问一句、暂放、实际核对或拒绝继续；看关系与本场需要 |

眼神、停顿、紧张和话多都可以写成人物体验，但不能单独证明撒谎。**“谁都看得出他在撒谎”**若只是作者替所有人下结论，会抹掉各人的信息差。作者明确选择评论型叙述者时可有判断语气，仍不能无依据让每个人都获得真相。
body.en:
A listener may provisionally accept an account because of trust, question a remembered contradiction, or suspend judgment without evidence. Do not transfer the author’s knowledge into the listener’s mind.

| Editorial question | What to establish |
|---|---|
| Available material | Accounts, objects, or records the listener actually encountered; no invented evidence. |
| What it establishes | A loan entry may contradict “at home” without proving every destination or hidden motive. |
| Actual response | Acceptance, a question, a pause, checking, or refusal to continue, shaped by the relationship and scene. |

Gaze, pauses, nerves, and verbosity may express experience but cannot independently prove lying. “Everyone could tell he was lying” may erase the different information each person has. A deliberately commenting narrator can judge while still preserving how characters actually acquire the truth.

heading.zh: 原创片段：一句“在家”怎样被查到
heading.en: Original Passage: Checking “It’s at Home”

body.zh:
设定：管理员林姐管理一间单位阅览室。借阅约定不允许私下转借，许闻明知这一条，仍把书借给同事唐夏；后来他当面写过一条转借记录交给林姐，自己也记得写过。唐夏已告诉许闻书仍在她那里，今天会带来。林姐有权查阅她管理的记录，没有见过那次实际交接。作者选定读者先知道真实事件。**本例写的是明知留下记录、仍逃避眼前追问的失败谎言；不是示范高明骗术，也不要求所有撒谎人物都犯这种错。**以下是本页原创示范：

> 昨天，许闻把书交给唐夏，说好今天还。午休前她发消息：“还在我这里，下班带来。”他看过，没有催她。
>
> 林姐问书能不能今天归还。
>
> “在我家，晚上拿来。”许闻说。
>
> 林姐翻到他昨天交的那张记录，放在桌上。“这里写借给唐夏。是你写的吗？”
>
> “是。”
>
> “后来收回来了吗？”
>
> 许闻看着自己的签名。他知道没有。“没收回来。她说今天下班带来。我刚才怕你追着问她，就说在家。”
>
> “我先问的是书能不能归还，”林姐说，“位置写错，我就没法按实情安排。今天由你交回；没拿到，就告诉我没拿到，别再说在家。”
>
> 许闻点头。“好。她给我以后，我再拿来；如果没拿到，我先给你消息。”
>
> 下班时唐夏实际把书交给他。他带到阅览室，林姐核对书名和借阅编号，接收后记下归还。许闻又把先前“在家”的说法更正为当天仍在唐夏手中。

谎言被查的是明确位置，记录和追问没有读出他的全部心理；他在回应中自己说出了害怕追问的理由。林姐要求实际交还与如实说明，不因此获得唐夏更多私事，也没有说“以后我都相信你”。归还完成解决这本书的去向，未自动解决信任。
body.en:
Setup: Lin manages a workplace reading room. Private relending is prohibited. Xu knows this but lends a book to Tang. He later writes a relending note for Lin and remembers doing so. Tang has told him she still has the book and will bring it today. Lin can inspect records she manages but did not witness the handoff. The author lets readers know the truth first. **This is a failed lie: Xu avoids the immediate question despite knowing his own note exists. It is not expert deception or a mistake required of every lying character.** This is an original demonstration:

> Yesterday Xu handed Tang the book, agreeing she would return it today. Before lunch she messaged, “Still with me. I’ll bring it after work.” He read it without pressing her.
>
> Lin asked whether the book could return today.
>
> “It’s at home. I’ll bring it tonight,” Xu said.
>
> Lin found yesterday’s note and put it on the desk. “This says you lent it to Tang. Did you write it?”
>
> “Yes.”
>
> “Have you got it back since?”
>
> Xu looked at his signature. He knew he had not. “No. She says she’ll bring it after work. I was afraid you’d question her, so I said it was home.”
>
> “I asked whether it could return,” Lin said. “The wrong location stops me arranging things accurately. Bring it back yourself today. If you don’t get it, tell me that. Don’t say it’s home.”
>
> Xu nodded. “All right. I’ll bring it once she gives it to me. If she doesn’t, I’ll message you first.”
>
> After work Tang actually handed him the book. He brought it to the reading room. Lin checked the title and loan number, accepted it, and recorded the return. Xu also corrected his earlier account: it had still been with Tang that day.

The discovery concerns a specific location. A record and a question do not reveal every motive; Xu supplies his explanation in his response. Lin requires return and accurate reporting without acquiring Tang’s private affairs or promising permanent trust. The completed return resolves this book’s whereabouts, not the entire relationship.

heading.zh: 让人物有选择，不把揭穿写成全知
heading.en: Give the Character a Choice Without Omniscient Discovery

body.zh:
| 节点 | 事实与选择 |
|---|---|
| 说“在家”前 | 许闻读过唐夏消息，知道书不在家，因此是故意虚报而非记错 |
| 林姐拿出旧记录 | 只知道昨天记过转借，还要问是否收回；没有直接宣布当前仍在唐夏处 |
| 许闻承认没收回 | 实际承认与解释发生，林姐才获得这项当前说法；解释是否完整仍可待后文 |
| 答应归还 | 是承诺；唐夏实际交书、许闻实际送回、管理员核收才完成 |

作者若要他继续圆谎，可选“昨天借了，后来收回了”，但要写清这会怎样碰到唐夏的当前消息、为什么他选择冒更大风险。不能让他忘记自己刚写过记录，只为制造反转。若没有这条记录，就找现有的核验途径或让听者暂不能揭穿；不为表格临时造证据。
body.en:
| Point | Fact and choice |
|---|---|
| Before “at home” | Xu read Tang’s message and knows it is elsewhere: deliberate falsehood, not faulty memory. |
| Lin produces the note | It records yesterday’s relending. She still asks about return instead of asserting present possession. |
| Xu admits no return | The admission and explanation occur; Lin now has his current account. Its completeness can remain open. |
| Promise to return | A commitment until Tang hands it over, Xu delivers it, and Lin checks and accepts it. |

For a continuing lie, he might claim he already got it back. Then show how that encounters Tang’s current message and why he risks a larger falsehood. Do not make him forget his own recent note merely to create a twist. Without that note, use an existing check or let the listener remain unable to expose him instead of inventing evidence for a worksheet.

heading.zh: 撒谎对白写得假，先改哪几处
heading.en: Repair an Unconvincing Lie

body.zh:
**全靠结巴、移开目光或解释太多：**先看具体说法怎样回应当前问题。人物可以说得流畅，也可以紧张；身体表现由人物与场合决定，不用作统一测谎标志。

**撒谎没有目的：**明确他在这一刻保护什么。动机可以是怕丢脸、怕问及别人、想逃责任或维持一种自我形象；不必每次都有宏大阴谋，也不必把动机全写成台词。

**别人一问就自动全招：**若人物选择承认，给当前压力、关系和证据一条可理解的路径；若仍拒绝承认，允许继续僵持。不是每个谎言都要立刻揭穿。

**揭穿后只留一句“他后悔了”：**按本场需要写具体回应、更正、弥补、拒绝或余波。道歉不保证对方原谅，完成一件补救不等于一切恢复。读者可以理解他的害怕，同时看到位置虚报确实给安排带来问题。
body.en:
**Only stammering, looking away, or overexplaining:** examine how the false account answers the actual question. A liar may be fluent or nervous; bodily expression belongs to the character and occasion, not a universal detection code.

**No purpose:** identify what the character protects now—face, someone else, freedom from responsibility, or a self-image. A grand conspiracy is unnecessary, and motives need not all become spoken lines.

**One question triggers a full confession:** make admission understandable through the present pressure, relationship, and evidence. If the character refuses, allow the impasse. Not every lie needs immediate discovery.

**Only “he regretted it” afterward:** include the response, correction, repair, refusal, or aftermath this scene needs. Apology does not guarantee forgiveness; one repair does not restore everything. Readers can understand his fear while seeing that false location information disrupted arrangements.

q.zh: 读者先知道谎言，会失去悬念吗？
q.en: Does showing readers the lie first remove suspense?

a.zh: 不一定。悬念可以变成听者会不会发现、人物是否继续隐瞒、真相到来会怎样影响关系。先知与后知是不同体验，按本书视角和预定效果选择。
a.en: No. Readers may wait to see whether the listener discovers it, the speaker continues, or the truth changes the relationship. Earlier and later knowledge create different experiences; choose by viewpoint and intended effect.

q.zh: 撒谎角色就是不可靠叙述者吗？
q.en: Is a lying character an unreliable narrator?

a.zh: 不一定。角色可以只对另一个人撒谎，而叙述仍如实呈现事件。不可靠叙述者涉及读者从叙述中得到怎样的偏差，两个问题可重叠，但不应混为一篇同义教程。
a.en: No. A character may lie to another person while the narrative presents events accurately. Unreliable narration concerns distortions in the reader’s account; the two can overlap without being identical.

text.zh: 用 $story-long-write 检查这段人物撒谎的对白。附真实事件、人物知道什么、故意改变的说法、动机、听者已有证据与预定揭露位置。找不可能知道的信息、作者替听者断言和没有后果的揭穿；按本书文风局部修订，不新增证明、自动原谅或通用测谎动作。
text.en: Use $story-long-write to review this lying character’s dialogue. Include actual events, the speaker’s knowledge, deliberate falsehood, motive, listener’s existing evidence, and the intended reveal. Find impossible knowledge, narrator-imposed conclusions, and discoveries without response. Revise locally within book style without inventing proof, automatic forgiveness, or generic lie-detection gestures.

label.zh: 真实动机、说法与谈话议程
避免叙述者替人物点破
误导与公平信息
叙述选择与已知事实

title.zh: 叙事游戏道具怎么设计：获得、使用和归属要真的生效
title.en: How to Design Items for a Story Game

seo_title.zh: 叙事游戏道具怎么设计
seo_title.en: Design Items for a Story Game

description.zh: 让道具改变可用行动，写清取得、使用、消耗和交还。附借手电的完整纸面路径、失败分支与存档核对。
description.en: Make items affect available actions. Includes a complete borrowed-flashlight design, failed uses, ownership, and save-state checks.

answer.zh: 先确定道具让玩家能做什么，再写谁持有、怎样获得、使用前要满足什么、用后是否消耗或转交，以及世界怎样回应。请求不等于取得，使用工具不必销毁工具，得到线索也不等于知道全部真相。只保留会改变行动、体验或后续读取的道具，不为背包数量增加无用物件。
answer.en: Choose what an item lets the player do, then define ownership, acquisition, prerequisites, consumption or transfer, and feedback. Requesting is not acquiring; using a tool need not destroy it; finding a clue does not reveal everything. Keep items with a role in actions, experience, or later state rather than filling an inventory for its own sake.

heading.zh: 先写用途，再决定要不要一个背包系统
heading.en: Choose the Function Before an Inventory System

body.zh:
原作里有信物、工具、证物，不代表改编时都要变成可点击道具。判断玩家拿到它以后，哪项行动、体验或后续回应会改变。

一把钥匙可改变可达空间，一件工具可改变观察方式，一封信可改变谁获得信息。只供观赏的纪念物也可以保留为叙事展示，不必包装成万能工具或数值奖励。

源世界设计方法要求必要系统参与核心决策，道具可以只存在于一小段场景中。若本关只借一支手电，用当前持物提示就可能足够；不必为它新增格子、负重、合成和装备栏。确实需要整理多件物品时，再让界面帮助玩家辨认用途与归属。
body.en:
An original novel’s keepsakes, tools, and evidence need not all become clickable items. Ask which action, experience, or later response changes when the player gets one.

A key can change access, a tool can change observation, and a letter can change who receives information. A keepsake may remain a narrative display without becoming a universal tool or numerical reward.

The world-design method makes systems serve core decisions. An item can belong to a single scene. One borrowed flashlight may need only a held-item indication rather than slots, weight, crafting, and equipment screens. A larger collection can justify an interface that clarifies uses and ownership.

heading.zh: 写一张取得与使用说明
heading.en: Write an Acquisition and Use Note

body.zh:
| 项目 | 需要决定的事 |
|---|---|
| 初始归属 | 在谁手里或什么位置；可见不等于玩家已经持有 |
| 取得 | 谁允许、玩家做什么、何时实际转交 |
| 使用 | 对什么有效、需什么权限或位置、失败时改变什么 |
| 使用后 | 保留、消耗、变成另一物件或交给别人；不混用几种结果 |
| 反馈与后续 | 哪项变化让玩家看见，后面在哪里读取 |

这是本页的组合编辑表，不是技能原生文件格式。消耗品要选定扣除时点：前置不满足而不能开始时是否不扣，开始后失败是否已消耗，按本作规则写清。耐用工具用过后通常仍可持有，本例也如此；这不是禁止其他作品设计损坏或耐久。
body.en:
| Field | Decision |
|---|---|
| Initial ownership | Holder or location; visibility does not give possession. |
| Acquisition | Permission, player action, and actual handoff point. |
| Use | Valid targets, permissions or positions, and effects of failure. |
| After use | Retain, consume, transform, or transfer; distinguish these outcomes. |
| Feedback and later read | Visible change and where subsequent content reads it. |

This is a combined editorial worksheet, not a native skill format. Choose when consumables are spent, including refused starts and failed attempts after use begins. A reusable tool remains held in this example; other games may deliberately implement damage or durability.

heading.zh: 完整纸面路径：借手电查看展品
heading.en: Complete Paper Path: Borrowing a Flashlight

body.zh:
原创设计《闭馆前的画册》：玩家想核对展品上被阴影挡住的编号。管理员有一支手电，可以借给玩家在本展厅使用；玩家已有查看这件展品的权限，不能因此进入办公室。编号直接支持的是展品编号，不证明作者、真伪或所有权。

**初始界面：**展品编号在普通光下看不清；桌上可见手电，但持物提示为空。玩家可问管理员借用，或先看清楚处的其他展品。下面选择借用路线：

> 玩家选择“借手电看这件展品”。
>
> 管理员说：“可以，在展厅用，走前还给我。”
>
> 玩家选择“接过手电”，管理员实际递出。持物提示变为“借用手电”。
>
> 玩家对该展品选择“用手电看编号”。光照到标签，显示“B7”；当前发现中记录“看见这件展品编号B7”。手电仍在玩家手里。
>
> 玩家回到桌边选择“归还手电”。管理员实际接回，持物提示清空；发现记录仍保留。管理员说：“收到了。”

| 此刻再操作 | 规则与反馈 |
|---|---|
| 对同件展品再次照明 | 手电仍持有时可重复观察；不多生成一份编号，不把手电扣成零件 |
| 持手电点击办公室门 | 没有进入权限；手电不能代替许可，归属不变 |
| 归还后再照标签 | 提示“手电已归还，可重新询问借用”；本次不能执行，不悄悄从旧按钮复制一支 |
| 带着B7继续查目录 | 可以读取已见编号；不知道的作者与去向仍需下一步核对 |

这是未构建、未试玩的设计片段。规则路径可查归属与重复效果，不能证明实际灯光、点击命中或玩家是否注意到提示。
body.en:
Original design, “The Album Before Closing”: the player wants to read an exhibit number obscured by shadow. A keeper can lend a flashlight for this gallery. The player already has permission to inspect this exhibit, not enter the office. Its number establishes neither authorship, authenticity, nor ownership.

**Initial view:** the label is unreadable in ordinary light. A flashlight is visible on the desk, but the held-item indicator is empty. The player may ask to borrow it or inspect other legible exhibits. Here is the borrowing path:

> Player: “Borrow the flashlight to inspect this exhibit.”
>
> Keeper: “Yes. Use it in the gallery and return it before leaving.”
>
> The player selects “Take the flashlight”; the keeper actually hands it over. The indicator reads “Borrowed flashlight.”
>
> At the exhibit the player selects “Light the number.” The label reveals “B7,” and the discovery records this exhibit’s visible number. The flashlight remains held.
>
> At the desk the player selects “Return the flashlight.” The keeper takes it, the held-item indicator clears, and the discovery remains. “Received,” says the keeper.

| Subsequent action | Rule and feedback |
|---|---|
| Illuminate again | While held, observation may repeat without duplicating the number or consuming the tool. |
| Click office door while holding it | Access is absent; the tool cannot substitute for permission. Ownership remains. |
| Illuminate after returning it | “Flashlight returned; ask to borrow it again.” No execution or copy from a stale button. |
| Search catalog with B7 | Read the known number; authorship and destination still need checking. |

This design is unbuilt and untested with players. Its path checks ownership and repeat effects, not actual lighting, click targets, or attention to feedback.

heading.zh: 存档与交还后，别让道具重新长出来
heading.en: Prevent Items Reappearing After Loading or Return

body.zh:
道具当前在谁手里，与曾经借过或曾经观察到什么，是不同记录。归还后的存档应保留管理员持有手电、玩家记得B7；不能只保存“借用成功”就恢复成玩家仍有手电。

一次性复印券则需要另一种规则：如果本作规定成功复印才消耗，资格检查失败就保留券；成功后扣一张，下一次读取实际剩余数量。不要因为输出了一句“复印好了”，就默认已经生成副本和消费券。

实现可以用现有游戏状态机，不要求为了文章的表格再造一套文件。画面动画、背包图标和角色对白读取已确认结果，不能各自决定物件突然属于谁。
body.en:
Current possession differs from borrowing history and discoveries. A post-return save should keep the flashlight with the keeper and B7 known to the player. Saving only “borrowing succeeded” cannot restore possession.

A one-use copying voucher needs a different rule. If consumed on successful copying, a refused prerequisite check retains it; success spends one, and the next attempt reads the remaining count. A line saying “copied” does not by itself create a copy or spend the voucher.

Use an existing state machine when available rather than creating files to imitate this worksheet. Animation, inventory icons, and dialogue read confirmed results; they cannot independently decide ownership.

heading.zh: 道具没作用或处处能用，怎样修
heading.en: Repair Useless or Universally Effective Items

body.zh:
**拿到后只有弹一句说明：**先找它应该改变的可用行动或体验。纯纪念物可按叙事展示处理，不硬塞到工具栏。

**任何地方点击都成功：**明确可用对象和条件。手电只改变照明，不替代钥匙、许可或证据解释。

**归还了还显示持有：**修当前归属与界面读取，保留确实发生过的观察；不要删掉所有历史来补一个图标。

**重复使用反复给奖励：**决定重复观察、重复取得和一次性消耗各自的效果。重放原失败路径，再走一条相邻反例；新规则改了旧存档含义时，应迁移或明确拒绝旧版本。具体乐趣和理解仍由实际试玩观察。
body.en:
**Acquisition only shows a description:** identify the intended change to action or experience. A keepsake may remain narrative display without a tool slot.

**Every target succeeds:** define targets and conditions. Illumination does not replace keys, permission, or interpretation.

**Returned item still appears held:** repair current ownership and its display while retaining real observations. Do not erase history to fix an icon.

**Repeated use repeats rewards:** distinguish repeat observation, repeat acquisition, and consumption. Replay the failure and an adjacent counterexample. Migrate or explicitly reject old saves when rules change their meaning. Observe understanding and enjoyment in actual play.

q.zh: 每个道具都要消耗或升级吗？
q.en: Must every item be consumed or upgraded?

a.zh: 不用。耐用工具、证物、一次性材料和纪念物可有不同用途。只在消耗、耐久或升级会改变本作决策时加入这些系统。
a.en: No. Reusable tools, evidence, consumables, and keepsakes may work differently. Add consumption, durability, or upgrades when they affect this game’s decisions.

q.zh: 道具说明能代替实际使用反馈吗？
q.en: Can an item description replace feedback from use?

a.zh: 不能完全代替。说明帮助理解用途，实际使用仍要呈现本次成功、拒绝或局部效果；尤其交给别人后，当前持有者和后续行动要跟着变化。
a.en: Not fully. A description helps explain use, but action should show success, refusal, or a partial effect. Transfers must change current possession and subsequent actions.

text.zh: 用 $game-world-design 设计本关道具。附当前场景、角色权限和核心动作。逐项写初始归属、取得条件、可用对象、使用效果、消耗或交还及后续读取；给一条正常路径和一条重复使用/归还后使用的反例。不要自动增加库存、合成或耐久系统，不把纸面路径当已试玩。
text.en: Use $game-world-design to design this section’s items from the scene, permissions, and core actions. Specify initial ownership, acquisition, valid targets, effects, consumption or return, and later reads. Include a normal path and a repeated-use or post-return counterexample. Do not add inventory, crafting, or durability systems automatically or report a paper design as a playtest.

label.zh: 动作前置、物件变化与系统取舍
label.en: Action prerequisites, item changes, and system scope

label.zh: 物件去向与后续回读
归属提交、载入与表现边界
label.en: Committed ownership, loading, and presentation limits

title.zh: 互动游戏选项锁定怎么设计：说明缺少条件，别提前揭底
title.en: How to Design Locked Options in a Story Game

seo_title.zh: 互动游戏选项锁定怎么设计
seo_title.en: Design Locked Options in a Story Game

description.zh: 给锁定选项明确的当前原因和可行下一步，保留未知路线。附许可与钥匙完整解锁示例、过期状态和反例检查。
description.en: Explain current requirements without exposing unknown routes. Includes a permission-and-key example, stale-state handling, and counterchecks.

answer.zh: 先确定玩家已经知道这项行动存在，再决定显示锁定原因还是暂不展示。已知限制应说明当前缺哪条条件和下一步能做什么；未知秘密不要写在灰色按钮里。解锁读取实际许可、持物或进度，点击时再核对当前状态，不能靠换一行文案就算条件满足。
answer.en: First determine whether the player knows the action exists, then choose a visible requirement or temporary omission. Explain known limitations and a feasible next step without revealing secrets in disabled labels. Unlock from actual permission, possession, or progress; recheck current state on selection. A changed label cannot satisfy a rule.

heading.zh: 先决定显示锁定，还是暂时不出现
heading.en: Choose Visible Requirements or Temporary Omission

body.zh:
玩家已经看见库房、听说能申请查看，锁定提示可解释为什么现在进不了。玩家还不知道有地下密室，按钮“进入密室：尚未发现”则提前说出了秘密。

| 情况 | 本页建议 |
|---|---|
| 行动与条件是已知规则 | 显示行动、当前缺口和可做的下一步 |
| 行动存在本身是秘密 | 等玩家通过既定信息得知再呈现，不用锁图标剧透 |
| 当前没有任何可行取得路径 | 说明暂不可用或按本书设计隐藏，别承诺必能解锁 |

这不是所有游戏的统一可见规则。如果作品明确把路线预览作为玩法，可以选择适度预告；要与玩家承诺一致，而不是无意暴露完整反转。可读的锁定提示与让角色提前知情是两回事。
body.en:
If players see a storeroom and hear that visits can be requested, a requirement can explain why entry is unavailable. “Enter secret basement: undiscovered” reveals a room they do not yet know exists.

| Situation | Suggested presentation |
|---|---|
| Action and requirement are known | Show the action, current gap, and available next step. |
| Existence is secret | Present it after the intended discovery instead of spoiling it with a lock icon. |
| No current way to qualify | State present unavailability or omit it by design; do not promise eventual access. |

This is not universal. A game deliberately built around route previews may offer controlled advance information consistent with its promise. A readable requirement does not automatically give story knowledge to characters.

heading.zh: 锁定提示要说当前缺口，不预告全部后果
heading.en: Explain the Present Gap, Not the Whole Outcome

body.zh:
“条件不足”没有帮助；“需要值班员同意”让玩家知道去问谁。若还缺钥匙，分别显示，别让玩家拿到钥匙后误以为权限也自动成立。

提示可以在按钮旁或选择后的拒绝反馈里，关键是必要信息在玩家需要时可见、语义一致。已知成本应在行动前出现；隐藏人物动机和结局不必一并公布。

源方法将按钮、代价提示与人物回应分工。避免每行重复完整任务历史，把当前缺口贴在受影响行动旁。原因不只有道具或数值，还可以是人物未在场、已有承诺冲突、位置不对或当前不愿接受。
body.en:
“Requirements unmet” offers little help; “Duty keeper’s permission needed” identifies whom to ask. Show a missing key separately so obtaining it does not imply permission.

A nearby note or a response to an attempted action can explain the limit. Necessary information should appear when needed and remain consistent. Disclose known costs before action without publishing hidden motives or endings.

The sources separate button, cost prompt, and character response. Put the present gap beside its action instead of repeating the whole quest history. Requirements may concern presence, conflicting commitments, location, or willingness as well as items and numbers.

heading.zh: 原创示例：获准之后，还要真正拿到钥匙
heading.en: Original Example: Permission Still Requires a Key

body.zh:
纸面游戏《库房访客》：门旁已贴规则“申请查看工具架，获准后领取本次钥匙”。玩家从这里知道可申请，当前没有许可或钥匙。值班员能批准本次工具架查看；档案区不在许可内。门在尝试进入时检查本次许可与玩家持钥匙两项，失败不消耗物件、不改变位置。

| 状态与玩家动作 | 界面和人物实际回应 |
|---|---|
| 初到门前 | “进入工具架区”暂不可执行；旁注“先向值班员申请，获准后领钥匙” |
| 请求查看工具架 | 值班员实际回应“可以，只看工具架，档案区不开放”；记录本次许可，仍提示“尚未领取钥匙” |
| 选择领取钥匙 | 值班员实际递给玩家；持物更新后，进入选项可用 |
| 选择进入 | 当前许可和持钥匙均有效，位置变为工具架区；没有自动打开档案区或完成全部查找 |
| 出来后交还钥匙 | 值班员接回，持物清空；再进提示“本次钥匙已交还，需重新领取” |

在本例中，许可只对本次来访有效，离开库房场景后结束；同一次来访中归还再领钥匙是否允许，由作者明确选择，这里允许向仍在场的值班员再次领取。不要因为最后一行提到“重新领取”，就在所有存档中免费复制钥匙。

**完整走读：**玩家先看到公开规则，申请并听到同意，再选领取并获得钥匙，进入工具架区；检查结束后出门交还，尝试旧“进入”按钮被拒，最后离开结束本次来访。每一步用当前状态判断，按钮之前出现过不等于永远有效。

以上是原创设计路径，不是已运行的产品或试玩录像。实际界面还要检查不可点击时能否读到原因、可用状态怎样被辨认以及反馈是否挡住下一步。
body.en:
Paper design, “The Storeroom Visitor”: a sign says, “Request a visit to the tool shelves; collect this visit’s key after approval.” The player learns the action here and initially has neither permission nor key. The duty keeper can authorize the shelves, not the archive area. Entry checks both current permission and possession; refusal spends nothing and changes no location.

| State, action | Response |
|---|---|
| First arrival | Entry unavailable; “Ask the keeper, then collect the key after approval.” |
| Request shelf visit | Keeper says, “Yes, shelves only; archives closed.” Permission is recorded; key still missing. |
| Collect key | Keeper actually hands it over; possession changes and entry becomes available. |
| Enter | Current permission and held key pass; location becomes the shelf area, not archives or a completed search. |
| Exit and return key | Keeper receives it; possession clears. Re-entry requires collecting it again. |

Permission ends when leaving the storeroom scene at the end of this visit. The author chooses that collecting again during the same visit is allowed from the keeper still present. A prompt mentioning recollection cannot freely duplicate keys in every save.

**Complete walkthrough:** read the public rule, request and receive approval, collect the key, enter, inspect, exit and return it, attempt the old entry option and receive refusal, then leave to end the visit. Each step reads current state; a once-visible button is not permanently valid.

This is an original design path, not a running product or playtest recording. Check whether actual players can read unavailable-action reasons, recognize availability, and proceed after feedback.

heading.zh: 条件变化以后，旧选项也必须重新检查
heading.en: Recheck an Option After Conditions Change

body.zh:
渲染出来时符合条件，点击时可能已不符合：钥匙交还、承诺撤销、人物离场或本次许可到期。表现层不能绕过规则；检查失败时保留应保留的状态，再给当前原因。

读档也要恢复当前来访、许可范围与持物，不能凭“曾获准”替代本次有效许可。若改了许可含义，说明旧存档迁移或明确失效，不让同一个旧记录突然扩大到档案区。

秘密选项同样如此。玩家从某条分支发现的事，另一条没有发现的路线不应仅因共享场景就出现同样标签。世界事实存在、玩家已经知道、人物是否相信，分别判断。
body.en:
An option may qualify when rendered and fail when selected: a key returns, a commitment is withdrawn, a person leaves, or permission expires. Presentation cannot bypass the rules. Preserve the appropriate state after refusal and give the current reason.

Loading restores the visit, permission scope, and possession. “Once approved” does not mean valid now. If permission semantics change, migrate or explicitly invalidate old saves rather than expanding an old record to the archives.

Secret options need the same care. Discovery in one branch cannot leak through a shared scene into an undiscovered route. Distinguish an existing world fact, player knowledge, and character belief.

heading.zh: 从四种反例查锁定设计
heading.en: Check Four Counterexamples

body.zh:
只有钥匙没有许可，进入应按本例规则拒绝；只有许可没有钥匙，也应指出缺物件；两项齐全可进入，但仍不能扩大到档案区；交还钥匙后点旧按钮，不能再进入或扣出负数道具。

若所有行动都锁着，给一个合法的询问、等待、离开或替代行动，按本场设计决定。不是每个限制都必须立即解除，但玩家应能理解为什么停在这里。

锁定提示过长时，保留当前必要条件，把完整任务史放到按需日志。若读者看提示就知道幕后人、全部路线或最终结局，退回当前知识。规则走读能发现泄露与错误放行；不能证明玩家一定觉得探索有趣。
body.en:
Key without permission must fail in this design; permission without key identifies the missing item; both allow entry but not archive access; a stale click after return cannot re-enter or produce negative item counts.

If everything is unavailable, offer a legal inquiry, wait, exit, or alternative by design. Every limit need not immediately disappear, but players should understand their position.

Keep essential current requirements near choices and full quest history in an optional log. If prompts expose culprits, entire routes, or endings, return to current knowledge. Rule walkthroughs detect disclosure and wrongful access, not whether exploration feels enjoyable.

q.zh: 所有锁定选项都应该显示吗？
q.en: Should every locked option remain visible?

a.zh: 不应该一律显示。已知规则可说明，未知秘密可以暂不呈现。路线预告若是本作明确玩法，也要控制信息量与角色知情边界。
a.en: No universal rule applies. Explain known requirements while withholding undiscovered secrets. Deliberate route previews still need controlled information and character knowledge boundaries.

q.zh: 条件满足后自动继续剧情可以吗？
q.en: May the story continue automatically after unlocking?

a.zh: 可以在本作明确选择的自动流程里这样设计。若原来承诺玩家自行选择进入，取得钥匙不应顺带替他进门、翻档案或提交证据；把自动动作范围写清。
a.en: Yes, in an explicitly chosen automatic flow. If entry is the player’s choice, receiving a key should not also enter, search archives, or submit evidence. Define the automatic scope.

text.zh: 用 $game-world-design 检查这些锁定选项。附玩家已知信息、行动前置、实际状态和可获得条件的路径。说明哪些限制可公开、哪些标签会剧透；给当前原因、可行下一步和满足条件后的真实动作。检查条件撤销、物件交还、旧界面点击和读档，不自动放行或泄露秘密。
text.en: Use $game-world-design to review locked options with player knowledge, prerequisites, actual state, and ways to satisfy requirements. Separate public limits from spoiler labels. Give a current reason, feasible next step, and actual unlocked action. Check revoked conditions, returned items, stale clicks, and loading without automatic access or secret disclosure.

label.zh: 行动前置、可预判信息与失败反馈
label.en: Prerequisites, foreseeable information, and failure feedback

label.zh: 隐藏因果与玩家当前知识
label.en: Hidden causality and current player knowledge

label.zh: 按钮、可见条件与提示分工
实际规则验证与状态提交

title.zh: 游戏开场教程怎么做：让玩家操作一次，再给下一步
title.en: How to Design a Game Opening Tutorial

seo_title.zh: 游戏开场教程怎么做
seo_title.en: Design a Game Opening Tutorial

description.zh: 先教一项本作核心动作，用可见依据、误操作和真实反馈建立理解。附投递任务完整首段设计与试玩观察表。
description.en: Teach one core action through visible information, a recoverable mistake, and feedback. Includes a complete opening delivery task and playtest questions.

answer.zh: 先让玩家知道眼前要完成什么，提供这次行动必需的依据，再让他亲手操作并看到结果。初次失误要说明原因与可改之处，完成后接一个需要再次使用所学的局面。不要先讲完整百科、全部系统和所有按键；教程长度跟随本作风险与玩家理解，不靠固定秒数判定成功。
answer.en: Give players a present goal and the evidence needed for the first action, then let them act and see its result. A first mistake should explain what happened and what can change. Follow completion with another use of the learned action. Avoid opening with every system, key, and lore detail. Length follows the game’s risks and player understanding, not a fixed number of seconds.

heading.zh: 先教当前动作，别先介绍全部系统
heading.en: Teach the Present Action Before the Whole System

body.zh:
“游戏背景是什么”“所有系统怎么用”“现在做什么”是不同问题。开场先给玩家身份、眼前目标和可操作对象一个足够短的锚点，然后教完成这一步需要的规则。

源方法要求首屏有主要焦点，并让核心动作、反馈和状态变化在同一节拍里闭合。动作可以是观察、选择回应、投递、摆放或移动，不要求所有改编游戏都先走路、战斗或打开背包。

教学可以融入人物请求、环境标记或简短提示。需要操作说明时直接说清，不必为了“沉浸”把必要信息藏起来；也不要让人物用一整段百科解释未来十个系统。
body.en:
Background, every system, and the present action answer different questions. Orient players to role, immediate goal, and an actionable object, then teach what this step needs.

The source calls for a primary opening focus and a complete action-feedback-state beat. The action may be observation, a reply, delivery, placement, or movement. Adaptations need not all begin with walking, combat, or inventory.

Use a character request, an environmental marker, or a short prompt. State necessary instructions clearly instead of hiding them for immersion, while avoiding encyclopedic dialogue about ten future systems.

heading.zh: 把初次操作写成一张完整教学卡
heading.en: Write a Complete First-Action Card

body.zh:
| 当前一步 | 设计内容 |
|---|---|
| 玩家目标 | 这一刻要完成哪件可观察的事 |
| 必要依据 | 操作前从哪里看见对象、条件或规则 |
| 玩家输入 | 点击、选择、移动或其他实际动作，不只读说明 |
| 成功反馈 | 世界怎样回应，什么状态确实变了 |
| 可恢复失误 | 失败原因、保留什么、下一次能改什么 |
| 下一步 | 哪里再次读取所学，而不是永久不再使用 |

这是本页的编辑卡。段数、按钮数与完成时长按游戏而定；不能用“已弹出教程”替代“玩家理解并能操作”。如果风险是手势、碰撞或空间阅读，要在目标平台原型里看实际输入，文本纸面稿只能查逻辑。
body.en:
| Present step | Design detail |
|---|---|
| Goal | An observable task now. |
| Needed evidence | Where the player sees objects, conditions, or rules before acting. |
| Input | Actual clicking, choice, movement, or another action beyond reading. |
| Success | World response and confirmed state change. |
| Recoverable mistake | Cause, retained state, and what can change next time. |
| Next use | A later read of the learned rule. |

This is an editorial card. Length, option count, and time follow the game. A displayed tutorial does not establish comprehension. Gesture, collision, and spatial risks need a prototype on the target platform; paper text checks logic.

heading.zh: 原创首段：先送一封信，再处理下一封
heading.en: Original Opening: One Delivery Before the Next

body.zh:
《驿站来信》是文字与选择主导的纸面改编例，核心动作是根据收件信息选择投递对象，并看对方实际是否接收。玩家是新来的递信员，先不讲整座镇的秘密、所有关系数值或全部工作日程。

**首屏局面：**“把这封库房信交给林姐。”信封上写“库房，林姐”；两个在场角色的名字和职责可见：林姐负责库房，方叔负责码头。当前只有这一封信，未投递；玩家可选“把库房信交给林姐”“把库房信交给方叔”或查看信封。按钮附近保留目标与收件信息。

**一条含误操作的完整路线：**

> 玩家先选交给方叔。
>
> 方叔看清地址：“库房的信不归我收。林姐就在柜台那边。”他没有接走信。
>
> 界面显示“未送出；仍持有库房信”，两项投递行动仍按当前状态可选。
>
> 玩家查看信封，改选交给林姐。
>
> 林姐核对收件名，接过并签收：“这封是我的，收到了。”
>
> 当前目标显示完成，信从玩家持物中移除；方叔没有因为第一次错误选择就获得信件内容。
>
> 林姐再交给玩家一封写着“码头，方叔”的信。玩家取得后出现第二项投递任务，这次不再重复完整说明，只保留信封信息与真实可执行的行动。

| 第二次操作 | 用同一条已学规则处理 |
|---|---|
| 交给方叔 | 他核收，信实际转交，第二任务完成 |
| 又交给林姐 | 她指出收件人不同且不接走；玩家仍可改投 |
| 只点击旧“库房信”行动 | 旧信已经送出，不能再次转交或多生成签收 |

玩家学到的是看信息→选择对象→核实际接收，第二封换对象来检验复用。误投不会暗中泄露内容或销毁信；本例选择了可恢复教学，其他作品若选择有代价失误，需要在行动前给相应依据。本段没有证明实际玩家已经理解，仍要构建后观察。
body.en:
“Letters at the Station” is an original paper adaptation led by text and choices. Its core action is choosing a recipient from delivery information and seeing whether they actually accept. The new courier does not begin with the town’s secrets, every relationship value, or the entire schedule.

**Opening:** “Deliver the storeroom letter to Lin.” The envelope names Lin and the storeroom. Two present characters have visible names and roles: Lin handles the storeroom; Fang handles the wharf. One letter remains undelivered. Actions are “Give the storeroom letter to Lin,” “Give it to Fang,” or inspect the envelope. Goal and recipient information stay near the choices.

**Complete path with a mistake:**

> The player offers it to Fang.
>
> He reads the address. “I don’t receive storeroom mail. Lin’s by the counter.” He does not take it.
>
> Feedback: “Not delivered; still holding the storeroom letter.” The delivery actions remain available according to state.
>
> The player inspects the envelope and selects Lin.
>
> Lin checks the recipient, takes it, and signs. “This one’s mine. Received.”
>
> The goal completes and possession clears. The wrong first choice did not reveal the letter’s contents to Fang.
>
> Lin hands over a new envelope addressed “Wharf, Fang.” After acquisition, a second task appears without repeating the full explanation; envelope information and valid actions remain.

| Second action | Same learned rule |
|---|---|
| Deliver to Fang | He checks and accepts; actual transfer completes this task. |
| Offer to Lin again | She identifies the different recipient and refuses; the player can redirect. |
| Select stale storeroom-letter action | That letter is gone; no duplicate transfer or receipt. |

The player practices reading information, choosing a recipient, and checking acceptance. A different recipient tests reuse. This design makes a first error recoverable without hidden disclosure or destruction. Games with costly mistakes need appropriate advance information. The paper path does not establish player comprehension; observe it after building.

heading.zh: 试玩时看玩家实际做了什么
heading.en: Observe What Players Actually Do

body.zh:
| 观察问题 | 有问题时先改什么 |
|---|---|
| 不知道目标在哪里 | 首屏焦点和当前目标表达 |
| 没看见收件信息就选 | 信息位置、行动旁依据；不是再弹一篇背景 |
| 误投后以为信已经丢失 | 真实持物反馈与可重试行动 |
| 第一封能送，第二封仍机械选同一人 | 是否理解收件规则；是否第二封信息清楚 |
| 说明遮住操作或必须先滚很久 | 拆短当前拍，长档案由玩家按需打开 |

可记录首次动作、误操作后的下一步和任务完成路径。完成一次可能是猜对，不能单独证明理解；拒收反馈被看见也不等于玩家理解所有剧情。真人感受、愿意继续玩和操作手感需要真实观察，不由自动化PASS替代。
body.en:
| Observation | First repair |
|---|---|
| Goal cannot be found | Opening focus and present goal. |
| Chooses without seeing address | Evidence placement near action, not another lore panel. |
| Thinks rejected delivery lost the letter | Accurate possession feedback and retry actions. |
| Always selects the first recipient | Understanding of the recipient rule and clarity of new information. |
| Instructions cover controls or require long scrolling | Shorten the present beat; make long records optional. |

Record first action, response after mistakes, and the completed path. One success may be a guess; seeing a refusal does not establish all story understanding. Feeling, willingness to continue, and control quality require actual observation rather than an automated PASS.

heading.zh: 教程过长、强制太多时，怎样删
heading.en: Shorten Long or Overbearing Tutorials

body.zh:
把未来才需要的规则推迟到首次有用时，保留这一拍的目标、依据、操作与反馈。已经证明理解的内容可以减少提示；新的对象、例外或操作仍可能需要说明，不一律取消。

若允许跳过，明确跳过后玩家位于哪里、持有什么、哪些教学事件没有发生。可以提供按需帮助，但不能声称玩家已经签收第一封信，除非设计明确选择自动完成并一致更新结果。

不要为了让教学显得有刺激，突然加入倒计时、敌人、货币和随机惩罚。先检验本作核心动作是否值得继续，再选择合适的压力。开场很短也可能不清楚，开场较长也可能有内容；具体判断来自本作体验和真实试玩。
body.en:
Defer future rules until useful while retaining this beat’s goal, evidence, input, and response. Reduce prompts after demonstrated understanding; new objects, exceptions, or controls may still need guidance.

If skipping is allowed, define position, possessions, and events that did not occur. Offer optional help without claiming a letter was received unless deliberate automatic completion updates results consistently.

Do not add timers, enemies, currency, and random punishment merely to make teaching exciting. Test whether the core action sustains interest before choosing pressure. A short opening may be unclear and a longer one worthwhile; assess this game through actual play.

q.zh: 开场必须在一分钟内教完吗？
q.en: Must an opening tutorial finish within one minute?

a.zh: 不用。首分钟目标帮助收束焦点，不是所有游戏的时长验收线。按操作风险、玩家背景和本作节奏组织，观察理解与下一步，而不只计时。
a.en: No. An opening goal focuses design rather than imposing a universal time gate. Structure teaching by input risk, player background, and pacing; observe understanding and continuation as well as time.

q.zh: 教程可以只靠人物对白吗？
q.en: Can dialogue alone carry the tutorial?

a.zh: 对白可以给目标与必要规则，但还需要玩家真正执行动作并看结果。如果只读“信已送到”，却从未选择接收者，就没有教到本例的核心操作。
a.en: Dialogue may give goals and rules, but players still need to act and see results. Reading “delivered” without choosing a recipient does not teach this example’s core action.

text.zh: 用 $game-world-design 设计首段教学。附本作核心动作、玩家身份、目标平台和原作约束。只教当前一步需要的规则，写可见依据、实际操作、成功反馈、可恢复误操作和下一次使用。列真实试玩要观察的问题，不把设计稿或规则演算当成理解、手感和乐趣已经验证。
text.en: Use $game-world-design to design the opening tutorial from core actions, player role, platform, and source constraints. Teach the current step’s rules with visible evidence, actual input, success feedback, a recoverable mistake, and another use. List questions for real playtesting without claiming the design proves understanding, feel, or enjoyment.

label.zh: 首分钟目标、教学动作与规则变式
label.en: Opening goal, teaching actions, and rule variation

label.zh: 引导信息与按钮文案
完整路径与实际试玩证据
label.en: Complete paths and actual playtest evidence

title.zh: 配音句间背景音乐忽大忽小怎么办：检查压低区间与恢复
title.en: How to Fix Music Swells Between Voiceover Lines

seo_title.zh: 配音句间背景音乐忽大忽小怎么办
